info.title: Atribu API
info.description:
Marketing attribution API. Get campaign ROAS, visitor analytics, customer journeys, and revenue attribution data.

## Authentication

All requests require a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header:
```
Authorization: Bearer atb_live_your_key_here
```

Get your API key from **Settings > API Keys** in the Atribu dashboard.

Two more credentials ride the same header, both identifying a PERSON rather than a tenant, and both requiring `?profile_id=<uuid>` on profile-scoped routes:

- an **MCP user token** (`atb_user_…`) — a public integration path, and the credential an AI agent holds after the MCP OAuth flow at `https://mcp.atribu.app` (or after `POST /api/v1/me/mcp-tokens`). One token covers both the MCP server and this API. See the `userToken` security scheme.
- a **Supabase session access token** — Atribu's own dashboard, 120 requests/minute per user. See the `bearerAuth` security scheme.

## Scopes

API keys have granular scopes:
- `analytics:read` — Read aggregated analytics: overview, timeseries, breakdowns, quality, touches, and channel/referrer/page/keyword/country/device/browser/OS dimensions.
- `campaigns:read` — Read campaign, ad set and ad performance: ROAS, trends, archetypes, creative patterns, DM ads and top performers.
- `conversions:read` — Read conversion counts and revenue, including cash-only revenue and conversion timeseries.
- `commerce:read` — Read the merchant's product catalogue (products, variants, stock and prices) and look an order up by number, email or phone. Returns no customer identity.
- `customers:read` — Read the customer list and per-customer journey detail — personally identifiable information.
- `visitors:read` — Read the visitor list — personally identifiable information.
- `realtime:read` — Read the live visitor count.
- `exports:read` — Read the conversion-export/signal-sync surface: Meta CAPI wiring diagnostics, dataset quality, Custom Audiences, export deliveries, and the compliance state behind Platform-Safe Mode.
- `exports:write` — Configure the conversion-export pipeline: create, edit and disable export destinations (Meta dataset/pixel, Google Ads conversion action) and the signal rules that map a conversion definition to a platform event, and send a Meta test event.
- `events:write` — Ingest server-side outcome events (e.g. a closed sale) via POST /api/v1/events.
- `goals:write` — Create, list and edit conversion goal definitions.
- `attribution:write` — Trigger an attribution recompute for a profile.
- `tracking:write` — Configure a site's tracking installation: issue and revoke tracking keys, change the tracker's session/enrichment settings (which enqueues a full attribution replay), and start an install verification.
- `reports:write` — Create, schedule, generate and send attribution reports (report schedules, deliveries and send).
- `workspaces:write` — Create a workspace (POST /api/v1/workspaces). Not granted by any OAuth connect scope; an MCP user token holds it through the `mcp:write` grant.
- `profiles:write` — Create a profile inside a workspace the caller already belongs to (POST /api/v1/profiles). Not granted by any OAuth connect scope; an MCP user token holds it through the `mcp:write` grant.
- `campaigns:apply` — Apply or dismiss a campaign recommendation. Not granted by default — a workspace admin must opt a key into it, or the app must hold the `attribution` connect scope.
- `creatives:write` — Queue an on-demand AI analysis of one ad's creative (`POST /api/v1/ads/{id}/creative-analysis`). Each accepted call queues a model call against the workspace's daily creative-analysis allowance, so it is capped per profile and per key per day and is not granted by default — a workspace admin must opt a key into it, or the app must hold the `attribution` connect scope.
- `connections:read` — Read the state of a profile's connections: the connection list and detail, and the progress of a running sync.
- `connections:write` — Run the connect rail: mint a connect hand-off URL, list the candidate accounts behind a parked provider token, finalize the selection, trigger a sync, and disconnect a connection.
- `calendar` — Create, update and delete events on Atribu booking calendars.
- `calendar.manage` — Create, list and share (ACL) Atribu booking calendars.
- `calendar.read` — Read-only access to Atribu booking calendars and their events.
- `whatsapp` — Send and manage WhatsApp messages, templates, flows, broadcasts, calling and phone-number registration.
- `whatsapp:read` — Read WhatsApp conversations, messages, templates and broadcasts. A read-only subset of `whatsapp`, which also allows sending and managing them.
- `instagram` — Send and manage Instagram DMs, comment replies, triggers and media.
- `email` — Read and send connected email (Gmail/Outlook): drafts, threads, labels and search.
- `conversations:read` — Read the unified inbox: conversation list and message threads across WhatsApp, Instagram and email, plus organic/ad match suggestions, contact-extraction review proposals and the Instagram DM↔payment reconciliation worklist.
- `conversations:write` — Reply on a conversation, save an email draft, apply Gmail labels, link/unlink a conversation to a customer, and approve/reject a contact-extraction review proposal.

See the API changelog (docs/api-changelog.md) for scope-catalogue changes — scopes are frozen into a key at mint time, so a key minted before a new scope was added to a grant does not carry it; re-mint via `client_credentials`.

## Rate Limits

Default: 60 requests/minute. Check `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header.
Heavy endpoints (customers, visitors, journey) cost 3x.

A few endpoints also carry their own sustained bucket, because one call is far more work than a read. That bucket is separate from the per-minute allowance, so it can neither consume it nor be consumed by it:

| Endpoint | Own bucket |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/v1/quality/utm/refresh` | 6 scans/hour per key (each is an 8-12s live scan) |
| `POST /api/v1/profiles` | 200 provisioning calls/hour per app credential |

## Date Range

Most endpoints require `date_from` and `date_to` in YYYY-MM-DD format. Maximum range: 366 days.

bearerAuth.description:
API key in Bearer format. Get your key from Settings > API Keys in the Atribu dashboard.

THREE credentials ride this header and the API tells them apart by SHAPE, never by a second header: an `atb_live_` API key (this scheme), an `atb_user_` MCP user token (the `userToken` scheme) and a **Supabase session access token** (three base64url segments).

`api.atribu.app` accepts the session token for Atribu's own console. It differs from a key in three ways: `profile_id` is a REQUIRED query parameter (a user belongs to many profiles — 400 `invalid_request` without it, and 404 `not_found` for one they cannot reach, identical to a profile that does not exist); scopes are derived per request from the user's workspace role and profile permissions rather than frozen at mint time; and the rate limit is 120 requests/minute per user, metered separately from any API key on the same profile.

A session token is a browser credential — it expires in an hour and is refreshed by the Supabase client that minted it. For a program or an agent acting as a person, use the `userToken` scheme instead: same person-shaped tenancy, long-lived, revocable per agent, and obtainable without a browser session of your own.

**Workspace-scoped routes (#487).** A handful of reads answer a question that spans every profile in a workspace (`/workspaces`, `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/…`). Those take the workspace in the path — or `?workspace_id=` where the path does not carry one — INSTEAD of `?profile_id=`, and admit a caller on an ACTIVE workspace membership (400 `invalid_request` without the id; 404 `not_found` for a workspace they are not a member of, identical to one that does not exist). Row scoping inside the workspace still applies: a caller sees only the profiles they can open. **An API key cannot use them** — a key is minted for exactly one profile, so it has no workspace set and no membership list, and receives 403 `insufficient_scope` naming the profile-scoped alternative.

userToken.description:
An **MCP user token** (`atb_user_…`) — the credential a person's own AI agent holds, and a fully public integration path (#1084).

HOW TO GET ONE. Either connect over MCP (`https://mcp.atribu.app`) and complete the OAuth 2.1 + PKCE flow, which is the bootstrap for an agent with no Atribu account of its own — the agent registers a client, hands the authorize URL to its human, and holds the token after consent — or, if you are already signed in, mint one with `POST /api/v1/me/mcp-tokens`.

IT IS THE SAME TOKEN ON BOTH SURFACES. One credential covers `mcp.atribu.app` and this API; there is no separate key to mint per profile.

TENANCY IS PERSON-SHAPED, exactly like a session token: `?profile_id=` is REQUIRED on profile-scoped routes (400 `invalid_request` without it; 404 `not_found` for a profile the person cannot reach, identical to one that does not exist), `?workspace_id=` or the path segment on workspace-scoped routes, and the workspace-grain routes an API key is refused on are open to it.

SCOPES ARE AN INTERSECTION, which is the one thing that has no analogue on the other two credentials. The token's `mcp:*` grant maps onto API scopes — `mcp:read` → `analytics:read`, `campaigns:read`, `conversions:read`, `realtime:read`; `mcp:read_pii` → `customers:read`; `mcp:write` → `exports:read`, `exports:write`, `goals:write`, `attribution:write`, `tracking:write`, `reports:write`, `campaigns:apply` — and the request holds the INTERSECTION of that map with what the person's own membership grants. So a 403 `insufficient_scope` can mean either half is too narrow; the message names both. Messaging, calendar, inbox, commerce, `events:write` and `creatives:write` are reachable by no MCP scope. A token minted BEFORE a mapping widens keeps the scopes frozen into its row: re-consent or re-mint to pick the new ones up.

ACCOUNT ADMINISTRATION IS OUT OF REACH, deliberately: `/api/v1/me/**` (including `/me/mcp-tokens`) answers 403 to a user token. A credential cannot mint, rotate or revoke the class it belongs to — sign in for that.

RATE LIMIT: the token's own `rate_limit_units_per_minute`, in a bucket of its own, so an agent's loop cannot 429 its owner's dashboard. A revoked or expired token answers 401 with the same envelope a revoked API key gets.

adminAuth.description: Atribu staff secret (`admin_secret_...`) for the `/api/v1/admin/*` surface. Constant-time hashed compare; rotate via `ATRIBU_ADMIN_SECRET` env var on the Next.js service.

clientSecretBasic.description: RFC 6749 §2.3.1 `client_secret_basic`. Used on `/oauth/token` and `/oauth/revoke`. The body-form variant (`client_id` + `client_secret` in body) is also accepted per RFC.

customer_name.description: Null unless the key also holds the customers:read scope.

customer_email.description: Null unless the key also holds the customers:read scope.

value_amount_reporting.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

candidate_count.description: How many candidate ads were scored for this conversion.

probability.description: 0-1, the model's credit share for this candidate. MODELLED decision support — never folded into ROAS.

evidence.description: The model's own explanation blob. Opaque by contract: its keys are data, not contract field names, and its shape may change without a version bump.

candidates.description: Every candidate ad the messaging attribution model scored for this conversion, highest probability first. EMPTY means the conversion exists and nothing was scored — a conversion that is not this profile's is a 404, never an empty chain.

high_count.description: High-severity UTM anomalies (placement-in-source, non-channel medium, unsubstituted macros, unresolved paid ad identifiers).

medium_count.description: Medium-severity anomalies (paid traffic with no UTMs at all).

refreshed_at.description: When this cached scan last ran — the daily utm-health-refresh cron, or someone's on-demand scan. Null if nothing has scanned this window yet.

attributed_cash.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

dangling_conversions.description: Cash conversions whose credited touch names an ad id that resolves to no known ad (deleted ad, no account access, or utm_content carrying an ad name instead of its id).

attributed_cash.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

refreshed.description: Whether a scan actually ran. `false` means the cached summary was still inside the 10-minute idempotency window and is returned unchanged — not that anything failed.

value.description: The observed value. `(empty)` when the field was absent.

count.description: How often this value was seen in the window.

severity.description: How much this issue distorts attribution. Currently `high`, `medium`, `low` or `info`. Treat as an open string: the scan is a database function and can gain a level without a version bump.

category.description: Which issue this is. Currently `placement_in_source`, `non_channel_medium`, `unsubstituted_macro`, `missing_ad_identifier`, `missing_utms_on_paid` or `inconsistent_source_vocab`. Treat as an open string — the scan can gain a category without a version bump, so branch with a default rather than exhaustively.

field.description: The UTM field at fault, or the pseudo-fields `any` / `all_utms` for the categories that span several.

count.description: Events exhibiting the issue — or paid TOUCHES, for `missing_ad_identifier`, which is measured on the touch layer rather than on raw events.

pct.description: `count` against that category's own denominator (all events, paid events, or paid touches), to one decimal. `0` for `inconsistent_source_vocab`, which has no meaningful denominator — not a computed zero.

samples.description: Up to 5 of the most common offending values, most frequent first. Always present; `[]` for the categories that collect none (`unsubstituted_macro`, `missing_utms_on_paid`).

recommendation.description: The fix, in prose, written by the scan itself. Safe to show to an end user.

recommendation_code.description:
The stable identifier for the remedy — ONE PER REMEDY, not one per `category`, so two categories can share a fix. Published alongside `recommendation` rather than instead of it: that sentence is composed inside the database function, so it is English on every screen and names warehouse tables. Key your own translated copy off this and fall back to the prose.

`null` on a breakdown cached before the codes existed — old rows are not rewritten. That means 'no code was stored', never 'no remedy'.

refreshed_at.description: When this BREAKDOWN was last computed. Not the same stamp as the badge's `refreshed_at` in GET /api/v1/quality/utm: that one also moves when the cheap daily cron recounts, and the cron does not recompute the breakdown. `null` means no deep scan has ever cached a breakdown for this window — which is NOT the same as a scan that found nothing, so do not render an empty list with a null stamp as 'clean'.

anomalies.description: One entry per DISTINCT ISSUE, at most six. This is not `high_count + medium_count`: those count events, this counts issues, so one entry can carry a `count` in the thousands.

destination.description: Which platform. Required on create; IMMUTABLE — a PATCH that changes it is rejected.

connection_id.description: The `data_connections` row this destination ships through. Must belong to this profile and its provider must match the kind (`meta_capi` ⇒ `meta_ads`).

meta_pixel_id.description: Meta dataset / pixel id. REQUIRED for `meta_capi`.

google_conversion_action.description: Google Ads conversion action resource name. REQUIRED for `google_ads`.

destination_config.description: Free-form destination settings (`signal_quality`, `relay_automatic_events`, …). DEEP-MERGED over the stored object on a PATCH, so keys written by the dataset wizard (`data_source`) and by Platform-Safe provisioning are never blanked by a partial update.

archived_at.description: Set to archive. An archived rule emits nothing and is excluded from the list.

source_ref_id.description: The `conversion_definitions` id a `conversion_definition` rule maps. Null on a pipeline rule.

source_config.description: `to_stage` / `from_stage` / `external_source` on a pipeline rule; `fixed_value` + `fixed_currency` on a `fixed_value` rule.

destinations.description: Per-destination toggle. A rule with no enabled destination produces no candidates.

platform_event_name_overrides.description: Overrides the event name derived from the definition's source events.

meta_custom_event_type.description: Meta's optimization category for the Custom Conversion created from this rule. Null means derive it. Meta's spellings are counter-intuitive — `INITIATED_CHECKOUT`, `CONTENT_VIEW`.

recurring_payment_mode.description: What this rule does with a SUBSCRIPTION RENEWAL — a `cash` `payment_received` conversion whose `is_first_payment` is false. `skip` (the default, and what every pre-existing rule was backfilled to) never exports it and records `skip_reason: "recurring_payment"` on the delivery. `custom_event` sends it to Meta as the custom event `SubscriptionRenewal` (Google Ads has no custom-event equivalent, so a Google destination skips with `recurring_payment_google_no_custom_event`). `purchase` is the pre-#1144 behaviour. FIRST payments are unaffected by every mode, as are refunds and every non-cash conversion.

privacy_override.description: Per-rule privacy config layered over the profile's. Null inherits.

delivery_stats_7d.description: Deliveries this rule produced in the last 7 days. An ENABLED rule sitting at zero is the most common broken state on this surface — it usually means the destination is disabled, the definition matches nothing, or the Meta event has no working Custom Conversion.

source_kind.description: Required on create; IMMUTABLE — a PATCH that changes it is rejected.

source_ref_id.description: REQUIRED for a `conversion_definition` rule: the `conversion_definitions` id it maps.

recurring_payment_mode.description: Defaults to `skip` on create: a renewal is not a `Purchase`, and Meta cannot unsend one. Set `purchase` only when the business genuinely wants renewals counted as purchases at the platform.

candidate_count.description: Source records this rule would have matched in the window. An UPPER BOUND on its effect, never a forecast of sends: a matched record still has to clear identity, the privacy guard, the platform staleness window and destination routing.

matched_on.description: The definition's source event names, or the single configured stage.

destination_id.description: Which enabled meta_capi destination to send through. Omitted ⇒ the oldest enabled one.

test_event_code.description: From Events Manager → Test Events. Without it the event is a real (if synthetic) event on the dataset rather than a test one.

rule_id.description: Borrow this rule's Meta event name and privacy override, so the test exercises the rule you are verifying.

channel.description: `business_messaging` sends a click-to-WhatsApp shaped event (sample `ctwa_clid`, `messaging_channel: whatsapp`).

event_id.description: The `event_id` the payload carried — search for it in Events Manager → Test Events.

filters_applied.description: Privacy filters that fired on the cleanse before the send.

quality_warning.description: Non-null when this profile's match-quality policy would BLOCK a real event carrying only what a test carries (IP + user agent). The test still sends — a test that could not run under a strict policy would prove nothing.

routing.description: Whether this destination will actually ship on the next run. `suppressed_platform_safe` means enabled but deliberately silenced: in Platform-Safe mode the provisioned Clean Dataset is the sole Meta feed, so every other meta_capi destination is held back to avoid double-sending and re-contaminating the old dataset.

meta_pixel_id.description: Meta dataset / pixel id. Null on a Google destination.

clean_dataset_id.description: The Clean Dataset id, when Platform-Safe provisioning stamped this destination.

external_account_id.description: The connected ad account id (Google Ads customer id on a Google destination).

connection.description: The provider connection this destination ships through. Its `status` is the usual reason a healthy-looking destination stops delivering. No credential is ever included.

last_delivery.description: The most recent ledger row for this destination. Null if it has never produced one.

privacy_mode.description: `standard` | `hipaa` | `custom` | `platform_safe`. Governs routing and the legal gate.

scoped.description: Source records the request resolved to.

enqueued.description: Ledger rows this call scheduled. NOT a count of events delivered.

already_delivered.description: Already at the platform under their canonical event id — including via a sibling ingestion path. Never re-sent.

already_queued.description: A job was already coming for these before this call. This is why repeating a trigger is a no-op.

not_ledgered.description: In scope, but the pipeline has never built an export candidate for them. A standard export run is queued to build them.

id.description: The batch id. Pass it to `GET /api/v1/exports/{id}`.

queued_job_ids.description: Queue message ids, for correlating with worker logs. Not durable identifiers.

progress.description: LIVE per-status counts of the ledger rows this batch queued, re-read at request time. Keys are the conversion_exports status ladder (pending | processing | sent | failed | skipped | dead_letter). Absent statuses are absent, not zero.

progress_missing.description: Rows this batch queued that no longer exist (a destination was deleted and cascaded).

destination.description: Restrict to one destination kind. Omitted ⇒ every enabled destination.

date_from.description: Inclusive lower bound on the SOURCE conversion's event time.

date_to.description: Inclusive upper bound on the SOURCE conversion's event time.

conversion_ids.description: `conversions.id` values. Mutually exclusive with the date range.

limit_per_destination.description: Ceiling handed to the export run, per destination. Default 100.

require_approval.description: Ask a human before anything is queued. Nothing is written: the response is still `202`, but `data` is `{status: "awaiting_approval", handoff}` instead of a batch. Hand `handoff.url` to the person who owns the account and poll `GET /api/v1/handoffs/{id}`; approving runs this exact request through the same path and the hand-off's `result.export` carries the batch id. Rejecting settles it `cancelled` and queues nothing. The legal gate is still checked first, so an approval is never handed out for a send this profile is not allowed to make.

canonical_event_id.description: The platform `event_id` this delivery carries — the booking cluster's canonical id. Two ingestion paths for one real conversion share it, which is both how Pixel↔CAPI deduplication works and how 'already delivered' is decided.

error_class.description: A CLASS, never the provider's raw message: those routinely quote the rejected request back, personal data included.

value.description: Their gross value in `currency`.

currency.description: Reporting currency of every `value` below. Null when the window has no cash.

CashCoverage.description: Where a profile's cash sits on the traceability spectrum, for the requested window and model. The five buckets are mutually exclusive and sum to `total` by both count and value. Settlement reversals (refunds, chargebacks) are excluded from the classification entirely — a reversal is not a unit of coverage in either direction.

allOf.description: Credited touch resolves to a navigable ad. THE traceable bucket.
Recovered through the lead→cash bridge — ad-attributed but a lower-confidence tier, deliberately excluded from `traceable_pct_*` and from ROAS.

Credited to an ad id that resolves to no known ad (deleted ad, no account access, or utm_content carrying an ad name instead of its id). The credit is real; it just cannot be placed in the ad hierarchy.
Has credited touches, none carrying ad signal.
No credited touch of any kind.

tracking_healthy.description: Is the website tracker firing AND identity stitching? This is the disambiguation behind a low `cash_coverage.traceable_pct_by_value`.

missing.description: Machine-readable names of the dead or incomplete signals above.

Instrumentation.description: Whether the measurement itself can be trusted. Read it BEFORE acting on `cash_coverage`: a low traceable percentage means 'you have great organic' when `tracking_healthy` is true and 'your tracking is broken' when it is false, and the two call for opposite responses.

fresh.description: A web touch inside the last 7 days.

pending_cash_conversions.description: Cash conversions stuck without an FX-normalized reporting value — they read as 0 revenue everywhere else.

window_days.description: The full window that was split in half.

recent_roas.description: Ad-attributed ROAS over the recent half. Null when that half carried no ad spend — a ratio with a zero denominator is not 0.

prior_roas.description: Ad-attributed ROAS over the prior half. Null on the same condition.

recent_spend.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

recent_traceable_revenue.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

days_with_cash.description: Distinct days across the FULL window carrying any ad-attributed cash — the density behind the two ratios. A trend over two cash days is not a trend, and this is how you can tell.

TraceableRoasTrend.description: Half-over-half ad-attributed ROAS. 'Traceable' is the `ad_attributed` bucket and nothing else, so this ratio is never inflated by revenue no ad can be shown to have driven. Directional only — it is not a causal or incrementality claim.

total_conversions.description: Non-reversal conversions in the window. The denominator of `coverage_percent`. (The underlying RPC calls this column `total_events`; it has never counted raw events, so it is published under the name it means.)

with_full_utms.description: Conversions whose first or latest touch carries a campaign / ad-set / ad id or a `utm_campaign`.

with_fbclid_only.description: No UTM or ad identifier, but an `fbclid` — placeable only through click-id recovery.

with_no_tracking.description: Neither. These conversions cannot be attributed to an ad at all.

coverage_percent.description: `(with_full_utms + with_fbclid_only) / total_conversions` as a percentage, to one decimal. 0 for an empty window.

recomputed_at.description: When the attribution projection last ran for this profile (the later of the touch and conversion projection watermarks). NULL means it has never run — returned as null rather than as a fabricated timestamp.

status.description: `ready` once a conversions projection has run for this profile, `pending` before that. Treat any other value as opaque.

conversion_key.description: The identity a `goal` filter matches on — it equals `conversions.conversion_type`.

source_event_names.description: The `outcome_events.event_type` values that produce this conversion.

revenue_type.description: `cash` | `pipeline` | `gross`. Decides whether the value nets into revenue.

attribution_eligible.description: False ⇒ the conversion is counted but never given attribution credit.

counts.description: `outcome_events.event_type` → how many landed in the window, summed across CRM pipelines. An event type with none in the window is ABSENT rather than present with 0.

value.description: The exact string the filter predicates compare against. Send it back verbatim as `filter[<dimension>]=is:<value>`.

label.description: Display label. Equal to `value` for every dimension but `goal`, which resolves the profile's own `display_name`.

count.description: Touches (or, for `goal`, conversions) carrying the value in the window. A RANKING signal for the picker — most-used first — not a reportable metric; the numbers come from `/api/v1/breakdown` once the filter is applied.

available.description: False is a normal answer, not an error — see `unavailable_reason`. Every metric below is null when false.

unavailable_reason.description: `stale_window`: the requested range ends more than two days behind today, and the source is a ROLLING aggregate whose numbers describe "the last N days from today" — returning them under an older label would be a wrong number wearing a right one. `no_messaging_data`: this profile has no messaging-objective cohort with any intent-scored conversation in the window.

score_window.description: Which rolling bucket answered — `7d` | `14d` | `28d` | `lifetime`, chosen from the length of the requested range.

spend.description: Messaging-cohort spend, in the profile's reporting currency.

cost_per_high_intent.description: `spend / high_intent_conversations`. NULL when none were high-intent — never 0, which would read as free.

field.description: The event attribute this condition tests.

op.description: Not every op is valid for every field — `click_id_key` is presence-only (`is` / `is_not`) and `exists` applies to `custom_payload_field`. An impossible pair simply never matches; it is not an error.

value.description: A string for the scalar ops, a string ARRAY for `in`, and `{ field_name, expected_value? }` for `custom_payload_field`. Untyped here because the SQL evaluator has no discriminant to narrow on.

all_of.description: EVERY condition must match. There is no `any_of`.

priority.description: Lower wins. The first rule that matches decides the channel.

all_of.description: EVERY condition must match. There is no `any_of`.

conditions.description: The STRUCTURED matcher. NULL on rules written before it existed — those match through the flat `*_pattern` columns above, which is why both are published.

is_system.description: True for Atribu's built-ins, false for channels this workspace added.

taxonomy.description: System channels plus this workspace's own, ordered by `sort_order`. `output_channel` on every rule is one of these names.

suggested_channel.description: A heuristic guess from the sample's source / medium / referrer. A default for a form field, not a classification.

all_of.description: EVERY condition must match. There is no `any_of`.

suggested_conditions.description: Ready to POST to `/api/v1/channel-rules/match-count` unchanged, and ready to save as a rule's `conditions`. NULL when every candidate field was empty.

sessions.description: Unclassified sessions in this cluster over the window. The size of the problem, and the only reportable number here.

sample_source.description: `(empty)` where the sessions carried no value — a real cluster, not a gap.

window_days.description: The window actually scanned, AFTER the Ephemeral Buffer clamp.

total.description: EVERY session in the window, not only unclassified ones — so `matches / total` is the share of ALL traffic the rule touches, which is what makes an over-broad rule visible before it is saved.

from.description: The channel today. `Direct` where the session has none.

changed.description: Sessions whose channel this rule set would CHANGE.

unmatched.description: Sessions no rule in the set matches. They keep the channel they have.

source_row_id.description: The row this event came from — a touch id or an outcome-event id. Stable, and the second half of the keyset the cursor encodes, so it is safe to key a rendered list by.

event_type.description: `session_start` | `ad_interaction` | `organic_interaction` | `outcome` — the complete set. ADR 0004 retired the `events_enriched` union, so `page_view` / `custom_event` / `engagement` can no longer arrive.

event_name.description: The touch type for a touch (`synthetic`, `organic_interaction`, …) or the outcome's own `event_type` (`lead_created`, `payment_received`, …).

session_id.description: The web session a touch belonged to. Null for synthetic and outcome rows.

source.description: Raw `utm_source` (or the outcome's first-touch UTM), not the derived platform.

derived_source.description: Derived platform label — instagram / facebook / google / meta / direct.

derived_placement.description: Normalized Meta placement token, e.g. `instagram_reels`. Always null today — the durable touch layer carries no placement dimension.

value_amount.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

is_synthetic.description: True for an off-site (ad-platform-derived) touch — one Atribu inferred rather than observed on the website.

event_payload.description: The row's own metadata, OPAQUE by design: its shape is per `event_type` (an `organic_interaction` carries `subtype` / `media_kind` / `text_excerpt`; an outcome carries `external_source` / `external_id`). Read defensively.

creative_thumbnail_url.description: Always null today — the read layer does not resolve creative previews on this grain. Published as null rather than omitted so "unresolved" is never read as "no creative".

ad_platform_id.description: The platform's ad id — join against `GET /api/v1/campaigns?level=ad`.

conversion_id.description: Outcome rows only: the conversion this outcome became, or null if it never became one (no `conversion_definitions` row lists its `event_name`).

is_credited.description: Whether this TOUCH received credit under `model`. NULL on an outcome row — "not applicable", never `false`: credit belongs to a touch, and `false` on an outcome would read as "this conversion was not credited".

credit_share.description: Mean credit weight (0..1) across the conversions this touch was credited in.

credited_revenue.description: Attributed money for this touch, in the profile's reporting currency. ADDITIVE across a visitor's touches — the sum is what the model gave this person's journey.

credit_model.description: The attribution model the four fields above were computed under.

is_primary.description: The value the customer profile is keyed by. Primary rows come first.

first_name.description: The customer's given name (`customer_profiles.first_name`). Null for an anonymous visitor and for a customer the CRM never named. Published because a customer opened by deep link is not in the `GET /api/v1/customers` list that carries the name per row, and a header with nowhere to get it fell through to the raw email — or to a literal "Unknown" — while the column was populated.

last_name.description: The customer's family name (`customer_profiles.last_name`). Same rules as `first_name`.

touch_count.description: Marketing touches over the visitor's WHOLE history. This replaces the retired pageview count (ADR 0006) rather than approximating it — a pageview number is not published at all, because a fabricated 0 would read as "never browsed".

total_cash_revenue.description: Sum of the visitor's CASH conversions, in the profile's reporting currency. Cash only: pipeline and gross revenue types are counted elsewhere, and adding them here would double-count a deal that is both.

time_to_completion_seconds.description: Seconds from the visitor's first touch to their first conversion of `goal`. NULL when either end is missing — 0 is a real answer here (converted at the same instant as the first touch) and has to stay distinguishable from "no such journey".

lead_quality_score.description: The score stored on this customer's `lead_created` event, or null when they have none or it was never scored. Read, never recomputed. Always null for an anonymous visitor.

identifiers.description: Email and phone only, primary first. The identity graph also holds anonymous ids and provider keys; those are plumbing, not identity, and are deliberately not published here. Empty for an anonymous visitor.

spend.description: A decimal string like every other amount here, but NOT exact: this leaf lives inside a jsonb document, which PostgREST cannot cast per-read, so the double was already formed at the database edge. See the header of @atribu/api-contract/dto-messaging.

excerpt.description: The customer's first inbound message, redacted server-side (email, phone, RUT/CURP/DNI/cédula) and truncated to 140 characters.

external_action_url.description: Set on a manual-only `creative_refresh_pre_fatigue` rec — the Ads Lab session prepared for it. When present the rec is a hand-off, not something to apply.

sample_n.description: Cohort ads the percentile was ranked against. A percentile without its sample is a rank presented as a fact; `sample_confidence` is the band derived from this number.

sample_conversations.description: Redacted excerpts of the conversations this ad started. NULL — never [] — unless the key also holds `customers:read`; an empty array would be indistinguishable from 'this ad started no conversations'.

baseline_win_rate.description: The win rate across the same filtered population — this profile's messaging ads, not the workspace's.

lift_vs_baseline.description: An ASSOCIATION, not a causal claim. Read it with the confidence interval; a point estimate alone overstates what the sample supports.

meta_connected.description: Whether this profile has a connected `meta_ads` connection — the difference between 'nothing to show yet' and 'connected, and the messaging cohort is genuinely empty'.

profile_id.description: Null for a workspace- or user-scoped request — no profile in that context.

principal_kind.description: Which credential made the request. Only key/session appear today — app-credential routes never declare a PII scope.

principal_id.description: The key id, the signed-in user's id, or (reserved) an app's client_id, depending on principal_kind. Never the raw key, token, or secret.

scopes.description: The scopes THIS ROUTE declared as required, not the principal's full set.

errors_4xx.description: Requests answered 400–499 — the caller's own errors, including 429s.

errors_5xx.description: Requests answered 500 or above. The SLO's error budget is spent here.

last_request_at.description: The most recent request inside the window, or null if there was none.

text.description: The greeting the customer was already shown, under the business's name, before they sent anything. Nullable: an ice-breakers screen with no greeting line is a real configuration.
text.example: Hola 👋, soy la Dra. Valentina Moreira. ¿En qué te puedo ayudar?

autofill_message.description: The text Meta pre-fills into the customer's input box. When the first inbound message equals this, the customer tapped — they did not type it.

ice_breakers.description: Ice-breaker button labels, in Meta's order. Always present, may be empty. The customer's first message is usually one of these verbatim.

landing_screen_type.description: Meta's own name for the screen.

type.description: The AD SET's `destination_type`, verbatim: `WHATSAPP`, `MESSAGING_MESSENGER_WHATSAPP`, `MESSAGING_INSTAGRAM_DIRECT_MESSENGER_WHATSAPP`, … Meta adds combined values without notice, so treat it as an opaque string containing `WHATSAPP` rather than an enum. Null on an ad whose ad set predates the field — such an ad is listed on the strength of its call-to-action instead.

whatsapp_phone_number.description: The WhatsApp number the ad opens — the BUSINESS's own, never a customer's. Null when the ad set names no number.

page_id.description: The Facebook Page the ad runs under.

ad_id.description: The Meta ad id. This is the value that arrives as `referral.source_id` on the customer's first inbound message, and the one `GET /api/v1/partner/whatsapp/ads/{ad_id}/welcome-message` takes. Meta ids exceed 2^53 and are always strings.

optimization_goal.description: The ad set's optimization goal, verbatim.

call_to_action_type.description: The creative's call-to-action type, verbatim — `WHATSAPP_MESSAGE` on a click-to-WhatsApp ad. Read from the creative's own field, from `object_story_spec`, or from `asset_feed_spec`, whichever the editor that built the ad populated.

creative_id.description: The creative carrying the configuration. Null when Meta withheld the creative edge — it does that for ads on Pages the token does not admin.

allOf.description: The welcome message the customer was shown before writing. Null whenever `greeting_status` is not `present` — read that field to learn which kind of nothing this is.

greeting_status.description: `present` — the ad has a greeting, and it is in `greeting`. `none` — the creative was read and configures none; a completely normal ad, and a final answer. `unreadable` — Meta would not show us the creative (deleted ad, a Page this token does not admin, a connection needing reconnection); worth asking again once that is fixed. Collapsing the last two into `greeting === null` would make a normal ad indistinguishable from a dead connection.

last_synced_at.description: When Atribu's nightly Meta sync last refreshed this ad's configuration. This surface never calls Meta live, so this is how stale the row may be — and an ad launched since the last sync is absent from the list entirely, while its greeting is already readable by id on the welcome-message route.

allOf.description: Null when this ad has no welcome message configured. That is a complete answer, not a failure, and it is still a 200.

fetched_at.description: When the answer was read FROM META — not when this request ran. On a cached hit this is older than now.

cached.description: Whether this answer came from Atribu's cache rather than a live Meta read.

docs_url.description: Deep link to the docs section explaining this exact code (#1065). Every Atribu response builder sets it; marked optional here (not required) for forward compatibility with any envelope a future surface emits before adopting it.

required_scopes.description: Present on `insufficient_scope` when the missing scope(s) are known by name. Mint a new key with one of these, or have a workspace admin grant a role that includes it.

reconnect_required.description: Present + true when the connection's token was revoked and the user must re-authorize.

reconnect_url.description: Where to send the user to reconnect (present with `reconnect_required` when the channel can build one).

upgrade_required.description: #1067 — present + true on a resource-limit denial (e.g. `profile_limit_reached`) the caller can fix by upgrading the plan or freeing up the resource.

plan.description: The plan the denial was evaluated against — not a suggested target.
