public_key.description: The tracking key embedded in the dealer's site — a PUBLIC identifier, not a secret. It ships inside the GTM tag / snippet / Shopify pixel to every anonymous visitor of the dealer's site, so returning it here is no more sensitive than returning the tag itself.

last_seen_at.description: When the tracker last used this key to send an event. Null if never seen.

created.description: True when this call minted the key (HTTP 201). False when an existing active key was returned unchanged (HTTP 200) — see the route description for the idempotency contract.

name.description: A label for the key, used only when this call actually mints one. Ignored on an idempotent replay — the existing active key keeps its original name.

force_new.description: Mint a key EVEN IF one is already active, and always answer 201. Default false — the idempotent behaviour described above. A profile may legitimately hold several active keys (which is why revoking the last one is refused); use this when rotating, and revoke the old key only after the new one is deployed.

gtmTagSnippet.description: Paste this verbatim into a GTM Custom HTML tag. Defer-loads the Atribu tracker.

snippet.description: The plain Atribu tracker snippet — paste before `</head>`.

combinedSnippet.description: Present only when `include_meta_pixel=true` AND a Meta CAPI pixel is configured.

extensionCode.description: A Shopify Web Pixel extension `index.js` body. Replace the extension's source with this.

external_ref.description: YOUR id for this dealer. Together with your client_id it is the idempotency key: calling this endpoint again with the same external_ref returns the same profile (HTTP 200) instead of creating a second one. Required — there is no fallback, because a generated one would make every retry a new dealer.

name.description: The dealer's display name. Becomes both the workspace and the profile name.

email.description: The dealer's owner email. A passwordless Atribu user is created for it and made owner of the dealer's workspace, so the dealer can claim the account later by magic link. This is IDENTITY, not the idempotency key — reusing one email across dealers is fine and still produces separate dealers.

timezone.description: IANA time zone. Defaults to UTC.

currency.description: ISO-4217 reporting currency. Defaults to USD.

site_domain.description:
The dealer's own website. Send it however you hold it — a bare host, a full URL, mixed case — and it is stored as one normal form: a lowercase hostname with no scheme, port or path (at most 253 characters), which is what `GET /api/v1/profile` returns as `site_domain`. `www.` is preserved, because `www.example.cl` and `example.cl` are different hosts. Rejected with a 400: IP addresses, single-label hosts, and URLs carrying credentials.

This records the dealer's SITE. It does not register a custom tracking host (no DNS is expected of you), and nothing about event collection is gated on it.

locale.description: The language the dealer's OWNER is written to in — alert digests and account email. Defaults to `en`. Applied only on the call that creates the dealer's owner: a language is a property of the person, and a later dealer sharing that email must not silently change it (nor overwrite what they chose themselves).

scopes.description: The delegation this app receives over the new profile. Defaults to ["connections"] (#1455 — connectivity is what a freshly provisioned profile is for; the `attribution` bundle is set by Atribu when you declare the `atribu_attribution` entitlement, not requested here). Must be a subset of your app's allowed_scopes, and every entry must be a profile-level scope (analytics, analytics_pii, attribution_write, connections, attribution) — a connection scope such as `whatsapp` is rejected, because a profile-level grant naming one would authorize nothing while appearing to.

grant_id.description: The oauth_app_authorizations row recording this delegation.

created.description: True when this call created the dealer (HTTP 201). False when an existing (app, external_ref) profile was returned unchanged (HTTP 200).

scopes.description: The scopes the grant now carries.

workspace_id.description: The EXISTING workspace to add this profile to. The caller must hold an ACTIVE owner or admin membership on it — an analyst, guest, or non-member answers 404, identical to a workspace that does not exist.

site_domain.description: Normalized server-side to a bare lowercase hostname.

created.description: Always true — this branch has no idempotency key and always creates.

archived.description: Always true on a 200 — see workspace_archived.

workspace_archived.description: Always true today: archiving a profile this app provisioned archives its dealer workspace with it (the one-workspace-per-dealer shape provisioning creates) — there is no mode that archives only the profile. Stated on the wire rather than left implicit, so a caller does not have to know that shape to know what happened to the workspace.

external_ref.description: YOUR id for this dealer — the SAME natural key `POST /api/v1/profiles` provisions on. Stamps `provisioned_external_ref` on the named profile so every later `POST /api/v1/profiles` replay (and the consent flow's own lookup) lands on it instead of minting a duplicate.

scopes.description: The delegation this app receives over the profile. Defaults to ["connections"]. Must be a subset of your app's allowed_scopes, and every entry must be a profile-level scope (analytics, analytics_pii, attribution_write, connections, attribution). Upserted on every call, replay included — a re-adopt that widens or narrows this list is a re-consent.

grant_id.description: The oauth_app_authorizations row recording this delegation.

created.description: True on the call that stamped `external_ref` (HTTP 201). False on every replay — the same ref already stamped, or a call that only changed `scopes` (HTTP 200).

scopes.description: The scopes the grant now carries.

is_default.description: Exactly one template per workspace can be the default.

sections.description: The section ids this template declares, in order. The full template document (per-section config, commentary HTML) is not published — it is the editor's format, not a contract. An empty list means the template declares no nameable sections; it never means the document could not be read.

schema.description: The template document — an ordered list of sections, each with its own per-type config. Not a stable public contract; consumers other than the Atribu console must not depend on its shape.

template_id.description: An existing, workspace-owned template. Mutually exclusive with `template_schema`.

template_schema.description: An unsaved draft document. Mutually exclusive with `template_id`.

recipients.description: Defaults to the profile's own report-schedule recipients. A SESSION caller's explicit list is checked against workspace membership, the same rule `POST /reports/schedules` applies; a KEY caller's is not.

window_days.description: The trailing window the test report covers. Defaults to 7.

message_id.description: The email provider's message id. `null` means it returned none — the send happened, but no delivery event can ever be matched to it.

reason.description: A soft/transient bounce never suppresses — only these two reasons do.

day_of_week.description: 0–6, Sunday-based. Null for cadences that pick no weekday.

language.description: The language the report emails render in — the client's, not yours.

recipient_count.description: How many addresses this schedule mails. Always returned.

recipient_emails.description: The configured recipients. Returned ONLY to a key holding `reports:write` — a recipient list is configuration, not an analytic fact, so whoever may set it may read it. A key without that scope receives `null`, never `[]`: an empty array is a real and different state (a schedule configured to mail nobody). Use `recipient_count` to tell the two apart.

suppressed_recipients.description: Which of `recipient_emails` the email provider has told us are undeliverable. Same gate as `recipient_emails`, for the same reason — `null` for a key without `reports:write`, an array (possibly empty) for one with it. Scoped to this schedule's own addresses only, never the workspace's whole suppression list.

next_scheduled_at.description: Null whenever the schedule is disabled.

recipient_emails.description: Up to 10 addresses. Enabling a schedule with none is rejected — it would mail nobody on every tick, forever, without telling anyone.

source.description: `manual` — a signed-in person clicked send. `scheduled` — the recurring cron. `api` — a delegated send with an API key. The CREDENTIAL decides, not the caller: a session bearer records `manual` with the person on it, a key records `api` (the actor is the key, which the request log carries).

status.description: `null` means UNKNOWN, not delivered: the provider returned no message id, so no delivery event can ever be matched to this send and its outcome will never be known. Never render a null as a success.

type.description: `api` for a delegated generation, `custom` for one a signed-in person asked for, or the schedule's cadence word. Decided by the credential, never sent.

share_slug.description: Slug of the hosted share page (`/reports/{share_slug}`), for linking a human to the rendered view. This API never serves that page.

data.description: The report payload: KPIs, chart series, breakdowns, top campaigns, top performers. This is DATA, not presentation — the same document Atribu's own renderers consume, published so you can render your own report in your own product. No HTML and no PDF is returned by any endpoint on this surface.

template_snapshot.description: The template document this report was rendered under, frozen at generation time. `null` only for rows generated before this field existed.

message_id.description: The email provider's message id. `null` means it returned none — the send happened, but no delivery event can ever be matched to it, so the ledger row's `status` stays `null` forever.

type.description: `custom` (a signed-in person generated it), `api` (a delegated consumer did), or the schedule's cadence word.

currency.description: Frozen at generation — the report's own currency, not the profile's today.

spend.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

revenue.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

kpis_failed.description: True when the read behind spend/revenue/roas/outcomes failed, so those four numbers are the coalesced defensive default (typically all zero) rather than a measurement. Absent-as-false on every report generated before this field existed — a stored report with no `kpisFailed` on its document renders exactly as it always has.

summary.description: The headline numbers, or `null` when the stored document carries none — a report predating a KPI, or one stored malformed. `null` is NOT zeros: rendering `0` for it would be inventing a measurement nobody took.

enabled.description: The state the schedule was left in by this change.

recipient_count.description: How many addresses the schedule mailed after this change. The addresses themselves are not published here: they are configuration, and configuration rides `reports:write` (see `ReportSchedule.recipient_emails`).

logo_url.description: The agency's logo, or null to render the Atribu wordmark.

hide_atribu_footer.description: Agency tier only. The entitlement is enforced when branding is resolved, never by the caller.

branded.description: True when any white-label branding resolved. False means the report renders as Atribu's own.

type.description: How this report came to exist — the schedule's cadence word, `custom`, or `api`.

document.description: The stored report, republished VERBATIM — the same document that was frozen at generation. `null` when the row carries none, which is a real state the renderer shows an empty message for; it is never `{}`, because a report of zeros would read as a measurement nobody took.

template_snapshot.description: The template as it stood at generation — which sections, in which order. `null` for a report stored before snapshots existed.

has_schedule.description: False when the profile has no report_schedules row at all.

next_scheduled_at.description: Null whenever the schedule is disabled — a stale timestamp never reads as upcoming.

id.description: `subscriptions.plan_tier` — the key `PLANS` is indexed by. The plan's display name is an i18n key, so it is not returned: resolving it is the client's job.

status.description: `trialing` | `active` | `past_due` | `canceled` | `expired` | `paused`.

current_step.description: The wizard step index (0-based) this draft last saved.

attribution_model.description: The draft attribution-model pick — not yet `default_attribution_model` until onboarding finishes.

updated_at.description: Stamped by the server on every `PATCH .../profile` write that includes `onboarding_state` — never the client's own clock.

currency.description: ISO 4217. Every money field this API returns for this profile is denominated in it.

timezone.description: IANA zone. Day boundaries in every date range are computed in it.

mode.description: How the profile makes money. Null when it was never set.

site_domain.description: The dealer's own website, as a bare lowercase hostname — no scheme, port or path. Null when none was recorded. Set through `site_domain` on `POST /api/v1/profiles`. This is the dealer's SITE; it is not a custom tracking host, and nothing about event collection is gated on it.

default_attribution_model.description: The attribution model a read uses when the caller names none.

allOf.description: #1056 — the reduced onboarding summary. Also on `WorkspaceProfile`.

#1056 — the full onboarding draft this profile last saved: current step, business type, the draft attribution-model pick, the GHL stage-mapping edits and the tracking sub-step. Null before its first `PATCH .../profile` write with `onboarding_state`. NEVER returned by `GET /api/v1/profiles` — see `WorkspaceProfile.onboarding` for the list route's reduced summary instead.

permissions.description: What the CALLER may do with this profile, in Atribu's own permission vocabulary. For a session bearer these are the user's effective permissions on the profile; for an API key they are projected from the key's scopes. Advisory — it says what a UI should offer. The enforced gate is the key's scopes, which this API checks at the route and again at the read.

allOf.description: The WORKSPACE's plan. Null when the workspace has no subscription row — reported rather than defaulted, because inventing a tier would make a feature gate assert something nobody configured. No prices, balances or invoice state are returned.

is_demo.description: #1069 — this profile was seeded by `POST /api/v1/profiles/demo`. The attribution engine runs on its rows for real, so every profile-scoped read here returns real numbers computed by the real pipeline. What the flag changes is everything OUTSIDE the profile: it is excluded from workspace-grain aggregates (pacing, Top Performers cohorts, the agency Reports hub, alert digests, the ML passes), it does not consume an `active_profiles` plan seat, and its conversion exports are RECORDED — the `conversion_exports` row carries the exact payload Meta would have received, with `status: "skipped"` and `skip_reason: "demo_profile_recorded"` — never sent.

has_subscription_revenue.description:
#1354 — TRUE when this profile has EVER processed a payment its source provider tagged as subscription-derived: a Shopify order whose sourceName is `subscription_contract`, a Stripe charge linked to an auto-charging subscription invoice, or a MercadoPago payment whose `operation_type` is `recurring_payment`. A coarse, all-time capability flag — not a per-window recount of which repeat customers are currently subscribed — for deciding whether a caption should say 'active subscriptions' or stay generic ('repeat customers').

When `analytics` is `unavailable` this is its fail-closed default (`false`), not a measurement.

analytics.description:
#1550 — whether Atribu's analytics store could be read while assembling this document.

`unavailable` means the request succeeded and every field above is trustworthy EXCEPT `has_subscription_revenue`, which is the only one read from analytics. The profile's own settings and its plan come from Atribu's messaging core, which is why this call keeps answering through such an outage instead of failing over a caption.

allOf.description: #1056 — the same reduced summary `ProfileContext` carries. NEVER the full draft: see `ProfileContext.onboarding_state`.

has_creative_scores.description: #487 — whether this profile has any creative scores at all. It separates 'no winners in this window' from 'never scored': two states a client would otherwise draw identically, and only one of which is a reason to go look at the ads.

is_demo.description: #1069 — a seeded demo profile. Present on the LIST as well as on `ProfileContext` so a switcher can badge it without a second call; a client must never infer it from the name, which a person may change.

workspace_role.description: The CALLER's role in this workspace. Advisory — it says what a UI should offer; the enforced gate is the scope check this API performs at the route and again at the read.

profile_count.description: Unarchived profiles in the workspace — the workspace's TOTAL, not the caller's accessible subset. The two are equal for owner/admin/analyst.

default_timezone.description: `workspaces.default_timezone` — the IANA zone this workspace's days are cut on, NOT the caller's browser zone. Every date boundary on the surfaces behind this workspace uses it.

acquisition_source.description: `workspaces.acquisition_source` — how this workspace was created (`web`, `shopify_app_store`, `oauth`, …). The onboarding plan-selector gates on this being exactly `shopify_app_store` before it will render.

member_count.description: ACTIVE members of the workspace — the same TOTAL sense `profile_count` carries. A count, never the roster: who is in an agency is not published by the existence of the agency.

at_risk_spend_dollars.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

lift_backed_count.description: Ads whose score is backed by an EXPERIMENT (`truth_grade='lift'`) rather than by a model or an attributed outcome. Normally small; that is the true state, not a bug.

open_recs_value_dollars.description: The summed `expected_impact_dollars` of the open recommendations. A FORECAST, never realised cash.

reporting_currency.description: ISO-4217 code the two amounts are denominated in — the WORKSPACE's `reporting_currency`, not any one profile's. Both sums add rows from profiles that may each report in a different currency, so every row is converted into this code before it is summed. There is no way to derive it from the response.

fx_missing_rows.description: Rows dropped from the two sums because no exchange rate existed for their (currency, date) pair. Amounts are never converted at an assumed rate of 1, so an unconvertible row is excluded instead. A non-zero value means the totals are incomplete and should be presented as such.

assessed_count.description: Ads in this window whose wear-out question was ANSWERED — a fatigue tier exists, or the ad platform itself reports the ad paused/degraded. `at_risk_count` excludes ads with no tier by design, so it reads low both when nothing is wearing out and when nothing was assessed. When `assessed_count` is 0, present the at-risk figure as NOT ASSESSED rather than as a zero: the zero is a fact about the model, not about the ads. `null` means this particular read does not carry the counter (the workspace-summary `brief` object does not) — it never means zero.

unassessed_count.description: The exact complement of `assessed_count` over the same window: no fatigue tier and no observed paused/degraded state. Together the two partition the window.

ads_with_any_sale.description: Ads with at least one CASH conversion (`revenue_type='cash'`) attributed to them in this window. Not a count of every conversion type.

ads_meeting_evidence_floor.description: Ads with at least THREE cash conversions — the minimum evidence Atribu requires before it will recommend an action on an ad. Zero here explains an empty recommendations list.

brief.description:
The `28d` attention counters for this workspace — the same six `/workspaces/{workspaceId}/top-performers/brief` returns, from the multi-workspace twin of that RPC.

A workspace with nothing scored gets the ZERO row, which is a real answer ("nothing needs attention"). `null` means the aggregate could NOT be computed — do not draw it as calm. It is nullable rather than fatal on purpose: this is the cold-boot read, and a workspace switcher that fails because the creative-scoring pipeline is unavailable is a worse outcome than a switcher with no indicators.

limits.description: The same `active_profiles` numbers `POST /api/v1/profiles` compares before answering `403 profile_limit_reached`.

upgrade_available.description:
The plans ABOVE this one, cheapest first, each naming the route that mints a Stripe Checkout hand-off for it (#1052).

An EMPTY array is a real answer with three possible meanings: already on the top sellable plan, on a tier this catalogue does not rank (`enterprise` — its price is negotiated), or nothing above it. None is an error; none should render an upgrade prompt.

used.description: Non-archived profiles in the workspace right now.

max.description: `null` when an admin or beta_tester override makes the cap moot — the workspace can never actually be denied on `active_profiles`.

plan.description: The plan id — a key of the published `PLANS` table.

currency.description: ISO 4217, and the unit for both amounts below.

price.description: The monthly LIST price. Not this workspace's effective price.

annual_monthly_price.description: The per-MONTH list price when billed annually — the discounted rate, NOT the yearly total.

path.description: A PATH, not a URL, so the same body is correct whichever host served it.

profile_ids.description: Profiles in the workspace currently running this pattern.

gap_profile_ids.description: Profiles that are NOT running it — the actionable half, and the reason this read is workspace-grain. 'This works for your other clients and this one is not doing it' is not a question a single profile can answer.

roas_ci_low.description: Lower bound of the interval `avg_smoothed_roas` sits in. Render the lift WITH the interval; a point estimate presented alone is a fact the sample does not support.

confidence_note.description: How the lift may be read. `associational` means exactly that: this pattern CO-OCCURS with better outcomes in this workspace. It is not a causal claim and not an experiment result.

lift_vs_baseline.description: The cluster's average over the workspace baseline. An association.

has_creative_scores.description: Whether this profile has any creative scores at all. It separates 'no winners in this window' from 'never scored' — two states a client would otherwise draw identically, and only one of which is a reason to go look at the ads.

email.description: The workspace owner's email. A passwordless Atribu user is created for it (or reused, if your app already provisioned one) and made owner of the new workspace. This is IDENTITY, not an idempotency key — reusing one email across calls is fine and legitimately produces a separate workspace each time, not a collision.

timezone.description: IANA time zone. Defaults to UTC.

locale.description: The language the workspace's OWNER is written to in — alert digests and account email. Defaults to `en`. Applied only on the call that creates that owner's shadow user: a language is a property of the person, and a later call sharing that email must not silently change it.

plan.description: Defaults to `starter` (Free). `growth` / `agency` immediately create a `trialing` subscription at that plan's real limits, rather than waiting for the workspace's first profile to bootstrap the Free tier, AND mint a real Stripe Checkout hand-off in `checkout` below — the human pays there while the trial already runs at the plan's real limits. `enterprise` is sales-led, not self-serve, and is not accepted here.

url.description: The Stripe Checkout hand-off URL — give this to a human to pay.

created.description: `false` on an idempotent replay of the session branch (same caller, same `name`, within a short window) — the status code carries the same signal (200 vs 201). Always `true` on the app-credential branch, which has no idempotency key.

allOf.description: A real Stripe Checkout hand-off for a session-branch `plan: "growth" | "agency"` request — poll `GET /api/v1/handoffs/{id}` (or send the human straight to `url`) the same way `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/checkout-session` works. `null` for `starter`/absent, always `null` on the app-credential branch, and `null` when a mint was attempted but could not complete (see `warnings`) — workspace creation is never blocked on billing either way.

warnings.description: Present only when something degraded without blocking creation — today, a single `checkout_unavailable` entry when `plan` asked for a checkout mint that did not happen. Omitted, not an empty array, when nothing degraded.

mcp_writeback_enabled.description: `true` only when the session branch's caller is an MCP user token whose grant carries `mcp:write` — that person already consented to writes on the MCP OAuth screen and is this workspace's only member and owner, so it starts writable rather than requiring a human to flip a setting a `user_token` can never reach (`PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/mcp-settings` stays refused to user tokens). Always `false` on the app-credential branch, a console session, or a `user_token` holding only `mcp:read`. On an idempotent replay this is the workspace's actual current value, not re-derived from this call.

retained_conversion_exports.description: `conversion_exports` rows left attached to the archived workspace. Never deleted — a database trigger refuses, and they are the record of what Atribu transmitted.

retained_signal_audit_rows.description: `tracking_signal_audit_log` rows left attached to the archived workspace.

archived.description: TRUE only when THIS call archived it. FALSE on a repeat — the workspace was already archived, `archived_at` is the original timestamp, and nothing changed. Both are 200.

profiles_purged.description: Profiles whose non-audit data this call purged.

warnings.description: Present only when something degraded. The workspace is archived either way — the archive commits in one transaction before any purge runs — so a purge that could not finish is reported here rather than as an error telling you to retry something that already succeeded. Omitted, not an empty array, when nothing degraded.

customer_profile_id.description: The customer to erase, when you already hold their id (from `GET /api/v1/customers`).

email.description: Exact match on `primary_email`, case-insensitive. No fuzzy matching anywhere on this route: erasure is irreversible, so erasing the wrong person is the failure to design against.

phone.description: Exact match on `primary_phone`. Unlike identity resolution elsewhere in Atribu, there is no phone-SUFFIX match here — see `email`.

identifier_type.description: With `identifier_value`, an exact match on `customer_profile_identifiers` — the way to name someone by a RUT, a GoHighLevel contact id, a Stripe customer id or a WhatsApp number. Both fields must be supplied together.

profile_id.description: Narrows the search to one profile inside the workspace. Omit to search the whole workspace, which is usually what a data-subject request means.

reason.description: Recorded verbatim in the audit row. **Never put personal data here** — the audit row exists to outlive the erasure, so anything in this field outlives it too.

customer_profile_ids.description: Every customer erased — the match plus its whole merge chain, followed in both directions. One person split across a survivor and its merged predecessors is one person, and half an erasure is not an erasure.

erased.description: TRUE when this call erased at least one customer that was not already redacted. FALSE on a repeat — still a 200, because a person may ask twice and a provider may redeliver.

counts.description: Rows changed per store. Keys are table names; the authoritative list is whatever the erasure touched, so treat this as data rather than a fixed shape.

audit_event_id.description: The `audit_log_events` row, written in the SAME transaction as the erasure — readable through the workspace audit trail. It records who erased whom and when, by id and count only; it never contains an e-mail, phone, name or national id.

media_objects_deleted.description: Conversation media files removed from object storage.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems. The erasure itself has already committed when these arise, so they are reported rather than raised — a 500 would tell you to retry something that succeeded.

profile_id.description: A profile in this workspace this person has ACTIVE access to.

permissions.description: This membership's `view:*` / `manage:*` permission keys, VERBATIM from `profile_memberships.permissions` — not re-derived from `profile_role` on read, so it reflects exactly what the last write set.

email.description: From Atribu's own user record. Null only on the rare miss where the admin read fails — never invented, and never absent because it was never asked for.

workspace_role.description: `owner`, `admin`, `analyst`, or `guest`. `owner` can appear here (it is the workspace's provisioned owner, always present) even though this endpoint can never assign or change it — see the module note on owner off-limits.

status.description: `user_memberships.status`. Always `active` for a row this endpoint returns.

profiles.description: This person's ACTIVE profile memberships in this workspace — never their raw reachable set. An `admin` or `analyst` reaches every profile in the workspace regardless of what is listed here (workspace-role inheritance, not a per-profile grant); `guest` reaches ONLY the profiles listed. Empty for `admin`/`analyst` unless an explicit `profile_memberships` row also exists for them.

email.description: The person. A passwordless Atribu user is found-or-created for it, exactly as provisioning does for the workspace owner. This is IDENTITY, not an idempotency key — the idempotency key is the pair (this workspace, this email).

workspace_role.description: `owner` is not offered — see the module note. `admin` and `analyst` reach every profile in the workspace regardless of `profiles` below (inherited, not granted); `guest` reaches ONLY the profiles named in `profiles`, and nothing if it is omitted.

locale.description: Seeded onto the person's `user_profiles.locale` ONLY on the call that CREATES that user. A later call sharing the same email must not silently change a language the person (or an earlier call) already set.

profile_id.description: Must belong to THIS workspace and be unarchived. Otherwise `404 not_found`.

permissions.description: `view:*` / `manage:*` keys. Absent ⇒ `profile_role`'s default bundle. Present ⇒ EXACTLY that list, taken verbatim after validation. An unknown key is `400 invalid_parameter` naming it — unlike the invitations surface, this endpoint never silently drops one: a 200/201 must mean everything sent was recorded.

profiles.description: When PRESENT, this is the person's COMPLETE profile access in this workspace: every listed profile is granted at the given role/permissions, and every ACTIVE profile membership NOT listed is removed. When ABSENT, existing profile access is left entirely untouched — omitting `profiles` is how you change only `workspace_role` without touching per-profile grants. A `profile_id` listed twice is `400 invalid_parameter`; a `profile_id` not in this workspace (or archived) is `404 not_found`.

created.description: True when this call created the WORKSPACE membership (HTTP 201). False when it updated an existing one (HTTP 200) — the status code carries the same signal.

created_user.description: True when this call also created the shadow Atribu user for `email` — i.e. no user with that email existed yet for this app. `locale` is applied only when this is true.

pattern_dim.description: Which creative dimension the row is about — `archetype`, `narrative_arc`, `dominant_third_combo`, `role_presence`, `social_proof_duration_bucket`, `hook_claim_cta`.

pattern_winning_signal.description: What the pattern appears to be doing well. Prose, never a measure.

sample_n.description: Ads carrying this value in the window — the denominator of `win_rate`.

win_rate.description: `winner_n / sample_n`. Meaningless without the baseline below.

workspace_baseline_win_rate.description: The workspace's OWN win rate over the same window — the honest comparator. A 40% win rate is excellent against a 20% baseline and poor against a 60% one.

lift_vs_workspace.description: `win_rate / workspace_baseline_win_rate`. An ASSOCIATION, never a cause, and never to be rendered without the interval below.

confidence_interval_high.description: Wilson 95% interval on `win_rate`. NULL when `sample_n` is 0.

archetype_cluster.description: The cluster's opaque id. Stable within a workspace and meaningless across one — never compare it between workspaces.

win_rate.description: `winner_n / sample_n`. Meaningless without the baseline below.

workspace_baseline_win_rate.description: The workspace's OWN win rate over the same window — the honest comparator. A 40% win rate is excellent against a 20% baseline and poor against a 60% one.

lift_vs_workspace.description: `win_rate / workspace_baseline_win_rate`. An ASSOCIATION, never a cause, and never to be rendered without the interval below.

confidence_interval_high.description: Wilson 95% interval on `win_rate`. NULL when `sample_n` is 0.

derived_state.description: Computed from the study's own timestamps rather than stored, so it cannot go stale against `start_time` / `end_time` / `observation_end_time`.

best_grade.description: Best `quality_grade` across this study's results; `A` is best.

primary_incremental_conversions.description: Conversions Meta estimates would NOT have happened without the ad. A COUNT, not money and not a percentage — the underlying column is `experiment_results.conversions_incremental`. NULL until results land.

primary_confidence.description: Confidence level the interval was computed at (e.g. 80, 90, 95).

primary_winner_cell_name.description: From the best `split_comparison` result — a DIFFERENT result row than the incremental estimate. A study can carry one without the other; they are not two views of one number.

profile_attributed_revenue.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

profile_spend.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

test_key.description: The stable key a decision is recorded against — `(workspace, profile, score_window, test_key)`. Never the exemplar ad, which rotates on every rebuild.

win_rate.description: `winner_n / sample_n`. Meaningless without the baseline below.

workspace_baseline_win_rate.description: The workspace's OWN win rate over the same window — the honest comparator. A 40% win rate is excellent against a 20% baseline and poor against a 60% one.

lift_vs_workspace.description: `win_rate / workspace_baseline_win_rate`. An ASSOCIATION, never a cause, and never to be rendered without the interval below.

confidence_interval_high.description: Wilson 95% interval on `win_rate`. NULL when `sample_n` is 0.

exemplar_ad_external_id.description: The concrete ad the evidence came from, so the suggestion can be checked.

exemplar_roas.description: The exemplar's ROAS — a ratio over attributed cash. NULL when it has none.

exemplar_composite_score.description: The exemplar's rule-blend score (0–100). NOT a probability and NOT cash — a separate field from `exemplar_roas` for the same reason the leaderboard keeps its three measures apart.

queued_status.description: `dismissed` | `drafted`, or null when nobody has decided yet.

at_risk_spend_dollars.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

lift_backed_count.description: Ads whose score is backed by an EXPERIMENT (`truth_grade='lift'`) rather than by a model or an attributed outcome. Normally small; that is the true state, not a bug.

open_recs_value_dollars.description: The summed `expected_impact_dollars` of the open recommendations. A FORECAST, never realised cash.

reporting_currency.description: ISO-4217 code the two amounts are denominated in — the WORKSPACE's `reporting_currency`, not any one profile's. Both sums add rows from profiles that may each report in a different currency, so every row is converted into this code before it is summed. There is no way to derive it from the response.

fx_missing_rows.description: Rows dropped from the two sums because no exchange rate existed for their (currency, date) pair. Amounts are never converted at an assumed rate of 1, so an unconvertible row is excluded instead. A non-zero value means the totals are incomplete and should be presented as such.

assessed_count.description: Ads in this window whose wear-out question was ANSWERED — a fatigue tier exists, or the ad platform itself reports the ad paused/degraded. `at_risk_count` excludes ads with no tier by design, so it reads low both when nothing is wearing out and when nothing was assessed. When `assessed_count` is 0, present the at-risk figure as NOT ASSESSED rather than as a zero: the zero is a fact about the model, not about the ads. `null` means this particular read does not carry the counter (the workspace-summary `brief` object does not) — it never means zero.

unassessed_count.description: The exact complement of `assessed_count` over the same window: no fatigue tier and no observed paused/degraded state. Together the two partition the window.

ads_with_any_sale.description: Ads with at least one CASH conversion (`revenue_type='cash'`) attributed to them in this window. Not a count of every conversion type.

ads_meeting_evidence_floor.description: Ads with at least THREE cash conversions — the minimum evidence Atribu requires before it will recommend an action on an ad. Zero here explains an empty recommendations list.

spend.description: Spend that day, in the row's `currency`. It rides inside a jsonb document, so the column cast that keeps this surface's other amounts exact cannot reach it: the WIRE TYPE matches every other monetary field, but the digits are whatever a double already held. A display series, never a figure to reconcile.

mtd_spend.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

monthly_budget_cents.description: In CENTS. NULL when no budget is set — a different state from a zero budget, and the one that makes `pace_spend_pct` meaningless.

pace_spend_pct.description: NOT percent-of-budget-spent. Spend so far over the budget PRO-RATED to `days_elapsed / days_in_month`, so `1.0` means on track today. NULL when no budget is set.

workspace_currency.description: The WORKSPACE's reporting currency — the only code a total across these rows may carry. `currency` is this ROW's, and the two differ whenever the workspace holds profiles that report differently.

mtd_spend_workspace.description: `mtd_spend` converted into `workspace_currency`, or NULL when no exchange rate existed for the pair. Sum THIS column, never `mtd_spend`, and exclude the NULLs rather than falling back to the unconverted number.

monthly_budget_cents_workspace.description: In CENTS. The budget converted into `workspace_currency`. NULL when no budget is set (`monthly_budget_cents` is NULL too) or when no rate existed (it is not). Converted from `currency`, which `monthly_budget_currency` may override, so this and `mtd_spend_workspace` do not necessarily share a rate.

ad_name.description: Display name of the target ad. NULL when the recommendation targets no ad. Render this, never `target.ad_id` — an ad id is not something a person can recognise.

expected_impact_dollars.description: A FORECAST made when the recommendation was written.

realized_impact_dollars.description: What the apply actually produced. NULL until measured — which is not zero, and a surface that shows only `expected_impact_dollars` is reporting a hope as a result.

calibration_error.description: `realized - expected`, in the same units. NULL until measured.

data_quality_tier.description: What evidence the recommendation rests on — `cash` / `outcomes` / `engagement` / `meta_only` / `none`. The same ladder `truth_grade` walks for a leaderboard row.

total_cost_usd.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

ads_lab_session_id.description: Set once the run has been handed to Ads Lab; the handoff is idempotent on it.

status.description: The status now on the run — `sent` after a handoff lands.

ads_lab_session_id.description: The session the run is bound to. On a repeat handoff this is the FIRST one, not the id you just sent — see `already_handed_off`.

already_handed_off.description: TRUE when the run already carried a session and this call changed nothing. Your `ads_lab_session_id` was NOT stored; open the one in this response instead.

status.description: What is now recorded — on a re-decide, the NEW value.

promotion_id.description: Stable for `(workspace, profile, ad)`. Re-posting returns the SAME id rather than minting a second promotion.

status.description: The status now on the row — NOT necessarily the one you asked for. See `advanced_beyond_write`.

advanced_beyond_write.description: TRUE when the row had already advanced past the status you wrote (the reconciliation sync moved it to `live` or `linked`), so YOUR DRAFT WAS NOT STORED and the existing promotion was left untouched. A client that ignores this shows an operator a draft that was never saved.

create_job_enqueued.description: Whether a direct-create job was queued. Gated by a server flag and by the profile having a Meta ad account; the enqueue is non-fatal, so `false` here does not mean the promotion failed.

locale.description: `en` | `es`, or null when the user never chose one.

pending_email.description: An email change awaiting confirmation, or null. Reported because a pending change is otherwise INVISIBLE — `email` still shows the old address. Starting or cancelling one is not on this API: it is a Supabase Auth flow with confirmation mail to both addresses.

provider.description: The provider key (`email`, `google`, …), never a display name.

email.description: The address THAT PROVIDER knows the user by — not necessarily the account email. A linked Google account with a different address is a normal state.

is_current.description: Whether this is the session the request was made with. Resolved from the `session_id` claim on the VERIFIED bearer token, so a client does not have to decode its own JWT to know which row not to offer a revoke on.

last_active_at.description: The freshest of `refreshed_at` / `updated_at` / `created_at`, as an explicit UTC instant. Supabase stores the first of those without a time zone; it is stamped here so the value does not mean something different per reader.

user_agent.description: The raw UA string. Turning it into 'Mac · Chrome' is presentation.

aal.description: `aal1` | `aal2` — the assurance level this session reached.

sole_owner_workspaces.description: Workspaces this user is the ONLY active owner of — the blockers on `DELETE /api/v1/me`. An empty array means nothing stands in the way. Enforced there, not merely advisory: `DELETE /api/v1/me` re-checks this same list server-side before deleting anything.

client_id.description: The OAuth app's public client id.

return_url_supported.description: True exactly when the app's EFFECTIVE `allowed_return_origins` is non-empty — the explicit column when set, otherwise derived from the origins of `redirect_uris`. This is the precondition for a delegated connect start to honour a `return_url`. Check it once instead of learning the answer from the first `origin_not_allowed` 400.

blockers.description: Empty when `deleted` is true. When `deleted` is false, the caller's `sole_owner_workspaces` — transfer ownership of each, then retry.

key_prefix.description: The first few hex chars of the secret. Never the secret itself.

token.description: The live secret. Shown exactly ONCE — this response is the only time it is ever returned.

rotation_deadline.description: Set only on a rotate — when the OLD token stops working.

key_prefix.description: The first few hex chars of the secret. Never the secret itself.

key.description: The live secret. Shown exactly ONCE — this response is the only time it is ever returned.

old_key_expires_at.description: Set only on a rotate — when the OLD key stops working.

onboarding_skip_reason.description: Recorded on the `PROFILE_ONBOARDING_COMPLETED` audit row's metadata when set alongside `onboarding_completed: true` — the reviewer-skip path, distinct from a normal finish.

onboarding_state.description: #1056 — a WHOLE-OBJECT replace of the onboarding wizard's in-progress draft (never a merge). `version` must be `1`; any key this schema does not name is a 400 naming it. The server always overwrites `updated_at` with its own clock, even if you send one.

event_key.description: Which milestone this CRM pipeline-stage label maps to.

definitions.description: The FULL new list for this family, in display order — `sort_order` is assigned from array position. Every existing definition of this `definition_type` on the profile is deleted first, so an empty array clears the family.

estimated_unattributed_revenue.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

pii_mode.description: Default PII handling for MCP tool reads. `masked_default` (recommended): email and phone are masked unless a request opts in. `full_default`: tokens with `mcp:read_pii` receive raw values automatically. The `mcp:read_pii` scope and `include_sensitive=true` flag always override this default either way.

mcp_writeback_enabled.description: Whether admins with mcp:write tokens may run send_meta_conversions.

amount.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

open_url.description: A one-hour signed URL for a stored file, or the row's `external_url`. Falls back to the external link rather than disappearing if storage cannot mint one — the row is the record that the agreement exists.

medianValue.description: Median seeded member value, or null when the seed has no valued members.

totalSeedValue.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

refundsSubtracted.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

value.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

url.description: The client-facing `/s/<token>` page. SECRET-BEARING: the unguessable link token is part of the URL, so anyone holding this string can open the provisioning flow. Treat it like a credential — do not log it, and do not put it in a URL bar a screen-share can read.

agencyName.description: The agency workspace's name, or `Atribu` when it has none. PERSONAL DATA in practice: a sole trader's workspace is usually their own name.

inviterName.description: PERSONAL DATA — the name of the person who created the link. Falls back through the account's `full_name`, then `name`, then the LOCAL PART OF THEIR EMAIL, so a user with no profile metadata publishes half their address here.

clientName.description: PERSONAL DATA in practice — the client profile's name, frequently a person's or a clinic owner's.

metaUserName.description: PERSONAL DATA — the display name of the Meta account holder who authorised the link, as Meta's `/me` reported it.

missingPermissions.description: Meta permissions the authorising user did not grant, from `['ads_read', 'ads_management']`. Empty once provisioning succeeds.

stages.description: The provisioning ladder, newest state per stage. Rebuilt on every state change; empty before the client opens the link.

adAccounts.description: The client's active Meta ad accounts, offered ONLY while `status` is `choice_required` — `null` in every other state, which is a state signal and not an absence of accounts. `currency` is an ISO-4217 CODE, never an amount.

resultSummary.description: What provisioning actually created, once it has finished. `currency` is an ISO-4217 CODE. Null until then.

lastError.description: Why the last provisioning attempt failed. USUALLY a stable machine token (`token_missing`, `no_ad_account`, `missing_ads_management`) but NOT guaranteed to be one: two paths put raw upstream text here — a Meta Graph error message and a Postgres error message — so do not switch on it without a default.

ConversionSyncFeedRow.description: A conversion_exports row, enriched with the credited touch, customer context and per-attempt delivery log — the same shape the internal dashboard's Deliveries feed renders. Deliberately open: the row carries the export's raw + redacted payload snapshots, which are large and change shape by destination.

checked_at.description: When the OLDEST verdict in `results` was computed. Null when nothing is cached.

stale.description: True when at least one verdict is past the 6h cache TTL. A stale read still returns the cached rows and kicks off a background refresh — it never blocks.

ttl_ms.description: The cache TTL the `stale` flag is computed against, in milliseconds.

current_custom_event_type.description: What this ad set optimizes for TODAY, resolved rather than copied: Meta's raw enum where the enum is the answer, and the real event name where it would misrepresent it (an inline pixel_rule, a custom_event_str, or a nameable Custom Conversion).

ad_count.description: Live ads in this ad set. NULL means the count could not be fetched — never a confident 0, which matters because an ad set with no ads cannot deliver anything.

daily_budget.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

lifetime_budget.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

spend_7d.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

conversions_7d.description: Meta-reported conversions on this ad set over the trailing 7 days.

repointability.description: Result of a validate_only preflight of the exact write (#306). `unknown` means the probe did not run or could not answer — Meta exposes no readable flag for a frozen ad set, so the only way to ask is to attempt the write.

needs_duplicate_swap.description: Meta froze these ad sets' conversion at publish. Rebuilding is the only route and it costs a new ad set id, a learning reset and (in `switch` mode) a pause of the original — so it needs its own yes: re-send with `confirm_duplicate_swap` and a `duplicate_swap_mode`.

double_spend_risk.description: The replacement is live and the ORIGINAL could not be paused — both are spending. Pause the original in Ads Manager.

code.description: Meta's classifier verdict for THIS ad set (`adset_published_immutable`, `reconnect_required`, `insufficient_scope`, `generic`, …).

active_since.description: When the Clean Dataset destination row was created — go-live.

daily.description: A dense 14-day series; missing days are zero-filled, never absent.

deltaPct.description: NULL until the dataset has been live a full 14 days. Before that the prior week is padded with pre-provision zero days, which would fabricate enormous growth — the DELTA is suppressed, never the counts.

wow.description: Last 7 chart days vs the prior 7.

learning.description: Progress toward Meta's ~50-conversion learning threshold. The total is counted since go-live and is deliberately UNCLAMPED: a rolling floor would reset the ring for exactly the low-volume advertisers this mode exists for.

verdict.description: `not_started` | `verifying` | `cutover_clean` | … — rolled up across the old datasets. A guardrail violation blocks `cutover_clean`: the Clean Dataset must stay single-source.

status.description: Absent on the `not_started` branch — with no clean dataset there is nothing to classify the old feeds against.

guardrail_violations.description: Config-level ways the Clean Dataset has stopped being single-source.

can_edit.description: Whether THIS caller may add or remove a field: a person must be a workspace owner or admin; an API key holding `exports:write` may.

safe_fields.description: The always-on floor. Present on every Platform-Safe payload and impossible to remove.

added_by.description: Display name captured when the field was added, or the API key id.

is_self.description: Always false for an API key — there is no 'you' behind one.

outcome_type.description: The Atribu outcome-event type this conversion is registered under.

meta_event_name.description: The NEUTRAL Meta event name the rule matches — never a health term.

destination_id.description: The `tracking_export_destinations` row the Clean Dataset now lives on.

manual_steps.description: The plan the advertiser must carry out by hand in Events Manager.

PlatformSafeProvisionResponse.description: TWO shapes at 200, discriminated by `status`. `action_required` is NOT a failure: Atribu asked Meta and the answer was that a human has to do this part — the token lacks `ads_management`, or the ad account's single self-created-pixel slot is already held by the advertiser's own pixel and a Clean Dataset must have zero restriction history. Neither is fixable by a retry, which is why neither is a 4xx.

current_event_name.description: The event the ad set actually NAMES, when it names one (an inline `pixel_rule` or a `custom_event_str`). Display only: go-live maps on the CATEGORY, and when this disagrees with it there is no safe mapping at all.

target.description: The Clean Dataset conversion this ad set would move to — the shared resolver's own shape (`cleanDatasetId`, `cleanCcId`, `metaEventName`, `eventType`, `neutralName`), passed through rather than re-described, so it cannot drift from its producer.

unmappable_reason.description: Why `target` is null. `event_diverges_from_category` means the ad set optimizes for a specific event its category does not stand for, so mapping on the category would change what it optimizes for — 25 ad sets on one prod account are in exactly that state (2026-09-09).

mode.description: `repoint` — Meta accepts an in-place `promoted_object` edit. `recreate` — Meta froze it at publish (subcode 3260011), so the only route is a NEW ad set, costing a new id and a learning reset. `blocked` — some other Meta error. Determined by attempting the exact write under `validate_only`: Meta exposes no readable published/frozen flag, so a dry write is the only honest classification.

current_event_name.description: The event the ad set actually NAMES, when it names one (an inline `pixel_rule` or a `custom_event_str`). Display only: go-live maps on the CATEGORY, and when this disagrees with it there is no safe mapping at all.

target.description: The Clean Dataset conversion this ad set would move to — the shared resolver's own shape (`cleanDatasetId`, `cleanCcId`, `metaEventName`, `eventType`, `neutralName`), passed through rather than re-described, so it cannot drift from its producer.

unmappable_reason.description: Why `target` is null. `event_diverges_from_category` means the ad set optimizes for a specific event its category does not stand for, so mapping on the category would change what it optimizes for — 25 ad sets on one prod account are in exactly that state (2026-09-09).

replaced.description: Source ad sets a previous go-live already recreated. Their `promoted_object` still names the old dataset, so without this list they would be offered forever as "not migrated yet" with a live replacement already running beside them.

needs_recreate.description: Meta froze these; re-send them with `confirm_recreate: true` to rebuild.

queued.description: Export jobs the worker was handed.

handoff_id.description: The `pick` hand-off minted BESIDE the link, so an agent that cannot open a browser has one id to poll via `GET /api/v1/handoffs/{id}`. Its clock mirrors the link's (14 days), not the hand-off default. NULL when the mint failed — the link is what the human needs, and losing the agent's poll handle never costs the agency the link.

skipped_no_identifiers.description: Customers dropped because they carry no hashable identifier.

cashCustomers.description: Buyers that made it into the seed.

totalCashIn.description: Sum of positive cash across the deduped input window — `conversions.value_amount_reporting`.

totalSeedValue.description: Sum of the member values actually seeded, refunds already netted out.

refundsSubtracted.description: Refunded cash removed from the seed values, as a positive amount.

leadCustomers.description: Qualified leads available for the identity-only fallback seed.

lookalikes.description: The proposed lookalike ladder (1% and a 1–5% BAND, not a second overlapping 5%).

consent_note.description: Always present, because the separation it describes is the feature: proposing computes the seed and records the proposal, and NOTHING reaches Meta until `/audiences/confirm`.

checked_at.description: When Meta last answered. The score is only meaningful beside it.

bucket.description: Meta's score band for the composite.

emq.description: NULL for a messaging dataset — read `coverage` instead.

coverage.description: Share of recent sent payloads carrying each match key. NOT an EMQ — Meta does not score messaging events, and this is Atribu's own proxy, present only when `kind !== "website"`.

emq_status.description: NULL for a messaging dataset — Meta does not score them.

sent_count_30d.description: Events ATRIBU sent under this name in 30 days — our ledger, not Meta's.

missing.description: Meta never saw this key on the event.

capability.description: Whether Atribu can supply it now, needs upstream capture, or excludes it.

fillable_now.description: Keys Meta is missing that Atribu already holds — what the re-send fixes.

needs_capture.description: Keys nobody holds yet; a re-send cannot help until capture changes.

history.description: Ascending by `captured_at` — the honest improvement state.

coverage.description: Share of recent sent payloads carrying each match key. NOT an EMQ — Meta does not score messaging events, and this is Atribu's own proxy, present only when `kind !== "website"`.

contact_stats.description: The profile's contact-identifier fill rates — the real-world CAUSE behind a low phone/email match. NULL when the read failed; it is context, not the answer.

events.description: Per event: the params Meta reports missing, split into fillable-now, needs-upstream-capture and excluded-by-design. Shape owned by `reconcileEmqRecommendations` in @atribu/export.

window_days.description: The window actually applied — 7, 14 or 28. A larger request clamps DOWN.

history_days.description: Distinct accumulated days — how far back this view can be trusted.

last_polled_at.description: `total_events` is a snapshot as of this moment while `atribu_sent` is live. Show it, or the current day's gap reads as disagreement rather than freshness.

total_events.description: NULL means no accumulated coverage for this event, not zero events.

count.description: ACTIVE ad sets only, as Events Manager counts.

names.description: Up to 10 ACTIVE names — a preview; `count` is exact.

ad_sets_unavailable.description: TRUE when the Graph read failed, so every `ad_sets.count` is 0 because we COULD NOT ASK — not because no ad set uses the event. A renderer must say "couldn't check" rather than printing the zero; that exact conflation is the bug this table exists to end.

blocked.description: Non-null ⇒ this profile cannot reach Meta yet, and every list in the response is empty for THAT reason rather than because nothing exists.

currency.description: Read live from the ad account and never guessed — every budget here is denominated in it, and CLP-vs-USD is a 100x error in the minor-unit conversion.

month.description: Server's `YYYY-MM`, so a client-side name preview matches the plan byte for byte.

adOptions.description: Existing ads available to copy into Testing cells, active first.

cells.description: The Testing cells, as stored. Shape owned by the planner.

retargeting.description: Always present, empty when blocked — "why is retargeting not offered" is itself the answer this step exists to give.

blocked.description: Non-null ⇒ the search COULD NOT RUN (no usable Meta connection) and `interests` is empty for that reason, not because nothing matched. Without this an empty list is indistinguishable from "no interest is named that".

refusal.description: Present on `refused`. A refusal is a considered product answer with a payload the caller renders (the assessment drives "run one cell instead"), which is why it is a 200 and not a 4xx — and why it guarantees NOTHING was created.

cells.description: The Testing cells, as stored. Shape owned by the planner.

ladder.description: Every rung the builder attempted, with its outcome.

failureDetail.description: On `failed`. A partial tree is entirely PAUSED so it costs nothing, but it EXISTS — the ladder carries every id. A retry needs a NEW idempotency key.

currency.description: The ad account's own currency, read live from Meta. NULL means the read FAILED — it is never guessed. See `currency_unavailable`.

currency_unavailable.description: True ⇒ the currency read failed, so `currency` and `minor_per_major` are null and every budget below is in an UNKNOWN unit. A renderer must say "couldn't check" rather than pick a symbol — printing dollars for pesos is a 100x misstatement on a screen that carries a one-click budget change.

minor_per_major.description: How many minor units make a major one in `currency`. 1 for whole-unit currencies (CLP, COP, CRC, HUF, IDR, ISK, …) where Meta's minor unit IS the major unit.

fatigue_unavailable.description: True ⇒ the Cox fatigue read FAILED, so every `fatigue` below is null for that reason rather than because nothing is fatiguing. Fatigue is the one signal that OVERRIDES a `room_to_scale` verdict, so this is the difference between "safe to scale" and "we could not check whether this ad is dying".

daily_budget_minor.description: MINOR units per day, verbatim from Meta — divide by `minor_per_major`, never by a hardcoded 100. Null when the campaign owns the budget (CBO) or the ad set is on a lifetime budget.

is_directional.description: Always `true`. A structural reminder that this is a DIRECTIONAL read of traceable ROAS and fatigue — never a causal or incrementality claim. Consumers must label it as such.

guidance.description: The directional call and WHAT it was derived from. `basis` names the signals that actually contributed — read it with `fatigue_unavailable` below, because a missing signal lowers confidence rather than changing the direction.

recent_spend.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

privacy_mode.description: FOUR values, matching the database's own CHECK. `platform_safe` means the profile sends Meta a deliberately narrowed payload from a NEW (Clean) dataset, so health or other sensitive context cannot reach the ad platform.

privacy_config.description: The profile's privacy filters: `url_sanitization`, `url_allowlist`, `event_blocklist_paths`, `parameter_allowlist`, `parameter_blocklist`, the `strip_*` booleans, `enable_ldu`, and `healthcare_export_allowlist`. Refresh it with `GET /api/v1/conversion-sync/dataset-quality`. An empty array means we have not asked yet, which is not the same as a healthy dataset.
