cached.description: True when the answer came from the stored summary rather than a model call.

ReadinessNext.description:
The one next action for this step, in one of two shapes.

`{method, path}` is a call you can make right now with the credential you already hold, and the path is always one this API serves TODAY — never a route that is being built. Where a step's own write does not exist on v1 yet, the nearest existing route is named and `why` says where the write actually happens.

`{handoff_kind}` is a class of action only a PERSON can take: `connect` (an OAuth consent — it needs a browser), `sign_dpa` (a signature), `checkout` (a payment), `contact_support` (Atribu itself has to change something). It tells you WHAT kind of hand-off is owed, not where: minting the actual URL is a separate capability.

`null` only when `status` is `done`. Every other status carries one.

key.description: Which step this is. The `steps` array is always ALL of them, in golden-path order.

status.description:
`done` — satisfied. `missing` — never configured; the ordinary next thing to do. `degraded` — configured and not working (a reconnect-required ad account), so the fix is to RE-connect rather than to connect. `blocked` — cannot be satisfied by you at all; today only `attribution_enabled` on a partner-provisioned profile.

Only `done` counts toward `summary.done`. `degraded` is not partial credit: a destination that is configured and failing exports nothing.

why.example: meta_ads is connected but its status is "reconnect_required" — it is not delivering spend or delivery data.
why.description: One plain-English sentence saying why the step is in this state — which provider is degraded, whether the attribution windows are defaults or a choice, where a write happens when this API has no route for it yet. Written to be read and relayed, so it names concrete routes and providers. Not localized: render Spanish off `key` and `status`, which are stable, rather than off this sentence, which is not.

evidence.description:
`measured` — every fact behind this step was read. `unavailable` — Atribu's analytics store could not be reached and this step's answer depended on it, so `status` is reported as `degraded` and says nothing about how the profile is configured.

Treat an `unavailable` step as "not known right now": do not tell anyone to configure something on the strength of it, and do not count it against them. Retry the call. Steps whose evidence is entirely core-side — the connection steps, the legal step, the plan, the entitlement — stay `measured` throughout such an outage.

docs_url.description: The documentation page that explains this step.

done.description: How many steps are `done`. `degraded` steps are not counted.

total.description: How many steps there are. Published so you need not hardcode it.

next_step.description: The FIRST non-`done` step in golden-path order, or null when everything is done. First, not 'most important': the order IS the priority.

steps.description: Every step, always, in golden-path order. A checklist that omitted the steps it could not evaluate would have a length that varies by profile, and `done`/`total` would stop meaning anything.

wizard_finished.description: `onboarding_completed` on the profile — REPORTED, NOT TRUSTED. It means one thing: a person pressed Finish in the Atribu console's setup wizard. Every wizard step is skippable, so it is not evidence that any step above is done, and nothing in `summary` is derived from it. Use it only to tell 'has been through onboarding and is still missing things' from 'nobody has started'.

analytics.description:
Whether the analytics store this checklist measures most of its steps from could be read.

`unavailable` means the request still succeeded — every core-side step is measured and trustworthy — but each step carrying `evidence: "unavailable"` is reporting a default rather than a measurement. `summary.done` is then a FLOOR, never a verdict. Nothing about the profile changed; retry the same call.

click_window_days.description: How many days after a CLICK a conversion still counts as attributed to it.

view_window_hours.description: How many hours after a VIEW (no click) a conversion still counts as attributed to it.

first_touch_window_days.description: How far back to look for a profile's FIRST touch on a conversion's path.

cash_window_days.description: Overrides the first-touch window for CASH conversions only — high-ticket sales that close long after the ad click. `null` (the default) means cash conversions use the normal windows above; leads and appointments always do, regardless of this setting.

AttributionSettingsUpdate.description: A PARTIAL update — an omitted key leaves that window untouched. `cash_window_days: null` clears the override; omitting it leaves the current value alone.

replay_queued.description: Whether a full-profile attribution replay was queued. A window redefines which touches attach to which conversion retroactively, so a save that could not queue one leaves already-reported numbers computed under the OLD window until the next replay.

replay_error.description: Why the replay could not be queued, when replay_queued is false.

timezone.description: IANA zone for the demo profile. Defaults to the workspace's `default_timezone`, then UTC. Day boundaries in every read are computed in it.

currency.description: ISO-4217. Every seeded amount — ad spend, payments, the one refund — is denominated in it. Defaults to USD.

touches.description: Marketing visits written to `touches` — paid Meta clicks plus organic/direct.

outcome_events.description: `outcome_events` rows written through the same CRM-ingest primitive every real provider uses: lead_created → appointment_booked → payment_received, plus one refund.

conversions.description: How many conversions the recompute this call enqueued WILL produce. It is the dataset's promise, not a count already in the table: the engine runs asynchronously, so poll `GET /api/v1/overview` until it matches.

spend_days.description: Distinct days of ad spend seeded, so ROAS has a denominator.

definitions.description: `conversion_definitions` on the new profile. Seeded by the database on profile creation, exactly as for a real profile — the demo does not get its own set.

id.description: `tracking_export_destinations.id`. Null only when the destination write failed — see `warnings`; the profile and its data are still there.

mode.description: Always `recording`. This is not a destination TYPE — the row is an ordinary Meta CAPI destination with a placeholder pixel id. Recording is a property of the PROFILE: the worker builds the real payload, applies the real privacy and legal gates, writes it to `conversion_exports.payload`, and never calls Meta. The row carries `status: "skipped"` and `skip_reason: "demo_profile_recorded"`.

created.description: True only when THIS call created the profile. A second call re-seeds the existing one and answers 200 with `created: false` — the status IS the idempotency signal, and this field repeats it for callers behind a proxy that rewrites statuses.

warnings.description: Non-fatal problems during the seed. Empty on a clean run. A seed never half-fails silently: anything that did not land is named here rather than swallowed.

archived.description: #1170 — always true alongside `deleted`. The delete is an ARCHIVE + PURGE: the seeded data is removed and the profile row is archived rather than deleted, because `conversion_exports` is audit evidence a database trigger refuses to let any user-facing path erase. The workspace's demo slot is released either way, so you can create a new demo immediately.

retained_audit_rows.description: How many audit rows stayed attached to the archived profile (conversion exports plus signal-audit entries). Zero for a demo that never ran an export.

session_timeout_minutes.description: Minutes of inactivity before the tracker starts a new session.

session_mode.description: `inactivity_only` starts a new session after `session_timeout_minutes` of inactivity and nothing else. `inactivity_or_source_change` ALSO starts one when the visitor arrives from a different marketing source, so a second ad click in the same browsing session is a second visit rather than a continuation of the first.

enable_geo_enrichment.description: Resolve country/region/city from the request IP during enrichment.

enable_user_agent_enrichment.description: Resolve device/browser/OS from the User-Agent during enrichment.

enable_channel_classification.description: Classify each touch into a marketing channel from its UTMs and referrer. Off means every touch stays unclassified.

export_meta_enabled.description: READ-ONLY here. Owned by Conversion Sync (the destinations catalogue) — returned so a caller can render current state without a second read, but PATCH does not accept it.

intercept_meta_fbq_enabled.description: Let the tracker observe the site's own `fbq()` calls, so a form the Meta Pixel already saw is captured even when no Atribu detection layer fired.

meta_bridge_pageview_enabled.description: Also mirror Meta Pixel `PageView` events. Off by default: a page view is already captured natively, and mirroring it doubles the volume for no extra signal.

early_identity_capture_enabled.description: Per-profile kill switch for pre-submit identity capture (email/phone read at input blur). Default on.

replay_queued.description: True when this save enqueued a full-profile attribution replay.

replay_error.description: Why the replay could not be queued. The settings were still saved — a queue failure is reported, never thrown.

value_amount.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

payload.description: The event's own body, verbatim. MAY CONTAIN PII — a `lead_submitted` payload carries the email/phone the tracker captured, which is why this route requires `visitors:read` rather than `analytics:read`.

days.description: The window ACTUALLY read, after the retention clamp.

nonce.description: Append `?atb_verify=<nonce>` to any tracked URL and load it once.

status.description: `expired` is computed on READ from `expires_at` — no cron flips it, so a pending attempt past its TTL always reads as expired.

business_conversions.description: The profile's conversions over the same window. NULL (never 0) when the count could not be read — a failed read rendered as zero is a wrong number read as fact.

missing_browser_ids.description: Bridge events carrying neither `fbp` nor `fbc` — unmatchable at Meta.

sent.description: A count OVER THE SAMPLE, not a total. Read it with `sampled_conversions` and `complete`.

fallback_event_id_count.description: Exports whose `external_event_id` fell back to the raw outcome-event id instead of the booking cluster's canonical id — those cannot dedup against the Pixel at Meta.

window_conversions.description: The window's true conversion total, or null when it could not be read.

complete.description: True when the sample covered the whole window, so `sent` IS the total. False means `sent` is 'N of the most recent `sampled_conversions`'.

conversion_events.description: The TRACKER's conversion events. Not the profile's conversions — that is `business_conversions`, and the two are routinely orders of magnitude apart because most conversions arrive from a CRM or a payment provider, never through a browser.

cname_target.description: The CNAME every domain on this profile must point at. Null when this deployment has no collect host configured — creating a domain then answers 503.

domain.description: The hostname to serve tracking from. A scheme and path are stripped, so `https://trk.dealer.com/` is accepted and stored as `trk.dealer.com`.

external_event_id.description: The id Meta/Google dedups on. Null means nothing was ever sent under an id — see the `missing_external_event_id` warning.

value_amount.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

outcome_event.description: The conversion this delivery carries. Null when the export outlived the outcome event it pointed at.

destination.description: Narrow the retry to one destination. Omit to retry both.

enabled.description: `true` starts Atribu's pipeline for this profile — recompute, the AI agent, conversation/conversion extraction, automatic events, and the ad-platform sync's performance-shaped work (insights/spend, messaging metrics, attribution, conversions, exports) — and enqueues the standard backfill window for any ad-platform connection this profile already holds. `false` returns the profile to connectivity-only mode: the ad-platform sync keeps refreshing structure and conversational configuration (campaign/ad names, the CTWA greeting) but skips everything performance-shaped. Nothing is ever deleted by turning this off.

occurred_at.description:
When YOU made this decision (the subscription event's own timestamp), ISO-8601 with an offset. Optional, and omitting it keeps the previous behaviour: the last call to arrive wins.

Send it if your delivery is at-least-once and unordered — an outbox retry, a webhook fan-out. Atribu records the newest value it has seen and IGNORES any later delivery carrying a strictly older one, answering `200` with `changed: false` and `ignored_stale: true` and writing nothing at all. That is the only protection against a retried cancellation landing after the renewal that superseded it; idempotency alone cannot order two contradictory calls.

changed.description:
False when the entitlement was already at this value — a replay. A replay answers HTTP 200 and enqueues NOTHING: the backfill fires once, on the real transition, because a duplicate delivery from an at-least-once outbox must not cost a second full sync pass. If a call flipped the entitlement and then failed before the backfill was enqueued, recover it with `POST /api/v1/connections/sync` (`force_full: true`) — the same endpoint a "Hard refresh" uses — not by replaying this one.

The grant side is the exception and converges on every call: see `grant`.

scopes.description: The connect scopes your profile-level grant carries NOW. `enabled: true` sets `["connections", "attribution"]`; `enabled: false` narrows it back to `["connections"]`. The grant itself is never revoked — connections are free.

revoked_keys.description: How many API keys this call revoked. Non-zero only on an `enabled: false` that found the grant actually carrying `attribution`; those keys stop authenticating within ~10 seconds. A repeated `enabled: false` reports 0 and revokes nothing, so a retry cannot kill the core key you minted after the first one — and a grant that never carried `attribution` (an older delegation such as `["analytics", "attribution_write"]`) is left exactly as it is, keys included: turning off an add-on only undoes what turning it on did.

revoked.description: True when the workspace owner has REVOKED your delegation on this profile from their connected-apps page. The entitlement still flipped — it is a billing fact — but nothing was written to the grant, `scopes` is empty, and no key was touched. Atribu will not silently re-authorize an app a human disconnected. Re-consent by replaying `POST /api/v1/profiles` (or `POST /api/v1/profiles/{profileId}/adopt`) for this dealer, then call this endpoint again.

grant.description: What this call did to your OAuth grant on this profile (#1455). Never carries a secret — mint a fresh key yourself with `grant_type=client_credentials`.

ignored_stale.description: True when this delivery was DISCARDED because its `occurred_at` is strictly older than the decision time already recorded — an out-of-order outbox retry. Nothing was written: no entitlement change, no grant change, no key revocation, no audit event. `enabled` then reports the value Atribu currently holds, not the one you sent. Treat it as success and stop retrying that delivery.

post_id.description: The platform's own post id — Instagram `ig_media_id` or Facebook `fb_post_id`. This is the value the two detail routes take as `{id}`.

media_type.description: IMAGE | VIDEO | CAROUSEL_ALBUM. Facebook attachment types are normalised into the same taxonomy.

media_product_type.description: FEED | REELS | STORY. Always FEED for Facebook — /posts has no Reels analogue.

caption_excerpt.description: First 240 characters of the caption (Instagram) or message (Facebook).

page_name.description: The MERCHANT's own account — Instagram username or Facebook page name.

touches_count.description: Organic touches recorded against this post inside the window.

attributed_revenue.description: Cash credit only. Pipeline value is never folded in.

ai_score.description: Null until the AI content scorer has run against this post.

visible_on_bio.description: Instagram only; always false for Facebook.

credit_value_reporting.description: This post's or story's credited share of the customer's cash conversions, in the profile's reporting currency.

touch_subtype.description: How the customer touched the content — e.g. `story_reply`, `dm`.

first_touch_time.description: Post detail only; the story read does not compute it.

Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

customers.description: NULL — not `[]` — unless the key also holds `customers:read`. An empty array would be indistinguishable from 'nobody', which is a fact you would act on; null says 'not returned to this key'.

credit_value_reporting.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

model_breakdown.description: The same post's credit under EVERY model, not only the requested one — the read computes it in the same pass.

credited_revenue.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

daily_trend.description: Credited cash by conversion day, last 30 days of the window.

allOf.description: NULL for a Facebook post, and that is a coverage statement rather than an empty result: per-post attribution detail resolves touches by `ig_media_id`, so it exists for Instagram only today. The Facebook numbers are on the post's row in `GET /api/v1/organic/posts`.

performance_score.description: 0-10. The scorer's headline read on the creative.

fatigue_score.description: 0-1. Higher means the creative repeats what this account already posted.

theme_cluster_id.description: Groups posts the scorer judged to be the same creative theme.

model_id.description: Which analyzer produced this row. A newer model supersedes an older one.

ad_external_id.description: The PLATFORM's ad id — the same identifier `GET /api/v1/ads/{id}/creative-analysis` and `GET /api/v1/top-performers` use, so a twin can be followed straight to the ad.

spend.description: LIFETIME spend on the ad, in the profile's reporting currency.

attributed_revenue.description: LIFETIME cash revenue credited to the ad. Pipeline value is never folded in.

allOf.description: NULL when the analysis pass has never covered this post. That is COVERAGE, not a verdict: the pass is a metered background job and this route never runs it.

twin_ads.description: `[]` — not null — when nothing matched: the profile has no paid creative near this caption, or has no creative embeddings yet.

attributed_revenue.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

customers.description: NULL — not `[]` — unless the key also holds `customers:read`. An empty array would be indistinguishable from 'nobody', which is a fact you would act on; null says 'not returned to this key'.

replies.description: Up to 50 story replies, newest first. The sender AND the text they sent are identity: NULL — not `[]` — unless the key also holds `customers:read`. An empty array would be indistinguishable from 'nobody', which is a fact you would act on; null says 'not returned to this key'.
Replies Instagram counted. `kpis.replies_count` is how many Atribu matched to a touch.

date_to.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive). Max range: 366 days.

model.description: Attribution model. One of: last_touch, first_touch, linear, time_decay, last_non_direct

analysis_version.description: The analysis schema this row was written under. The route serves the current version only, so this is informational, not a selector.

method.description: `llm_vision_v2` (video analysed) | `llm_thumbnail_v2` (still image only) | `llm_copy_only_v2` (no visual). The pass degrades down this ladder rather than failing when a video source cannot be resolved.

primary_angle.description: One line naming the specific promise the creative makes, in its own language.

audience_warmth.description: prospecting | retargeting | unknown — the cohort dimension this feeds.

dominant_scene_role.description: The beat role the most screen time went to.

AdCreativeVideoAnalysis.description: The visual/temporal half. NULL-heavy by design: populated only when `method` is `llm_vision_v2`. On a thumbnail-only or copy-only pass every time-based field is null and `scenes` is empty — a null here means 'not observed', never 'the ad does not do this'.

role.description: hook | problem | solution | product_demo | social_proof | offer | cta | b_roll | other. A hint, not an enum — the extraction schema accepts free text so a single off-vocabulary beat cannot fail the whole analysis.

on_screen_text.description: Verbatim on-screen text or captions visible during this beat.

spoken_excerpt.description: Verbatim excerpt of what is said during this beat.

camera_shot.description: handheld | static | split_screen | talking_head | b_roll | screen_recording | other. A hint, not an enum.

what_changed.description: The specific change from the previous beat.

id.description: The job id. Stable for the life of the 24h idempotency window: a second POST for the same ad and the same creative returns THIS id rather than minting a new one.

status.description: The returned job is always live — `queued`, `running` or `succeeded`. A terminal failure is never handed back as the current job (see `previous_attempt`).

reused.description: True when an existing job came back instead of a new one — the same fact the 200-vs-202 status carries, repeated here so it survives in a logged body.

requested_at.description: When the returned job was FIRST requested, which on a reuse is earlier than this call.

analysis_version.description: The analysis schema the job will write under.

input_hash.description: The creative's source signature at request time — the idempotency key. Edit the ad's name, headline, body, video or thumbnail and this changes, which is what makes the next POST a new job rather than a reuse.

previous_attempt.description: The most recent attempt at this same creative that ended terminally, if there was one inside the window. `failed` means the run was attempted and did not produce an analysis; `blocked` means it was never attempted — either the background analysis pass is switched off for this deployment, or the workspace's daily creative-analysis allowance was still spent after the job had already waited a full UTC day — and cost nothing against your daily budget. A failed or blocked job is deliberately NOT reused, so this is how you see it.

budget.description: Where this request left the two daily budgets, both per UTC day. `api_key_*` is 0/0 for a session credential, which has no key to charge. A reuse consumes nothing and reports zeros.

marked.description: Ads that will be (or have just been) marked for analysis.

already_analysed.description: Ads in the window that already carry a current-version analysis.

total_with_spend.description: Every ad with spend in the window — `marked + already_analysed`.

lookback_days.description: The window the RPC actually used, after clamping to the nearest option ≤ it.

daily_cap.description: The workspace's daily `creative_analysis` allowance, from the plan tier.

estimated_days.description: `ceil(marked / daily_cap)`, or null when the plan's cap is 0.

resets_at.description: The next 00:00 UTC, when the allowance refills.

applied.description: False for a dry run, true once the ads were marked.

sum_clp.description: Sum of rows resolved to CLP. The whole total for a Transbank parse (CLP-only by construction); a CLP-only subtotal for offline sales — see by_currency.

by_currency.description: Sum of `monto` per resolved ISO-4217 currency, across every row.

conversion_goal_ok.description: Whether the event type this importer writes (`payment_received`) resolves to a conversion_definitions row for this profile. False is a BLOCKING condition — .../import/commit refuses when this is false, because an imported sale would otherwise persist and never become a counted conversion (data-model.md #437).

dedupe_summary.description: Offline sales only — aggregated over EVERY parsed row (not just the 5-row `preview` sample). Null for a Transbank parse.

moneda.description: Offline sales only. ISO-4217; null means the row will use CLP.

dedupe_status.description: Offline sales only — the preview-time dedup verdict for this row. Null on a Transbank row (no pre-commit dedup preview there).

csv.description: The whole template file, as text.

AdCopyAnalysis.description: Present only when the entity carried creative text.

hook_score.description: 1-10, whole numbers — how well the first three seconds capture attention.

AdVideoAnalysis.description: Present only when a video was actually analysed — read `video_status` first.

message.description: Why a requested video analysis did not happen, in plain language — no Meta connection, no access token, no video asset on this ad, a non-ad level, no playable source from Meta, or a model that returned no structured video block. Null when nothing needs explaining.

id.description: The ad's platform/external id.

spend.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

attributed_revenue.description: Atribu-attributed CASH only, last-touch. Pipeline and messaging outcomes are deliberately excluded — mixing revenue types makes the ratio below meaningless.

ratio_roas.description: attributed_value / spend. A RATIO, not money — 0 when there was no spend.

id.description: Stable only within this response — `ai-1`, `ai-2`, … or `fallback-1` when `used_ai` is false. It becomes durable once published.

reasoning.description: Why the model made these choices, in its own words.

score.description: 0-100. A DETERMINISTIC length-and-shape heuristic computed here, never a model claim and never a performance prediction: it rewards a headline near 40 characters, body copy near 180, and the presence of a call to action.

token_count.description: Approximate token count of the document's raw content.

processing_status.description: `pending`/`processing` while the async chunk+embed pipeline runs after a POST or a content-changing PATCH; `ready` once the document is searchable; `failed` with `processing_error` set if the pipeline errored.

active.description: False once soft-deleted (`DELETE`). Inactive documents are excluded from search.

content_hash.description: sha256 of `content` — how the pipeline detects an unchanged PATCH.

status.description: `reprocessing` when `content` changed and the async chunk+embed pipeline was re-queued; `updated` for a metadata-only change (title/tags/active), applied synchronously.

outcome_value.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

frequency.description: impressions / reach, 0 when the entity had no impressions in the window.

AdDetail.description:
A strict superset of the row `GET /api/v1/campaigns?level=` returns, with the fields the list shape drops: the first-payment metric pair, the creative copy, the video funnel and the messaging funnel.

THE THREE OUTCOME FAMILIES ARE DISTINCT AND DO NOT ADD UP. `outcome_*` is every attributed conversion of any revenue type; `*_first_payment` is the first-payment-only SUBSET of it; `messaging_*` counts conversations, not cash. Adding two of them together produces a number that describes nothing.

spend.description: In the AD ACCOUNT's billing currency.

spend_reporting.description: The same money in the profile's reporting currency, or null when no FX rate applied.

cost_per_click.description: Prefers `spend_reporting`, falling back to `spend`. The two are never mixed inside one figure — that would give a currency-crossing profile a CPC correct in neither.

stage_rule_count.description: The subset of active rules fired by a CRM pipeline-stage transition.

force.description: Scan even when the cached summary is inside the 10-minute idempotency window.

provider.description: The `connection_provider` value — the same string `GET /api/v1/connections` returns as `channel` and the same one stored on the connection. Only these four have a consent-then-pick flow; Google Calendar finalizes inside its own callback.

expires_at.description: When the parked provider token dies (60 minutes from the consent). After this the consent is gone and the connect flow must be started again.

candidate_count.description: How many candidates the OAuth callback counted when it parked the token. `candidates` below is what the provider reports NOW; the two may legitimately differ if an account was added or removed in between, and the list is what you should render.

warning.description: An operator-facing note when the list is degraded — today only GoHighLevel produces one (a location-scoped token that cannot enumerate sub-accounts, or a missing `oauth.readonly` scope, so names may appear as ids). Not an error: the candidates returned alongside it are real and finalizable.

id.description: Pass this back verbatim as `candidate_id`. It is the provider's own identifier and becomes the connection's `external_account_id` — an `act_…` ad account (Meta), a bare customer id (Google Ads), a `sc-domain:` or URL property (Search Console), a location id (GoHighLevel).

name.description: Display label. Falls back to `id` when the provider returns no name.

currency.description: meta_ads / google_ads. ISO-4217.

account_status.description: meta_ads only. Meta's numeric ad-account status (1 = active).

manager.description: google_ads only. True for a manager (MCC) account. Managers are not offered as candidates — their child accounts are listed instead — so this is informational.

login_customer_id.description: google_ads only. The MCC this account is reached through, when it is.

company_id.description: gohighlevel only. The agency this sub-account belongs to.

PendingConnectionCandidate.description: One account/property/location the dealer can pick. One flat shape across all four providers: `id` and `name` are always present, the rest are null for providers that do not have them.

provider.description: The `connection_provider` value — the same string `GET /api/v1/connections` returns as `channel` and the same one stored on the connection. Only these four have a consent-then-pick flow; Google Calendar finalizes inside its own callback.

already_finalized.description: True when this call changed nothing because the same `candidate_id` had already been finalized. Retries are safe and answer 200 either way.

id.description: The connection's Atribu id (uuid).

external_account_id.description: The candidate id that was connected.

currency.description: Meta only, and only when the ad account reports one.

status.description: Connection status: 'connected'|'syncing'|'error'|'disconnected' for every channel. Email connections additionally re-derive 'connected'/'syncing' into 'degraded' when the provider watch/subscription has expired AND no message has been processed in the last 24h, and Stripe connections do the same when disputes are unreadable on this account (missing Connect application permission) while payments and refunds keep syncing normally — see `status_reason` for either case.

status_reason.description: Human-readable reason for a non-nominal `status`. Populated for email connections when the provider watch/subscription has expired and no message has been processed recently (`degraded`), and for Stripe connections when disputes are unreadable on this account for lack of a Connect application permission (`degraded`; payments and refunds are unaffected). `null` when `status` needs no explanation.

display_name.description: Human-readable connection label (WA: phone number; IG: @username; email: mailbox address; calendar: Google account email; everything else: the ad account / store / property / location name the connect recorded).

external_id.description: WA phone_number_id, IG ig_business_account_id, email mailbox address, Google account email, or — for every non-messaging kind — the provider's own account id, which for the picker providers is the value passed to `POST /api/v1/connections/pending/{provider}/finalize` as `candidate_id`.

authorized_at.description: When your app was authorized for THIS connection. Always null for every non-messaging kind (those are not delegated per connection) and for direct admin keys, which hold no authorization row.

created_at.description: When the connection was created — i.e. connected.

kind.description:
Which class this connection belongs to.

`messaging` — WhatsApp / Instagram / email / Google & Microsoft Calendar, delegated to your app one connection at a time, so an OAuth-app key sees only the ones it was authorized for. Every other kind is listed for the key's profile and carries no `authorized_at`.

`ad_platform` — Meta Ads, Google Ads, Search Console. `crm` — GoHighLevel. `commerce` — Shopify. `payments` — Stripe, MercadoPago. `integration` — Notion, ManyChat.

**Changed 2026-08-26:** `gohighlevel` reports `crm`, not `ad_platform`. The four non-messaging kinds beyond `ad_platform` are new in the same release, which is when this list stopped being 'messaging or not' — see the API changelog.

currency.description: The connection's reporting currency (ISO-4217), when the provider reports one — Meta and Google Ads do. Null for every messaging channel, and for any provider whose connect does not record one.

ad_account_timezone.description:
IANA timezone the ad platform aggregates this account's DAILY SPEND in (Meta: the ad account's `timezone_name`).

Spend arrives from the platform already bucketed by day, with no offset in the payload, so a day of spend and a day of Atribu-attributed revenue are not necessarily the same 24 hours when this differs from the profile's timezone. Atribu does not re-bucket spend; this field is what lets a client say so.

Null for every messaging channel, and for any ad connection not reconnected since this field shipped. Null means *unknown* — do not read it as agreement with the profile's timezone.

delivers_spend.description:
Has any ad spend at all ever been recorded for this profile on this connection's platform?

An ad account can be connected, healthy and syncing and still deliver no spend — it was authorized and never used. Such a connection contributes nothing to any spend total, so a surface that names it (a timezone disclosure, a 'where your spend comes from' list) would be describing an account the numbers do not come from.

**Grain is the PLATFORM, not the individual ad account.** `spend` is indexed on `(profile_id, platform, …)` and not on the account id, so the probe behind this field asks whether the profile has spend on this connection's provider. Two connections of the SAME provider on one profile therefore report the same value even if only one of them delivered it — the over-disclosing direction, chosen deliberately.

Null for every kind that cannot report spend (`messaging`, `crm`, `commerce`, `payments`, `integration`) — null is *not applicable*, never *no*. Since #1550 it is ALSO null when `spend_unavailable` is true, which is *unknown*; read that field to tell the two apart.

spend_unavailable.description:
The spend probe behind `delivers_spend` could not run, so that field is null because the answer is UNKNOWN — not because it does not apply.

`spend` is the only table this endpoint reads outside Atribu's messaging core, and it feeds exactly one field. Everything else on this response — the channel, the status, the identity, the sync counters — is unaffected, and is as trustworthy on a request with this flag set as on any other. **A client sweeping channel health must not degrade a connection because of it**; the correct reaction is to re-read `delivers_spend` later and to keep whatever it last knew in the meantime.

Always `false` for a kind that cannot report spend at all, and `false` on every row of a healthy response.

last_synced_at.description: When a sync for this connection last COMPLETED, ISO-8601. `null` means it has never completed one — normal for a channel that is push-driven rather than polled (email, calendar).

last_error.description: The connector's own failure text from the last run, and the only explanation a `status: "error"` connection carries. Distinct from `status_reason`, which is the derived, email-only sentence about a stale provider watch.

started_at.description: When the current (or last) sync run started, ISO-8601.

heartbeat_at.description: Last progress tick of the current run, ISO-8601. A `status: "syncing"` connection whose heartbeat is far in the past is stalled, not busy.

total_jobs.description: Jobs in the current or last run. `0` when none has run.

eta_seconds.description: The worker's estimate of seconds remaining on the in-flight run.

current_task.description: What the in-flight run is doing right now, e.g. the resource being paged.

ConnectionSync.description: State of the last (or in-flight) sync run for this connection. Always present on both kinds; every field reflects what the connector last recorded.

id.description: The Meta pixel / dataset id. This is the value `meta_pixel_id` takes on `POST /api/v1/exports/destinations` — the reason this endpoint exists.

name.description: The pixel's name in Events Manager. `null` when Meta returned none.

created_at.description: When the pixel was created, in Meta's own ISO-8601 spelling (offset, not `Z`). `null` when Meta did not return it.

last_fired_at.description: When this pixel last received an event, in Meta's own ISO-8601 spelling. `null` means Meta returned no value — typically a pixel that has NEVER fired, which is the signal that matters when choosing between several.

is_unavailable.description: `true` when Meta reports the pixel as unavailable (disabled or otherwise unusable). `null` is NOT `false`: it means Meta returned no verdict, so treat it as unknown rather than as healthy.

owner_business.description: The Business Manager that owns the pixel, when Meta discloses it. `null` when it did not — commonly because Atribu's token holds no `business_management` on that business, which is normal for a shared asset and is not an error. A pixel owned by a business other than the ad account's own is readable here but may still refuse server events.

revoked_keys.description: How many active API keys the revocation cut. `0` is a normal answer: the authorization was already revoked, or it belongs to a newer key generation than the one calling. The count can also exceed the keys minted under this one authorization — when it was your app's last live authorization on the profile, older key generations that no authorization names are cut with it.

outcome_event_id.description: The payment's `outcome_events.id`. Pass this back as the override's `outcome_event_id`. Same spelling `GET /api/v1/attribution/explore` uses.

value_amount_original.description: The amount as charged, in `currency` — pre-FX, not the reporting currency.

currency.description: ISO-4217 of `value_amount_original`.

external_source.description: Where the payment was ingested from (`stripe`, `mercadopago`, `fintoc` — a bank transfer read off a linked account — `gohighlevel`, `manual`, …), or `unknown`.

is_first_payment.description: The EFFECTIVE flag, after any override — what LTV cohorts, the first-payment-vs-recurring revenue split and the CAC denominator use.

manual_override.description: The operator's stored decision, or `null` for none. `null` is NOT `false`: `false` means someone said this is not a first payment, `null` means nobody has said anything and `is_first_payment` is derived (earliest payment, plus a 7-day grace window and same-invoice grouping).
The override now stored — echoes the request.

changed.description: False when this call wrote nothing because the payment already carried the same override. Retries are safe and answer 200 either way.

status.description: `superseded` means a later scan replaced this proposal with a better one; it is never returned for a decision you made.

allOf.description: The customer that would be merged away — its events move to the survivor.

revenue_survivor_cents.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

revenue_merged_cents.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

MergeProposalEvidence.description:
The counting evidence stored when the proposal was raised — what was true THEN, not now (use the preview for that).

`events_*` count `public.touches`, not raw events: the source moved off the 30-day ephemeral event buffer so the number stops collapsing as events age out. The KEYS keep their old names because they are read back out of a stored JSON column — renaming them would make every proposal raised before the change read as zero.

id.description: `customer_profiles.id`.

identifier_sources.description: The DISTINCT `id_type` values this customer carries (`email`, `phone`, `ghl_contact_id`, `anonymous_id`, …), sorted. Where the identity came from; the values themselves are never included.

MergeProposalCandidate.description: The customer that would REMAIN. Override it when deciding, if the other is better.

cash_revenue.description: Sum of the merged side's CASH conversion value, in the reporting currency.

lead_coalesce.description: True when BOTH customers carry a `lead_created` — the merge collapses two leads into one, so the profile's lead count drops by one.

email_collision.description: Both sides have a primary email and they differ. The survivor's wins.

status.description: The proposal's status AFTER this call — the one it already held when `changed` is false.

changed.description: False when the proposal was already decided and this call wrote nothing. Retries are safe and answer 200 either way.

recompute_enqueued.description: Whether an attribution recompute was enqueued. True only for a `merge` that actually merged — nothing else here moves attribution credit.

auto_repairable_count.description: Backfills the auto pass would apply. Merges are NOT counted here.

auto_merge_count.description: Profiles with an unambiguous merge partner. Reported, not actionable here — merges go through the proposal queue, not the bulk repair.

profile_id.description: `customer_profiles.id` — the CUSTOMER, not the Atribu profile. Named this way by the underlying scan and kept verbatim rather than renamed in one of three places.

suggested_email.description: What a backfill would write — recovered from identifiers or CRM raw data.

social_only_identifiers.description: Non-empty only for a "ghost": no email AND no phone, reachable only through a messaging surface (`instagram`, `manychat`, `whatsapp`).

profile_id.description: The customer being CHANGED — for a merge, the one merged away.

will_apply.description: False when the operation is a no-op or no longer valid; `reason` says which.

IdentityRepairApply.description: A partial success is the NORMAL outcome, not an error: an operation whose precondition moved since the preview lands in `skipped` with the reason, and the rest still apply. That is what makes the whole call safe to retry.

IdentityRepairOperation.description: One repair. There is NO actor field: the merge audit row records who did it, and that comes from the authenticated principal (a session's user, or null for an API key). Accepting it in the body would let any caller write any user's id into the audit log.

audit_log_id.description: Identifies the MERGE, not the customer. It is what an undo is keyed on.

merged_by_user_id.description: Who merged, or null for an automated repair.

is_currently_merged.description: False once the merge was undone. The row stays as the audit record.

merged_profile_id.description: The customer that has been restored as a separate person.

unmerge_audit_log_id.description: The audit row the UNDO itself wrote. The original merge's row stays as the record.

lead_restored.description: True when the merged customer's `lead_created` event was put back — the mirror of `lead_coalesce` on the preview.

recompute_enqueued.description: Whether the re-attribution this undo requires reached the queue. False is reported, never fatal: the unmerge has already committed and the hourly staleness sweep will pick it up.

provider.description: null for a product not synced from a store.

active.description: `false` for a product the store deactivated or deleted. Deactivated products ARE returned: a mirror has to learn about the removal, and omitting them makes a deleted product indistinguishable from one that simply stopped changing.

updated_at.description: When Atribu last wrote this row — the `updated_since` clock and the first half of the keyset cursor. Not the store's own timestamp; see `external_updated_at`.

variant_id.description: Atribu's own id, stable across syncs.

price.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

currency.description: ISO-4217. `null` on rows synced before the catalogue sync began capturing the shop's currency — reported as unknown rather than defaulted, because a price with the wrong unit is worse than a price with none.

inventory_quantity.description: Units available across every location; null when untracked.

inventory_state.description: The stock band Atribu derives. `low_stock` is Atribu's threshold (5 or fewer available), not something the store reports; `discontinued` means the product left ACTIVE status or was deleted. `null` means the band is unknown — which is what an UNTRACKED item is, and is not the same as `in_stock`.

inventory_policy.description: The store's oversell policy, verbatim (Shopify: DENY/CONTINUE).

updated_at.description: When Atribu last wrote this row.

order_ref.description: The number the shopper sees on their confirmation, where the store sent one. Frequently null — it reaches Atribu on the order-created webhook and never on a bulk re-sync.

status.description: Atribu's single answer to 'where is my order'. Coarser than the store's own two status fields, which are carried alongside unmodified. `delivered` outranks `fulfilled`: a store leaves `fulfillment_status` at `fulfilled` after delivery.

value_amount.description: The captured total where there is one, else the ordered total.

external_user_id.description: The phone number (WhatsApp), IGSID (Instagram) or Gmail thread id (email).

linked_customer_is_payer.description: True when the linked customer is a real payer — has an email/phone or a cash conversion — as opposed to a thin DM-only profile.

enrichment_unavailable.description:
#1550 — Atribu's analytics store could not be read for this page, so the three fields it feeds hold their absent-evidence value rather than a measurement: `ad_name` and `campaign_name` are null, and `linked_customer_is_payer` was decided on the contact's own email/phone alone, without consulting cash conversions.

Everything else on the row — the conversation, its counts, its last message, its contact and every `referral_*` field — comes from Atribu's messaging core and is unaffected. `false` on every row of a healthy response.

is_inferred_source.description: True when Stage 5c inferred this ad as the conversation's likely source (`attribution_mode = native_conversation_model`). Decision-support only, never a deterministic claim.

amount.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

id.description: The `handoff_id` the minting call returned. Not the handle the URL carries — that is the human's capability, this is the agent's.

kind.description: What the human is being asked to do. `connect` an OAuth consent, `pick` a choice among the assets a consent exposed, `sign_dpa` a Data Processing Addendum, `checkout` a plan payment, `approve` a consequential write you asked to make.

status.description: `pending` until the human finishes, then terminal. `expired` is DERIVED at read time from `expires_at` — polling an expired hand-off answers 200 with this status, never 404, so you can tell 'mint a fresh one' from 'wrong id'.

url.description: The URL to hand to the human. Present ONLY while `status` is `pending`; null once the hand-off is terminal, because a spent capability is not handed back out. The page is session-less — whoever holds this link can complete it, signed in or not, on a phone.

expires_at.description: When the URL stops working. 45 minutes from the mint unless the kind says otherwise — the same budget Atribu's consumer connect detour ships against.

completed_at.description: When the hand-off settled, in any terminal status. Null while pending.

result.description: Kind-specific output, written when the hand-off settles. Carries `completed_by` (the Atribu user id) when a signed-in person finished it, and null there when an anonymous link holder did. Null while pending.

PendingAction.description: One hand-off: a step of the golden path only a human can take. Mint it through the route for its kind, hand `url` over, poll this endpoint until `status` is no longer `pending`, then continue.

document.description: Which agreement was accepted. `dpa` writes only the DPA columns; `baa` is the combined DPA & BAA click-wrap that Healthcare Mode requires and writes both.

document_version.description: The version stamp actually recorded — one of the shipped texts, never the raw string a caller sent.

already_accepted.description: True when this document was ALREADY accepted and nothing was written — the call is idempotent at the document grain, so a reload never collects a second signature and never moves the original timestamp.

document_version.description: Which shipped text you displayed. Allowlisted — an unknown value is a 422. Omit to accept the document's current version.

plan.description: The plan to buy. Free has nothing to sell and Enterprise is negotiated, so neither is accepted here — `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/subscription`'s `upgrade_available` lists exactly what this workspace can be sold.

interval.description: Billing cadence. Defaults to `monthly` — an agent asking for "the Growth plan" has expressed a complete intent, and requiring a cadence would turn a one-argument hand-off into a two-argument one for no gain.

webhook_url.description: The URL the merchant pastes into Shopify admin → Settings → Notifications → Webhooks. It carries the connection's inbound token, which routes the delivery; the delivery is only TRUSTED after its HMAC verifies against the signing ID below.

topics.description: The webhook topics to create. Deliberately narrower than the App Store install's set: every other topic needs the Admin API, which a manual connection has no token for, so advertising them would ask the merchant to queue work that can only fail.

state.description:
`pending` — created, no verified delivery has ever arrived. `connected` — a delivery verified inside the staleness window. `stale` — deliveries arrived once and stopped, which is the ONLY signal available: Shopify deletes a failing admin-created webhook and emails the store owner, not us.

Derived from `last_delivery_at`, never stored — `connection_status` has no such members.

last_processing_error_at.description: A delivery that verified and then threw while being processed. This route answers 200 to those (a 5xx would walk Shopify toward deleting the subscription), so without this field the dropped order is invisible in both directions.

signing_id_configured.description: Whether a signing ID has been stored. **The value is never returned.** It lives inside the sealed credentials envelope and leaves this API in no response, on any route — set it with the PATCH below, and if it is lost, set a new one.

shop_domain.description: The store handle, `<handle>.myshopify.com`, or a pasted admin URL — all three normalise. A custom storefront domain is REFUSED: Shopify always sends the `.myshopify.com` form on `X-Shopify-Shop-Domain`, so a stored custom domain could never be cross-checked against a delivery.

plan.description: `free` provisions the $0 tier here. `growth`/`agency` both hand back the same Shopify plan page — see above.

profile_id.description: Where to land the merchant after a `free` selection. A BODY field rather than the request's scope: this route reads and writes the WORKSPACE, and the profile only names a destination.

value.description: Normalised: lowercased, with a leading `@` or `#` stripped.

media_count.description:
Distinct media captured on this source's most recent snapshot day.

**`null` is not zero.** The count is a paged read of a snapshot-shaped table; when it cannot be assembled the field is `null` so a stalled sync is distinguishable from a handle that has never returned a post. Rendering it as `0` is exactly the bug #748 fixed.

id.description: `instagram_accounts.id` — the BINDING, not the Instagram account itself.

provider_subtype.description: `fb_login` (through a Facebook Page) or `ig_login` (Instagram Business Login). They differ in which id sends a DM and which scopes the grant carries.

comment_to_dm_paused_until.description: Set while the comment-to-DM circuit breaker is tripped. Clear it with `POST /api/v1/instagram/accounts/{account_id}/resume-comment-to-dm`.

is_automation_owner.description: One IG account can be connected from several workspaces; exactly one binding runs its automations. Disconnecting the owner promotes a surviving binding.

connection_status.description: From `data_connections`; `unknown` when that row could not be read.

post_id_allowlist.description: Media ids this trigger is restricted to; `null` means every post.

opening_message.description: The DM sent when the trigger fires.

public_comment_reply.description: Optional public reply left on the comment itself.

exact_dm_ad_count.description: Attributed to an ad by an exact DM referral — deterministic.

exact_follow_proxy_count.description: Attributed through a Follow Proxy click — deterministic.

avg_modeled_confidence.description: Mean 0–1 confidence of the MODELED credit; null when nothing was modeled.

mapped_in_manychat.description: False means this ad's conversations cannot be attributed deterministically — it is what makes the list actionable.

expected_followers.description: The SUM of per-event probabilities, not a count — a fractional value is correct.

evidence.description: The extractor's raw evidence blob — opaque, for display only.

widget_token.description: One-shot token for Fintoc's own widget.

stage_mapping_provider.description: `gemini` when the AI-assisted pass ran and returned at least one mapping, `rules` otherwise (AI unconfigured, the workspace's daily allowance is spent, or the model call failed — every case degrades to the rule-based suggestions, never an error).

stage_mapping_model.description: The model id that produced the AI-assisted mappings, or null on `rules`.

gemini_mappings_applied.description: How many stages took the AI suggestion over the rule-based one.

spend.description: Ad spend in the window. `null`, never `"0"`, exactly when `spend_available` is `false` — a measured zero still arrives as `"0"`. Read `spend_available` for WHY it is null.

spend_available.description: `false` when spend could not be scoped to the requested `filter[…]` set — either because a geo/device/browser/os dimension is not resolvable from an ad touch, or because the matching touches carry no ad ids at all. `spend`, `roas` and `clicks` are then `null`; this flag is the reason behind those nulls, not a substitute for reading them.

clicks.description: Ad clicks — the head of the conversion path. `null`, never `0`, exactly when `spend_available` is `false`.

revenue.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

organic_direct_revenue.description: Exact decimal string (ADR 0018). Unrounded, no thousands separator, no currency symbol — the currency is a separate field. Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

roas.description: Attributed revenue / spend. `null`, never `0`, exactly when `spend_available` is `false`. CAC, MER and NMER are not published — derive them from `spend` and the denominators here, and they inherit the null.

attributed_cash_outcomes.description: Attributed CASH outcomes only. NOT the CAC denominator — CAC is total spend / `first_payment_customers` (new customers, attributed or not). Divide spend by THIS and you get cost per ad-attributed cash payment, which on a low-coverage profile differs from CAC by two orders of magnitude.

event_id.description: The idempotency key this event is filed under.

outcome_event_id.description: The stored outcome event. The same id on every retry of the same key.

action.description: What the write did: `inserted` on the first delivery, `updated` on a retry, `enriched`/`skipped_lead_exists` on the one-lead-per-customer path.

customer_profile_id.description: The identity the sale was filed under, when one resolved. NULL is normal for an anon-only sale — it stays joinable by `anonymous_id`.

matched.description: Whether a conversion goal on this profile lists `event_name` in its `source_event_names`. FALSE means the event was stored but will never become a conversion and will never be attributed — fix the event name, or create the goal via `POST /api/v1/goals`.

event_name.description: The outcome type. Use `payment_received` for a closed sale where money changed hands (revenue_type `cash`, the only kind that counts toward ROAS) and `closed_won` for a won-but-unpaid deal (revenue_type `pipeline`). Any other name is accepted, but unless a conversion goal lists it in `source_event_names` the event becomes no conversion at all — check `conversion.matched` in the response.

anonymous_id.description: The Atribu tracker's visitor id (`atribu_visitor_id` cookie / `atribu_anon_id`), when your checkout captured it. The most direct sale↔click link there is: it needs no email match.

session_id.description: The tracker's session id, when captured. Links the sale to one specific visit.

timestamp.description: When the sale closed (ISO-8601). Defaults to now. Send the ERP's own timestamp: it must be stable across retries, and it is what the attribution window is measured against.

properties.description: Free-form payload, stored verbatim on the outcome event. `value` (or `amount`) and `currency` are read out of it: `value` is the sale amount as a number or numeric string, `currency` an ISO-4217 code (defaults to USD). A `value` that is present but unparseable is a 400, never a silent zero.

campaign.description: For Meta, the campaign's numeric platform id.

content.description: For Meta, the AD's numeric platform id.

term.description: For Meta, the AD SET's numeric platform id.

utm.description: The marketing parameters the buyer arrived with, if your ERP recorded them. Used to build a synthetic touch for a sale that never had a web session.

click_ids.description: Ad-platform click ids captured at the landing page. `fbclid`, `gclid`, `msclkid` and `ttclid` are joined against the click index to recover the originating session for up to 90 days; any other kind is stored for later.

idempotency_key.description: The sale's own deal/order id. Retries with the same key land on the same outcome event — `external_id` is `api:<key>`. REQUIRED whenever `properties.value` is set: without it the key defaults to a fresh UUID, so a retried sale would be counted twice, and double-counted cash cannot be undone from the data. Also accepted as the `Idempotency-Key` header.

IngestEventBody.description: A server-side outcome event. The worked example is the sale-closed case: a dealer's ERP reporting a paid sale with the identity signals needed to join it back to the ad click.

email.description: Buyer email. Normalised and resolved through the identity graph, which is how an off-site sale reaches the ad click captured on the website.

phone.description: Buyer phone. Normalised to E.164 when parseable.

external_id.description: YOUR customer id (the ERP/CRM primary key), stored as an `external_customer_id` identifier so repeat sales from the same buyer converge on one customer profile. On its own it is used for a READ-ONLY lookup: an identifier with no email or phone never creates a profile, because a profile minted from a foreign key alone can never be merged with the real one later.

national_id.description: A government identity document number (e.g. a Chilean RUT) — the phone↔RUT↔email bridge a clinic's own practice-management software already holds. Normalised and stored as a `national_id` identifier, the same type MercadoPago's own `payer.identification` writes, so it is used as a match key alongside email and phone: unlike `external_id`, a `national_id` with no email or phone still creates a profile. An SII **generic receptor** RUT — `66.666.666-6` (boleta de ventas y servicios), `55.555.555-5` (export / Factura Especial Turista) or `44.444.446-0` (boleta de honorarios to a foreigner) — is IGNORED: those are the values a document carries when the issuer did not record who the customer is, they all pass the mod-11 check, and storing one would merge every anonymous customer of a profile onto a single non-person.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 hint for parsing `national_id`. Defaults to `CL` — the only country national_id parsing understands today.

IngestEventUserTraits.description: Identity signals. At least one of these — or `anonymous_id`, or a click id — is what makes the sale attributable; a sale with none of them is recorded but can never be joined to an ad.

results.description: One entry per request row, in the SAME order — degrade visibly, never drop.

index.description: The row's position in the request's `rows` array.

reason.description: Present only on a `rejected` row — why it was rejected.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 hint for the WHOLE batch's `national_id` (and phone) parsing — one CSV is one clinic, one country. Defaults to `CL`.

CustomerImportBody.description: A batch of customer identities from the clinic's own records — a PMS export or a spreadsheet, not an event.

national_id.description: A government identity document number (e.g. a Chilean RUT). Normalised exactly like `user_traits.national_id` on POST /api/v1/events, SII generic receptor RUTs included — a row whose only identity is one of those is REJECTED with a reason naming it, never silently imported.

external_id.description: YOUR customer id (PMS/CRM primary key). Never enough on its own — a row with no phone, email or national_id is REJECTED, because a profile minted from a foreign key alone can never be merged with the real one later.

attribution_carrier.description: Which field the visitor identity was recovered from. NULL means the passthrough carried nothing and the sale falls back to an email/phone match — check that your `Transaction.create()` really sent `getAttributionRef()` as `session_id`.

anonymous_id.description: The visitor the sale was tied to, decoded from the carrier.

forwarded.description: true when the read receipt (plus the typing indicator, unless `indicator: "read"`) reached Meta. false when Meta refused the `message_id` (stale / already-read / re-registered number) — a knowing no-op, still a 200.

indicator.description: The mode that was applied, echoed back. Absent means the deployment predates this field and therefore behaved as `typing` — the only way to detect that a requested `read` silently showed a bubble.

reason.description: Present only when `forwarded` is false. `stale_message_id` — Meta refused the wamid. `message_id_conversation_mismatch` — the wamid belongs to a different conversation than `to`, so it was never forwarded.

expires_at.description: ISO timestamp at which `url` stops working.

status.description: DRAFT | PUBLISHED | DEPRECATED | BLOCKED | THROTTLED (Meta-owned enum).

categories.description: Typed loosely on reads — Meta may add categories.

validation_errors.description: Meta's flow.json validation findings, forwarded verbatim. Empty when valid.

preview.description: Web preview URL for the flow (renders in a browser).

download_url.description: Time-limited URL to download the asset bytes.

canSend.description: Meta's overall `can_send_message`, or null when `health_status` could not be read. null means unknown, never healthy.

refreshedAt.description: When this snapshot was last read from Meta (ISO). null on a never-refreshed account.

stale.description: True when this snapshot was NOT confirmed against Meta just now — either it is older than the 6h TTL and a revalidation was throttled, or a revalidation ran and its live read failed, so these are last-good values. Treat it as "the last thing we knew", never as a verification. A successful live/forced refresh returns false.

reconnectRequired.description: True when the channel needs re-authorization (invalid/expired token).

reconnectUrl.description: Where to send the user to reconnect the WhatsApp channel, or null when not required.

entityType.description: Meta entity_type (PHONE_NUMBER, MESSAGE_TEMPLATE, WABA, BUSINESS, APP) or a synthetic bucket (APP) for token/webhook issues.

code.description: Meta error_code (number), a synthetic string code, or null for advisories.

remediation.description: Meta's `possible_solution`, or Atribu's remediation for synthetic issues.

WhatsAppCallingSettings.description: Meta's `calling` object, passed through verbatim in both directions. Atribu holds no opinion about its contents — the SIP peer, the SRTP key exchange and the codec list are the caller's recipe. Documented as free-form on purpose: a schema enumerating Meta's fields would reject a field Meta shipped this morning.

sip_user_password.description: Meta-generated digest password for this SIP peer.

media_url.description: Short-lived CDN URL, or null when Meta omits it. A CAROUSEL_ALBUM parent may carry its own cover URL or not — read `children` for the per-item URLs rather than relying on the parent.

children.description: Ordered carousel items; null for non-carousel media.

id.description: Conversation id — pass to the messages endpoint.

updated_time.description: When the last message was added. This is a LAST-ACTIVITY stamp: Meta exposes no conversation-creation time, so it cannot tell you how far back a thread goes.

id.description: IGSID of the participant (or the account's own id).

message.description: Text body, or null when Meta withheld it — the documented outcome for any message past the 20 most recent in the thread. The id and created_time still identify the message.

is_unsupported.description: Meta returns this only when true.

InstagramMessageAttachment.description: Meta returns only a URL for shared media — a shared post or reel does not come back as a re-hostable asset.

merchant_label.description: Which Merchant this app was made available to — the Shopify API Terms §2.3.20 audit trail.

plus_org_id.description: Non-null asserts every bound store belongs to ONE Shopify Plus organization, which is the only case §2.3.20 permits a Custom Application to serve more than one store.

attribution_deferred.description:
#1550 — the join was ACCEPTED and recorded in Atribu's messaging core, but the outcome event that carries it into attribution could not be written yet because Atribu's analytics store did not answer. The work is parked durably and replayed automatically, on the same key the outcome row uses, so nothing is duplicated and nothing is lost.

`conversation_started` is then `false` and `outcome_event_id` is `null` whatever the replay eventually produces: this response says what Atribu knew at the time. **Do not retry on it** — a retry re-parks the same row and buys nothing. Every other field is fully resolved: the join tiers read the messaging core, which is the project that answered this request.

`false` on every response from a healthy Atribu.

get.description:

A funnel made only of `outcome_event` steps reads durable `outcome_events` and is unbounded (subject to the general 366-day cap).

get.summary: Explain one conversion's messaging attribution
get.description:
Every candidate ad the messaging/DM attribution model considered for ONE conversion, with the probability and confidence band it assigned, ordered highest-probability first. This is the drill behind a row of `GET /api/v1/attribution/messaging`.

`probability` is MODELLED credit, not cash, and is never folded into ROAS.

Requires `customers:read`: the whole response describes one person's conversion, and `evidence` can carry the text of their messages. A conversion belonging to another profile answers **404**, not 403 and not an empty chain — a foreign id and a nonexistent one are the same fact to a caller, and separating them would let one enumerate conversion ids.
