Expected followers per ad with a confidence band, plus the window's total follow events.

The caveat is served with the data rather than left to a UI to remember.

get.description:
The queue of proposed matches between an Instagram DM sender and a customer profile, each carrying the evidence (username, and the email or phone extracted from the thread).

post.description:
Approving STITCHES the DM's identity onto the customer profile — it merges identities and is what unlocks modeled attribution from a DM conversation to a payment. Rejecting closes the review and leaves both identities alone.

The review's ownership is re-checked against your profile before the merge runs: the underlying routine keys only on the review id, so the scope gate alone would not be enough.

Counts are within one flush window of live (the writer batches, at most 5 seconds or 200 requests behind). The 4xx/5xx SHARE is unaffected by that lag — a delayed batch delays successes and errors alike.

Rows older than 90 days are pruned, so a window reaching further back returns only what is still retained.

get.summary: List the profile's click-to-WhatsApp ads
get.description:
Every click-to-WhatsApp ad on this profile: which ones open WhatsApp, the number and Page they open, the call-to-action they carry, and the greeting ("Saludo automático") each shows the customer BEFORE they type anything.

An ad is listed when WhatsApp is named either by its ad set's `destination_type` or by its creative's call-to-action — the two are set in different places by different people and an ad commonly carries only one of them.

SCOPING: the credential is the tenant selection, exactly as on `GET /api/v1/partner/whatsapp/ads/{ad_id}/welcome-message` and `POST /api/v1/partner/wa-joins`. There is no `profile_id` parameter — every Atribu key is profile-scoped, so a multi-tenant consumer sends the per-connection token carrying the right profile rather than one global key.

NO LIVE META CALL. This is served from what Atribu's nightly structure sync already read, so refreshing a screen costs the advertiser's `ads_management` quota nothing. `last_synced_at` on each row says how stale that is; an ad launched since the last sync is not listed yet, and its greeting is still readable by id on the welcome-message route.

NO SPEND, NO METRICS, NO PII. Everything here is the advertiser's own configuration — the greeting every person who taps the ad is shown, the business's own WhatsApp number, the campaign's name. Performance data stays behind `campaigns:read` on the ads routes that serve it.

PAGINATION is keyset on `ad_id`: pass `pagination.cursor` back as `after`. A row written by the sync mid-walk cannot shift the window, which an offset would allow.

Scope: `whatsapp` OR `campaigns:read`.

get.summary: Read a click-to-WhatsApp ad's welcome message
get.description:
The welcome message ("Saludo automático") configured on a click-to-WhatsApp ad: the greeting the customer was ALREADY shown under the business's name before they sent their first message, plus the pre-filled text or the ice-breaker buttons they most likely tapped instead of typing.

Meta never delivers this over the Cloud API webhook. The `referral` object on the customer's first inbound message carries the ad's headline, body and thumbnail — the greeting is ad CONFIGURATION and is readable only from the Marketing API. Without it, an assistant composing the first reply greets a customer who has already been greeted, and asks what it can help with after they have already said.

SCOPING: the credential is the tenant selection, exactly as on `POST /api/v1/partner/wa-joins`. There is no `profile_id` parameter — every Atribu key is profile-scoped, and a multi-tenant consumer must send the per-connection token carrying the right profile rather than one global key. `connection_id` is optional and only NARROWS: it must name a `meta_ads` connection on that same profile.

CACHED per (profile, ad): 24h for an ad Meta answered for, 1h for one it refuses. `cached` says which, and `fetched_at` is when the answer was read from Meta — not when the request ran.

An ad with NO greeting configured answers `200` with `welcome: null`. That is a complete answer, cached for the full 24h, and distinct from every failure below.

Scope: `whatsapp` OR `campaigns:read`.

get.summary: Get dashboard overview
get.description:
Spend, clicks, attributed revenue, ROAS, outcome counts and the cash /
first-payment / recurring / refund / dispute legs for a window, alongside the
immediately-preceding window of equal length.

`grain` selects ONE of two response shapes — they never appear together:

- `grain=total` (the default) — `data.current` and `data.previous`, each one
  aggregate row.
- `grain=day` — `data.days` and `data.previous_days`, one row per calendar day
  with the same legs plus a `date`. Days are zero-filled, so a day with no
  activity is present and reads `0`.

`first_payment_customers` and `recurring_customers` are `count(DISTINCT)`:
summing them across `grain=day` rows does NOT reproduce the `grain=total`
number, because one customer can appear on several days. Use `grain=total`
for a CAC denominator.

`spend`, `roas` and `clicks` are `null` — never `"0"` / `0` — when the engine
could not scope spend to the requested filter; `spend_available` says so and is
the reason WHY. A measured zero spend still arrives as `"0"` with
`spend_available: true`, and the two are different facts.

`filter[<dimension>]=<operator>:<value>`, e.g. `filter[channel]=is:Paid Social` — the
same parser `/campaigns`, `/breakdown` and `/drill` accept (#628). Operators: `is`,
`is_not`, `contains`, `not_contains`. A malformed entry is silently skipped rather than
rejected; a dimension the engine cannot scope spend by makes `spend`/`spend_available`
answer honestly rather than 400ing (see `spend_available`'s own description).

Scope: `analytics:read`.

schema.description: `total` (default) returns `current`/`previous`; `day` returns `days`/`previous_days`. Any other value is a 400.

parameters.description: `total` (default) returns `current`/`previous`; `day` returns `days`/`previous_days`. Any other value is a 400.

get.summary: Break conversions and revenue down by any set of dimensions
get.description:
One breakdown for any SET of dimensions, replacing the seven fixed
single-dimension routes (`/channels`, `/pages`, `/countries`, `/devices`,
`/browsers`, `/os`, `/referrers`). A single-dimension request returns the
same numbers as the fixed route it replaces.

`data` is keyed by the dimension token you asked for, so `?dimensions=channel,country`
returns `{ "channel": [...], "country": [...] }`. Every requested dimension gets a
key even when it has no rows — an empty array means "asked, and there was nothing".

`limit` applies PER DIMENSION: `?dimensions=channel,country&limit=5` returns up to five
channels and up to five countries, each ranked by attributed revenue.

Dimensions: `browser`, `campaign`, `channel`, `city`, `country`, `device`, `entry_page`, `medium`, `os`, `page`, `referrer`, `region`, `source`. `page` is an alias for
`entry_page` (it is the LANDING page — Atribu does not measure pageviews).

Filter-only: `goal`. `goal` scopes a
breakdown via `filter[goal]=is:payment_received` but is not itself a pivot —
the engine groups by attributed-touch dimensions, and a conversion type is not
one. Passing it in `dimensions` is a 400 rather than an empty bucket.

Counts every revenue type, not just cash — the same choice the fixed routes make.

`filter[<dimension>]=<operator>:<value>` (#625), e.g. `filter[channel]=is:Paid Social` — the
same parser `/campaigns`, `/overview` and `/quality/attribution` accept. Operators: `is`,
`is_not`, `contains`, `not_contains`.

Scope: `analytics:read`.

get.summary: Get campaign performance
get.description:
TWO response shapes on one path, picked by whether `level` is present (#627) —

- no `level` (the default) — `data` is `CampaignDTO[]`: a ranked top-N (honours `limit`).
- `level=campaign|ad_set|ad` — `data` is `AdsRankingDTO[]`: every entity at that level, no limit, `filter[…]`-aware. Its rows publish `platform_id` (the provider's own id) alongside `entity_id` (the internal uuid) — use `platform_id` for a deep link back into the ads surface.

**Filters** apply only when `level` is set — the default top-N shape ignores them. `filter[<dimension>]=<operator>:<value>`, e.g. `filter[channel]=is:Paid Social` — the same parser `/breakdown` and `/drill` accept. Operators: `is`, `is_not`, `contains`, `not_contains`. A malformed entry is silently skipped rather than rejected; a dimension the engine cannot scope spend by returns an empty result set rather than 400ing.

A malformed entry (missing colon, empty value) is silently skipped rather than rejected, and the dimension is not otherwise validated.

get.summary: Get a campaign's attributed conversions (drill-down)
get.description: The conversions attributed to one campaign under the given model — the drill-down behind the campaign rollup at GET /api/v1/campaigns. `{id}` is the campaign's EXTERNAL (platform) id, the same value GET /api/v1/campaigns returns as `campaign_external_id` on each row — not `campaign_id` on that same resource, which is an internal identifier. Each row carries the credited share (credited_weight/credited_value), the touch's position within the full path (touch_count/path_length), and whether the credit is `is_inherited` (bridged lead→cash, never counted in ROAS). `customer_name`/`customer_email` are null unless the key also holds `customers:read`; every other field is visible under `campaigns:read` alone. The campaign's unattributed bucket has no external id and is not drillable — it returns an empty list.

get.summary: Get the profile's top-performing ads (cohort-normalized creative scoring)
get.description: Best ads scored against *comparable* creative (a cohort = channel × format × objective × audience warmth × geo × placement): cohort-normalized, empirical-Bayes-smoothed (small-sample ads shrink toward the cohort mean), and maturity-staged. Each ad carries THREE distinct measures — present them separately, never merge: `composite_score` (0–100, a transparent rule blend), `top_performer_likelihood` (0–1, a probability — a *likelihood, not a guarantee*; the calibrated ML-ranker output when `score_source='model'` with `model_version` set, else a monotone function of `composite_score`; never ROAS), and `attributed_revenue`/`roas` (real cash attribution, present when `truth_grade='attributed'`). `maturity_stage` (cold→early→mature→calibrated) says how settled the score is; `reason_codes` explain which funnel layer is strong/weak with a sample-confidence band. Scores refresh on a daily cadence. `window` is a rolling lookback (`7d`/`14d`/`28d`/`lifetime`), not a custom date range. The workspace-wide cross-profile view is exposed via the Atribu MCP server's `top_workspace_performers` tool.

sample_n.description: Cohort ads the percentile was ranked against. A percentile without its sample is a rank presented as a fact; `sample_confidence` is the band derived from this number.

day_from.description: First day of DELIVERY inside the window — not the window's nominal start. An ad that ran six days of a 28d window says so here; dividing by 28 instead of by `metrics.delivery.days_active` is wrong about every per-day number drawn from it.

attribution_model_used.description: The model the `attributed_*` legs were credited under. Rows scored under different models are not comparable.

days_active.description: Days in the window with non-zero delivery — the denominator for any per-day rate.

spend_reporting.description: Spend in the PROFILE's reporting currency; the top-level `spend` is the ad account's own. They differ whenever an account bills in a currency the profile does not report in, and only this one is meaningful to sum across profiles.

video.description: Every rate is NULL — never 0 — for an ad with no video. 'No plays to measure' and 'nobody held past three seconds' are opposite findings.

messaging_total_connections.description: Distinct people reached on the messaging surface — the rates' denominator.

block_rate.description: Share of connections that blocked. The one rate here that is bad when it is high.

messaging.description: Conversation DEPTH, which is the messaging funnel's point: a conversation that starts and dies is not an outcome.

outcome_value_first_payment.description: The FIRST-PAYMENT subset of `attributed_revenue`, not an addition to it. `roas_first_payment` is the acquisition ROAS a subscription business budgets against.

top_performer_likelihood_calibrated.description: The ML ranker's CALIBRATED probability — non-null only when a model actually scored this row (`score_source = 'model'`). The top-level `top_performer_likelihood` falls back to a monotone squash of `composite_score` when it did not, so this is how a consumer tells 'a model said 0.71' from 'the rule blend implies 0.71'.

has_vision_analysis.description: The honesty flag on this whole group. False means the fields were derived from COPY alone, so an absent `camera_shot` is 'not looked at', not 'no camera movement'.

creative_signature.description: Stable hash of the creative's structural features. Equal signatures mean the same creative — how a duplicate is spotted across profiles.

internals.description: UNSTABLE — NOT PART OF THE PUBLIC CONTRACT. Present only when `include=internals` is requested by a session credential (Atribu's own console); absent otherwise, and the parameter is ignored for any other credential. The shape belongs to the scoring engine and may change or disappear in any release without a version bump. Do not build against it.

get.description: Which structural creative patterns (archetype cluster, narrative arc, dominant-third role combo, role presence signature, social-proof duration bucket, hook×claim×cta) win MORE than the workspace baseline. One row per (pattern_dim, pattern_value) with sample_n, winner_n, win_rate, workspace_baseline_win_rate, lift_vs_workspace, Wilson 95% CI bounds, and the top-5 exemplar ads embodying the pattern. get.summary: Per-ad funnel diagnosis (Phase 2.8)
get.description: Per-ad funnel-layer percentile breakdown — delivery, attention, retention, click_intent, postclick_messaging, attributed_revenue, platform_diagnostics. Each layer carries the ad's percentile within its cohort, the smoothed metric, sample_n, weakest-layer flag, diagnostic codes (e.g. retention_below_p25_at_mature_stage), and a recommended_priority — one of: fix_offer_or_audience, fix_landing_or_offer, fix_hook, improve_creative_clarity, increase_spend, rework_offer_or_landing, maintain. Cold-maturity ads with spend < $50 return 'increase_spend' (the 'spend_below_learning_phase' code). When the ad has no per-layer percentiles yet but at least one diagnostic_code applies, the response contains a single layer='no_data' row carrying the codes + recommended_priority. Scope: campaigns:read.

get.summary: Get customer conversions
get.description:
Paginated list of customers who achieved a goal. Requires `customers:read` scope. Returns PII (name, email).

**Filters** are `filter[<dimension>]=<operator>:<value>`, e.g. `filter[channel]=is:Paid Social`. Dimensions: `channel`, `campaign`, `country`. Operators: `is`, `is_not`, `contains`, `not_contains`. Anything else is 400 `invalid_parameter` — a filter this endpoint cannot apply is refused, never silently dropped.

A row is returned when the customer/visitor has **at least one touch** matching every filter (for `/customers`, a touch at or before the conversion; for `/visitors`, a touch inside the requested window). That is the same rule the rest of the attribution engine applies, so a filtered list reconciles with a filtered KPI. Note the consequence: the `channel` / `campaign_name` / `country` a row DISPLAYS are first-touch (customers) or last-touch (visitors) projections, so a returned row may show a different channel than the one filtered on.

`campaign` compares against the campaign identifier carried on the touch — the value surfaced as `raw_campaign`, which for Meta is the campaign's platform id — not the resolved campaign name. `country` is the ISO-3166 alpha-2 code, the same value returned as `country`.

Filtering is applied in the database before pagination, so a filtered page is a full page and `pagination.cursor` stays correct.

post.summary: Ingest a server-side outcome event (e.g. a closed sale)
post.description:
Records an outcome event — the path an ERP or backend posts a closed sale through, so Atribu can join the sale back to the ad click that produced it.

**Event name.** There is no `sale_closed` type. Send `payment_received` for a sale where money changed hands (revenue type `cash`, the only kind counted as revenue for ROAS) or `closed_won` for a won-but-unpaid deal (`pipeline`, deliberately excluded from ROAS). Any other name is accepted and stored, but produces no conversion unless a goal lists it in `source_event_names` — the response's `conversion.matched` tells you which happened.

**Idempotency.** Send the sale's deal/order id as the `Idempotency-Key` header or `idempotency_key` field; retries collapse onto one outcome event. It is REQUIRED when `properties.value` is set.

**Attributability.** Include whatever identity you have: `anonymous_id` (strongest — the tracker's visitor id from your checkout), `user_traits.email`/`phone`, `click_ids.fbclid`/`gclid`, `session_id`, `utm`. Attribution runs asynchronously; 202 means the event was recorded, not that credit has been assigned yet.

Requires the `events:write` scope.

202.description: Event recorded. Conversion extraction and attribution run asynchronously.

400.description: Invalid body — including a value-bearing event sent without an idempotency key.

post.summary: Report a Webpay (Transbank) payment
post.description:
Records a completed Webpay Plus transaction as a cash outcome event, with the ad click that produced it.

**Why this exists.** Webpay has no `metadata` field and no webhook, so the Stripe/MercadoPago passthrough has nowhere to live. The only merchant-supplied values Transbank echoes back on `commit` are `buy_order` (26 chars) and `session_id` (61) — and the `atb1.` attribution token is 80–904 characters, so it cannot ride either.

**Two steps.** (1) When you call `Transaction.create()`, send `session_id: atribuTracker.getAttributionRef() || yourOwnSessionId` — a 48-character packed reference to the visitor. (2) After `Transaction.commit()`, POST the response here verbatim. Atribu maps `amount`/`transaction_date`/`buy_order` and decodes the visitor from `session_id`.

**Idempotency is automatic**: the event is filed under `<buy_order>_<authorization_code>`, the same key the webpay.cl report importer uses, so retries — and a later monthly PDF upload of the same payment — collapse onto one conversion.

Only `status: AUTHORIZED` with `response_code: 0` becomes revenue; anything else comes back as `ignored`. Requires the `events:write` scope.

buy_order.description: Transbank's `buy_order`, echoed back verbatim on commit. With `authorization_code` it forms the idempotency key — and it is the SAME key the webpay.cl report importer builds from the report's OC column, so a monthly PDF upload lands on this row instead of double-counting the sale.

session_id.description: Transbank's `session_id`, echoed back verbatim. This is the attribution carrier: put `atribuTracker.getAttributionRef()` here when you call `Transaction.create()` and the sale ties to the exact ad click with no email match. Your own value passes through untouched when it is not an Atribu ref.

amount.description: The authorized amount. Integer for CLP; up to 2 decimals on the USD products. Send Transbank's own number, or an exact decimal string.

status.description: Webpay transaction status. Only `AUTHORIZED` becomes a cash conversion; anything else is reported back as `ignored` and stored nowhere.

authorization_code.description: Transbank's authorization code. Required on an AUTHORIZED transaction — it is half the idempotency key.

transaction_date.description: ISO-8601 authorization timestamp. Becomes the outcome event's `event_time`, which is what the attribution window is measured against. Defaults to now if omitted.

response_code.description: 0 is approved. Any other value is a decline and is ignored even when `status` reads AUTHORIZED.

balance.description: Monto restante para un detalle anulado.

vci.description: Stored, never validated — Transbank's own reference tells merchants not to gate on it.

commit.description: The `Transaction.commit` response from Transbank, forwarded verbatim. `Transaction.status` returns the identical field set and is equally acceptable.

currency.description: ISO-4217 override. Defaults to CLP — Webpay Plus settles in Chilean pesos.

attribution_token.description: A full `atb1.` token from `getAttributionToken()`, if your backend kept one in its own session across the redirect. It carries the UTMs and click ids as well as the identity, so it wins over the ref in `session_id`. Optional — the ref alone is enough.

allOf.description: Buyer identity, if you have it. Webpay returns none — it hands back only the last 4 card digits.

schema.description: A completed Webpay Plus transaction. Post the commit response exactly as Transbank returned it; Atribu does the field mapping.

202.description: Commit processed. `status: accepted` recorded a cash event; `status: ignored` means the transaction was not an authorized sale.

400.description: Invalid body — including an AUTHORIZED transaction with no authorization code.

post.summary: Send a channel-agnostic message
post.description:
Sends a WhatsApp or Instagram message via a connected `data_connection`. Requires the `whatsapp` or `instagram` scope on the API key (matching the `channel`). For keys minted through the OAuth provider flow, an active `oauth_app_authorizations` row must also exist for the (app, profile, data_connection).

**WhatsApp media (image/video/audio/document)** accepts either `media.media_id` (pre-uploaded via Meta's `/media` endpoint, 30-day cache) or `media.link` (public HTTPS URL Meta fetches once per send — no caching, size caps enforced). High-fanout sends should pre-upload.

**Instagram image/video** accept `image_url` / `video_url` directly (Meta fetches the URL). Quick replies are IG-only.

**WhatsApp Flows** (`content.type='flow'`) send a Meta-hosted multi-screen form behind a CTA button. Manage flows via `/api/v1/whatsapp/flows`; the customer's answers arrive on the `message.received` webhook as `raw.interactive.nfm_reply.response_json`.

**Email is capped per mailbox per UTC day** (#341). Atribu holds each connected mailbox well under its provider's own daily send limit — crossing that limit suspends the mailbox itself for up to 24 hours — so a send beyond the cap answers **429** and outbound resumes automatically at the next UTC midnight. Defaults are 300/day for a personal-domain mailbox (gmail.com, outlook.com, …) and 1,500/day for a Google Workspace / Microsoft 365 one; the effective cap is per connection and can be raised. Inbound sync is never paused.

schema.description: Optional (#1517). A client-generated retry token, unique per logical send — Vitrina uses the message id. Scoped to your API key, this route and this key: a repeat within 24 hours replays the first response verbatim and sends nothing, a repeat that arrives while the first send is still in flight answers 409 `idempotency_key_in_flight` (retry with backoff), and a repeat carrying a different body answers 409 `idempotency_key_conflict` (mint a fresh key). Only a 2xx is stored, so a send that failed can be retried under the same key. Omit the header and every request sends, exactly as before.

post.summary: Mark a WhatsApp message read (with or without a typing indicator)
post.description:
Marks the customer's inbound message read and, by default, shows the "typing…" bubble, so an agent that takes tens of seconds to compose a reply produces the signals a human agent would. One Meta call: the indicator is a field on the read receipt, so **the read receipt is not optional** — Meta offers no way to show typing without marking read.

**Two modes, via `indicator`.** `typing` (default) = read receipt + bubble, for an agent that is composing. `read` = read receipt only, for a human who just opened the conversation in your inbox — blue ticks without a bubble that would promise a reply nobody made. Everything else on this route is identical between the two, which is why they share one endpoint. Consumers written before `indicator` existed send nothing and keep the original behaviour.

Auth, scope (`whatsapp`) and connection resolution are identical to `POST /api/v1/messages`, including the `oauth_app_authorizations` grant check for OAuth-flow-minted keys.

**Best-effort.** One upstream call, no retries, no queueing, a 4-second upstream budget. The indicator shows for at most 25 seconds and is dismissed the moment you send a message on that thread — there is nothing to cancel and no "typing off" call.

**`message_id` is the INBOUND wamid** (the customer's message), not one of yours — Meta derives the recipient from it. An unknown or stale wamid (older than ~24h, already read, number re-registered) answers **200** with `forwarded: false`, not an error: none of those is a caller fault or has a remedy, and non-2xx is reserved for faults somebody can act on.

**This route never answers 404.** An unknown, wrong-profile or unauthorized `connection_id` answers 403 — consumers treat 404 on this path as "typing is not deployed on this bridge" and disable the feature.

WhatsApp only today; Instagram and Messenger are the intended extension of this same endpoint (which is why `to` is required even though WhatsApp does not need it). Email has no typing concept.

channel.description: `whatsapp` only today; anything else is a 400.

to.description: The customer's wa_id (conversation external id). Redundant for the Meta call itself — Meta derives the recipient from `message_id` — but load-bearing here: it is the only thing that can catch a `message_id` from a different conversation (see below), it is logged truncated on every non-delivery, and it is what the future Instagram/Messenger extension of this endpoint keys on.

message_id.description: The INBOUND wamid the receipt anchors to (e.g. `wamid.HBgLNTY5…`). Unknown/stale values are a 200 no-op. When the wamid is one Atribu has stored AND its conversation belongs to somebody other than `to`, the request is a 200 no-op with `reason: "message_id_conversation_mismatch"` and is NOT forwarded — a mismatched pair would blue-tick (and, in `typing` mode, animate) a thread you did not mean to touch.

indicator.description:
Which signal to send. `typing` (the default) marks the message read AND shows the "typing…" bubble — use it when an agent is composing a reply. `read` marks the message read ONLY, with no bubble — use it when a human opened the conversation in your inbox: blue ticks say "a person saw this", while a bubble would promise a reply within 25 seconds that nobody made.

Omit it for the original behaviour. The applied mode is echoed back in `data.indicator`; if that field is absent the deployment predates this option and showed a bubble regardless.

Prefer this over `media.link` for reliability: with a media_id Meta never fetches your URL, so origin-hosted, private, short-lived, or non-public media works — a `link` requires Meta to fetch a public HTTPS URL at send time. It's also the right path for high-fanout sends.

get.summary: Read a number's SIP digest credentials
get.description: Returns the Meta-generated SIP credentials for one number, so they can be configured on the SIP server that will answer Meta's INVITEs. **This is the only endpoint that returns a secret.** It is a separate route rather than a flag on `GET /whatsapp/calling` on purpose: that route's guarantee that it never requests `include_sip_credentials` is then a property of the code, not of an argument value. Meta publishes no static SIP egress IP ranges and does not support mTLS, so digest auth is the practical control on who may INVITE your trunk: your server answers with `407` and Meta re-sends carrying the challenge response. `username` is the digest username — the business number as DIGITS ONLY, with NO leading `+`. Meta's guide calls it "the (normalized) business phone number", which reads as E.164, but a captured call shows Meta authenticating as `username="16065177691"` while its own request URI carries `sip:+16065177691@...`. It is not the `phone_number_id` and not the punctuated `display_phone_number`. Configure any other spelling and every call is rejected with a 401 that presents as ringing which never answers. The response is an allowlist projection of named fields, never Meta's payload, and it is `Cache-Control: no-store`. Atribu stores none of it: the drift snapshot is written by the settings route and structurally cannot hold a credential. Returns 404 when the number has no SIP credential (calling disabled, or no `sip` configuration).

post.summary: OAuth 2.0 token endpoint
post.description:
Mints an Atribu API key. Two grant types:

**`authorization_code`** (RFC 6749 §4.1.3) — exchanges a single-use `code` issued at `/oauth/authorize` consent. Requires `code` + `redirect_uri`.

**`client_credentials`** (RFC 6749 §4.4) — mints a delegated per-profile key with no user interaction. Requires `profile_id`. Succeeds **only** when an active (non-revoked) `oauth_app_authorizations` grant already exists for (client, profile); it never creates one, so it cannot be used to acquire access, only to mint a token for access already granted. A profile with no grant answers `invalid_grant`, deliberately indistinguishable from a profile that does not exist.

Every call mints **new** key material and does not rotate: previously issued keys stay valid until explicitly revoked at `/oauth/revoke`. At most **5** active keys may exist per grant — the 6th call returns `invalid_request` telling you to revoke one first.

Revoking the underlying authorization (the connected-apps page in the Atribu UI) revokes **every** key minted under it, `client_credentials` keys included.

post.summary: Apply a recommendation (inline, terminal response)
post.description:
Executes the recommendation through the meta-actions layer: one write spine, one audit trail (`meta_action_log`), one rollback system. There is no queue and nothing to poll — the response says what happened.

Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header (1–256 chars). Leg-level dedup is automatic (the executor derives its keys from the recommendation id), so retrying an already-applied recommendation returns `200` with `replayed: true` rather than double-spending.

`applied_by` is REQUIRED for the budget kinds (`scale_winner`, `budget_reallocate_winners`): money-tier changes never move without a human on the record, and the id is verified to be an active owner/admin of the key's workspace.

**`require_approval: true` routes the apply past a person instead of executing it.** You get `202` with a hand-off — a URL to give your user (session-less, works on a phone, expires in 45 minutes) and an id to poll. That is how an agent, or an agency acting for a client, puts a human between itself and an ad account's money. Every refusal the direct apply gives (`404`, `409`, `410`, `403`) is still answered BEFORE the hand-off is minted, so a hand-off is never handed out for a change that cannot succeed.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

require_approval.description: Ask a human before applying. Nothing is written: the response is `202` with `{status: "awaiting_approval", handoff}` — hand `handoff.url` to the person who owns the account and poll `GET /api/v1/handoffs/{id}`. Approving runs this exact call through the same audited path; the hand-off's `result.apply` then carries the same body a direct apply returns. Rejecting settles it `cancelled` and writes nothing.

Read this when an apply reported `failed` or `partial`, or before applying to see what earlier attempts did. `campaigns:read` — it writes nothing, and gating a post-mortem behind the apply scope would make operators hold write access just to find out why a write failed.

post.summary: Join an inbound WhatsApp message to the web session that produced it
post.description:
Runs Atribu's join tiers in descending determinism — `text_token` (opt-in per profile) → `text_correlation` (the default, invisible tier) → `phone_identity_submitted` → `phone_identity_early` — and, when the join lands, records a `whatsapp_conversation_started` outcome event so the conversation flows through the normal attribution chain.

Supplying `ctwa_clid` (Meta's click-to-WhatsApp click id, resolved on the caller's side) makes that the reported `join_method` while `session_join_method` still names whichever Atribu tier produced the linkage — both facts stay measurable.

A deliberate non-join is a success, not an error: an ambiguous match (two different visitors sending the same prefilled text inside the window) returns `200` with `ambiguous: true` and `conversation_started: false`, because writing an unplaceable conversation would inflate the profile's pipeline count.

IDEMPOTENT — retry it. The recorded event's `external_id` hashes facts about the MESSAGE (merchant phone, sender phone, `occurred_at`, normalised body), all of which a retry resends verbatim, so redelivery converges on one row.

Scope: `events:write` OR `whatsapp`.

get.summary: Drill into a dashboard KPI — the rows behind the number
get.description:
The row-level detail behind a KPI tile, in seven kinds — the seven `p_kind` values of the canonical conversion-detail read. Dashboard tiles map onto them many-to-one: MER and NMER are ratios over `attributed_revenue`, so both drill to the same rows.

| `kind` | grain | backs |
|---|---|---|
| `first_payment` | conversion | new-customer / first-payment counts |
| `attributed_revenue` | conversion | Revenue, ROAS, MER, NMER |
| `recurring_customer` | customer | MRR / recurring revenue |
| `refunded` | conversion | refund rate |
| `excluded_first` | conversion | the payments the first-payment count left out, and why |
| `cac_by_channel` | channel | CAC |
| `spend_by_campaign` | campaign | Spend |

**Dashboard tile aliases.** The console's KPI tiles have their own names, and this route accepts them as `kind` aliases so a caller can send what the tile is called. The response's `kind` is always the CANONICAL one — `mer` and `nmer` both come back as `attributed_revenue`, because the row shape is what `kind` discriminates and there is one shape behind all three. Aliases are not members of the `kind` enum: they are a courtesy on the way in, never part of a response.

| tile alias | canonical `kind` |
|---|---|
| `first` | `first_payment` |
| `revenue` | `attributed_revenue` |
| `mer` | `attributed_revenue` |
| `nmer` | `attributed_revenue` |
| `mrr` | `recurring_customer` |
| `cac` | `cac_by_channel` |
| `spend` | `spend_by_campaign` |
| `refundRate` | `refunded` |

**`include=excluded`.** On `kind=first_payment` only, adds an `excluded` array to the same body: the payments the first-payment count deliberately left out, and why — the same rows `kind=excluded_first` returns on its own. One request instead of two, so a first-payment view cannot render a count from one window beside exclusions from another. Sending it on any other kind is 400 `invalid_parameter` rather than silently ignored, and it is refused with `format=csv` because a CSV body is a single table with a published column order — request `kind=excluded_first&format=csv` for those rows. When it is not sent the key is ABSENT, not empty: `[]` would claim there are none.

**Scopes.** `analytics:read` for every kind, plus `customers:read` for the five that name a person (`first_payment`, `attributed_revenue`, `recurring_customer`, `refunded`, `excluded_first`). A key with `analytics:read` alone reads `cac_by_channel` and `spend_by_campaign` and gets 403 `insufficient_scope` on the rest.

**Every kind is model-aware.** Filters and acquisition touches resolve against the conversion's attributed touch under `model`, so a filtered drill reconciles with the filtered KPI rather than contradicting it.

**Filters** are `filter[<dimension>]=<operator>:<value>`, e.g. `filter[channel]=is:Paid Social`. Only the dimensions the engine can scope **spend** by are accepted (`channel`, `referrer`, `campaign`, `entry_page`, `goal`); anything else is 400 `invalid_parameter`. That is deliberate — a dimension spend cannot be scoped by makes every ratio built on spend silently wrong, so it is refused rather than answered.

**CSV.** Add `format=csv` for a downloadable `text/csv` body — the same rows as the JSON form, `Content-Disposition: attachment` with a filename derived from the kind and the date range. Content negotiation via `Accept` is deliberately NOT used: the header is unreachable from the `<a download>` links that consume this, and a hidden switch between two body types is worse than a visible one. Column order per kind (stable — treat it as contract):

`first_payment`: conversion_id, customer_profile_id, customer_name, customer_email, amount, currency, paid_at, channel, source, campaign_name, ad_name, ad_set_name, provider, first_touch_at, first_touch_source, last_touch_at, last_touch_source, session_count, journey_days, attributed_credit, confidence, payment_kind, possible_duplicate

`attributed_revenue`: conversion_id, customer_profile_id, customer_name, customer_email, amount, currency, paid_at, channel, source, campaign_name, ad_name, ad_set_name, provider, first_touch_at, first_touch_source, last_touch_at, last_touch_source, session_count, journey_days, attributed_credit, confidence, payment_kind, possible_duplicate

`recurring_customer`: customer_profile_id, customer_name, customer_email, recurring_revenue, recurring_payments, lifetime_payments, lifetime_value, first_payment_at, last_payment_at, avg_cadence_days, acquisition_channel, acquisition_source, acquisition_campaign

`refunded`: conversion_id, customer_profile_id, customer_name, customer_email, amount, currency, refunded_at, external_source, reason

`excluded_first`: conversion_id, customer_profile_id, customer_name, customer_email, amount, currency, paid_at, exclude_kind, reason, detail, prior_payment_at, prior_payment_amount

`cac_by_channel`: channel, spend, first_customers, cac

`spend_by_campaign`: campaign_id, platform_id, campaign_name, provider, spend, impressions, clicks, cpm, cpc, ctr, revenue, outcome_count, roas, prev_spend, spend_change_pct

post.summary: Provision a dealer (app-authenticated)
post.description:
Creates an Atribu tenant for one of your dealers and grants your app access to it, in a single call. No end-user browser bounce is involved.

**Authentication is different from every other endpoint.** Send your app's `client_id` and `client_secret` as HTTP Basic auth — *not* an `atb_live_` key. There is no key to send: this is the call that creates the profile a key would be scoped to.

**What it creates.** A passwordless owner user from `email`, a workspace of its own for this dealer (one workspace per dealer, so workspace-level views can never mix two of them), a profile inside it, and the authorization grant carrying `scopes`.

**Getting a key — the sequence.** This endpoint returns NO key material, on purpose. Once you hold `profile_id`, mint keys yourself:

```
POST /oauth/token
Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret)
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&profile_id=<profile_id>
```

That returns an `atb_live_` access token scoped to the dealer, which every other endpoint accepts as `Authorization: Bearer`. It works because the grant this call wrote already exists — `client_credentials` mints tokens for access you hold, it can never create access. Mint on your own schedule; keys stay valid until revoked, up to 5 live per dealer.

**Idempotency.** Keyed on (your app, `external_ref`). A repeat call returns the same `profile_id` / `workspace_id` / `grant_id` with HTTP 200 and `created: false`; only the first returns 201. A repeat with different `scopes` updates the grant in place, which is how you widen or narrow a dealer's delegation.

**#488 (PR-2) — a SECOND, unrelated way to call this endpoint.** Send a Supabase session bearer (`Authorization: Bearer`, the credential Atribu's own console uses) instead of Basic auth, and the body shape changes to `SessionProvisionProfileRequest`: an owner/admin adds a profile to a workspace they already run. No workspace, shadow user or grant is created — see that schema's own description. The two branches share a URL and nothing else; a consumer app's integration is entirely unaffected by this branch existing.

**#1067 — the session branch enforces the workspace's `active_profiles` plan limit.** A workspace already at its cap answers `403 profile_limit_reached` with `upgrade_required: true` and `upgrade: { plan }`; check `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/subscription`'s `limits.active_profiles` before calling if you want to avoid it. The Basic-auth branch is NOT subject to this limit — each call provisions a brand-new workspace holding exactly one profile, and a consumer app's dealer count is governed by its own commercial agreement, not `PLANS.starter.limits`.

201.description: Dealer provisioned, or (session branch) the new profile created

Present a Supabase session bearer (the credential Atribu's own console uses) to call it.

delete.description:
Retires a profile your app provisioned, and its dealer workspace with it. **Terminal — there is no un-archive.**

**Preconditions:** the profile was provisioned by **your** app (`provisioned_by` = your `client_id`). Any other profile — unknown, another app's, or one a human created — answers `404 not_found`, identically; there is no way to tell which of the three you hit.

**One workspace per dealer is the shape this assumes.** Provisioning gives every dealer a workspace of its own, so archiving the profile and archiving its workspace are the SAME transaction — the same `archive_workspace` primitive `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}` uses: every membership removed, pending invitations revoked, the workspace's API keys revoked, its webhook subscriptions paused, and its non-audit data purged. If a human has since added a SECOND live profile to that workspace, this call answers `409 invalid_state` instead of silently widening to destroy a profile your app never provisioned.

**Effect, one call:** revokes every LIVE grant on the profile — any app's — and every delegated API key each one minted, then runs the shared workspace archive.

**Idempotent.** The first call and every later call both answer `200 {"archived": true, "workspace_archived": true}` — a DELETE that 404s an already-archived profile would make a retry look like a failure.

post.summary: Adopt an existing profile (app-authenticated)
post.description:
Names an EXISTING profile your app already provisioned with `external_ref`, for a profile that predates your use of it — most commonly one your consent flow created before you switched it to ADR 0020's `external_ref` addressing. Stamps `provisioned_external_ref`, upserts the profile-level grant with `scopes`, and writes an audit event, all in one call.

**Preconditions** (all four, or the request answers 404 — see below): the profile was provisioned by YOUR app, it carries no external_ref other than the one you are sending, it is not archived, and your app holds at least one LIVE grant on it (profile-level, or per-connection from a completed WhatsApp/Instagram consent).

**Idempotency.** Keyed on the profile, not on `external_ref` — you name the profile in the path. A repeat call with the SAME `external_ref` returns HTTP 200 with `created: false`; only the call that performs the stamp returns 201. A repeat with DIFFERENT `scopes` still updates the grant, exactly like re-provisioning does.

**A 404 never distinguishes** an unknown `profileId`, another app's profile, an archived one, or one your app holds no live grant on — the same rule every ownership check on this surface follows. **A 409** means the profile is legitimately yours but already carries a DIFFERENT `external_ref` — including the case where a concurrent `POST /api/v1/profiles` claimed this exact `external_ref` for a different profile while this call was in flight; the underlying unique index is the arbiter either way.

post.summary: Create a workspace
post.description:
Creates a brand-new workspace.

**Two unrelated ways to call this endpoint, sharing one URL** — the same shape `POST /api/v1/profiles` uses, for the same reason.

**Session bearer** (`Authorization: Bearer`, a Supabase session access token, or an MCP user token): you create your OWN new workspace and become its owner. Body: `SessionWorkspaceRequest`. A second workspace for the same caller is allowed — the plan gate is on `active_profiles` per workspace, not on how many workspaces one person owns.

**HTTP Basic** (`client_id:client_secret`, a registered consumer app): you create a bare workspace for one of YOUR OWN users, identified by `email`. Body: `AppWorkspaceRequest`. No profile and no delegation grant are created here — follow with your own `POST /api/v1/profiles` call (Basic auth) if you also need those.

**The session branch is idempotent on `(caller, name)` for a short window** — a retried call with the same `name` returns the SAME workspace with `created: false` and `200`, instead of a duplicate; a call minutes later with the same `name` is a genuinely new workspace. The app-credential branch has no idempotency key at all — every call creates, and `created` is always `true`. A replay never mints a second checkout hand-off either — `checkout` is `null` on the `created: false` response.

**`plan: "growth" | "agency"` also mints a Stripe Checkout hand-off**, returned as `checkout`: give the human its `url`, poll `GET /api/v1/handoffs/{id}` the way `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/checkout-session` already works. Minting is never allowed to block workspace creation — a failed mint (unconfigured billing, Stripe refusing the request) still answers 201 with `checkout: null` and a `warnings` entry naming `checkout_unavailable`; retry the mint alone with `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/checkout-session`.

200.description: Idempotent replay of the session branch — the same workspace, `created: false`.

get.summary: The workspace's top-performing ads, across every profile
get.description:
The cross-profile creative leaderboard. Ads are scored against *comparable* creative — a cohort is channel × format × objective × audience warmth × geo × placement, and that cohort is populated ACROSS the workspace, which is why this read exists at this grain and cannot be assembled from per-profile calls.

**Three distinct measures per ad. Present them separately; never merge them.** `composite_score` (0–100) is a transparent rule blend of within-cohort percentiles. `top_performer_likelihood` (0–1) is a PROBABILITY — a likelihood, not a guarantee, and never ROAS; it is the calibrated ML-ranker output when `score_source='model'` (with `model_version` set) and a monotone function of `composite_score` otherwise. `attributed_revenue`/`roas` is real cash Atribu attributed, present when `truth_grade='attributed'`. `meta_reported_conversions` is a FOURTH thing again — Meta's own last-click count, never folded into `truth_grade` and never added to Atribu's outcomes.

`primary_outcome_kind` is the cohort-appropriate HEADLINE: `cash` → revenue/ROAS, `pipeline` → attributed leads + `attributed_pipeline_value` (a projection, never in ROAS), `messaging` → conversations started, `meta` → Meta's own number (labelled as such), `none` → the composite score alone. Filter on it with `outcome_kinds` rather than sorting a lead-gen workspace by a ROAS that is null on every row.

`maturity_stage` (cold→early→mature→calibrated) says how settled a score is; `reason_codes` say which funnel layer is strong or weak, with a sample-confidence band and the `sample_n` that band was derived from. Scores refresh on a daily cadence.

**The four nested groups** carry the rest of the feature-store row: `identity` (external ids, creative copy, the delivery days and the attribution model the `attributed_*` legs were credited under), `metrics` (`delivery` / `video` / `messaging` / `outcomes` — sub-grouped because an all-null `video` means 'not a video ad' while an all-null `messaging` means 'no conversation funnel', and flattening loses that), `score` (the within-cohort `pct_*` percentiles and the empirical-Bayes `smoothed_*` estimates the blend consumes) and `creative` (what the ad is made of, with `has_vision_analysis` as the honesty flag over the rest).

Four things are deliberately NOT published: the ML ranker's per-feature contributions, the raw score-explanation blob, the ten empirical-Bayes effective sample sizes (an input to the smoothing, not a statement about the ad — the smoothed estimate is here and is what can be acted on), and the cohort classifier's `*_source`/`*_confidence` provenance, which is about our pipeline rather than about the advertiser's ad.

**Session bearers only.** An API key is minted for exactly one profile — the credential IS the scope — so it has no workspace to read across and this route answers `403 insufficient_scope` for one. Present a Supabase session bearer (the credential Atribu's own console uses).

A workspace owner, admin or analyst sees every profile in the workspace; anyone else sees only the profiles they hold a membership on. That narrowing happens in the database, not in the response shape, so a guest gets a 200 over a smaller set — never someone else's rows.

Parse before doing arithmetic, and keep sorting and range filters server-side: a page of decimal strings sorted lexically gives `"9.00" > "10.00"`, and that failure is silent.

sample_n.description: Cohort ads the percentile was ranked against. A percentile without its sample is a rank presented as a fact; `sample_confidence` is the band derived from this number.

day_from.description: First day of DELIVERY inside the window — not the window's nominal start. An ad that ran six days of a 28d window says so here; dividing by 28 instead of by `metrics.delivery.days_active` is wrong about every per-day number drawn from it.

attribution_model_used.description: The model the `attributed_*` legs were credited under. Rows scored under different models are not comparable.

days_active.description: Days in the window with non-zero delivery — the denominator for any per-day rate.

spend_reporting.description: Spend in the PROFILE's reporting currency; the top-level `spend` is the ad account's own. They differ whenever an account bills in a currency the profile does not report in, and only this one is meaningful to sum across profiles.

video.description: Every rate is NULL — never 0 — for an ad with no video. 'No plays to measure' and 'nobody held past three seconds' are opposite findings.

messaging_total_connections.description: Distinct people reached on the messaging surface — the rates' denominator.

block_rate.description: Share of connections that blocked. The one rate here that is bad when it is high.

messaging.description: Conversation DEPTH, which is the messaging funnel's point: a conversation that starts and dies is not an outcome.

outcome_value_first_payment.description: The FIRST-PAYMENT subset of `attributed_revenue`, not an addition to it. `roas_first_payment` is the acquisition ROAS a subscription business budgets against.

top_performer_likelihood_calibrated.description: The ML ranker's CALIBRATED probability — non-null only when a model actually scored this row (`score_source = 'model'`). The top-level `top_performer_likelihood` falls back to a monotone squash of `composite_score` when it did not, so this is how a consumer tells 'a model said 0.71' from 'the rule blend implies 0.71'.

has_vision_analysis.description: The honesty flag on this whole group. False means the fields were derived from COPY alone, so an absent `camera_shot` is 'not looked at', not 'no camera movement'.

creative_signature.description: Stable hash of the creative's structural features. Equal signatures mean the same creative — how a duplicate is spotted across profiles.

internals.description: UNSTABLE — NOT PART OF THE PUBLIC CONTRACT. Present only when `include=internals` is requested by a session credential (Atribu's own console); absent otherwise, and the parameter is ignored for any other credential. The shape belongs to the scoring engine and may change or disappear in any release without a version bump. Do not build against it.

currency.description: The profile's reporting currency (ISO-4217). Present on the WORKSPACE leaderboard and not on the profile-scoped one, because this response can carry a CLP profile's ads beside a USD profile's and a renderer has no other way to tell them apart. `null` when it could not be resolved — render the amount uncoded rather than assuming dollars.

delete.description:
Retires a workspace and everything under it. **OWNER ONLY**, and **terminal — there is no un-archive.**

**"Delete" here means ARCHIVE, and the response says so.** A workspace that has ever exported holds `conversion_exports` rows, which a database trigger refuses to let any path erase — they are the record of what Atribu transmitted on a customer's behalf. So this call stamps `archived_at`, sets every membership to `removed`, revokes pending invitations, archives every profile and purges their non-audit data, revokes the workspace's API keys and pauses its webhook subscriptions; `conversion_exports` and `tracking_signal_audit_log` stay attached to the archived workspace and are counted in `counts.retained_*`. Same contract as `DELETE /api/v1/profiles/demo`.

**Idempotent.** The first call answers `200 {"archived": true}`; every later call answers `200 {"archived": false}` with the ORIGINAL `archived_at`. A DELETE that 404s an already-archived workspace would make a retry look like a failure.

**Credentials.** A session bearer, or an MCP `atb_user_…` token whose grant covers `workspaces:write` (a default `mcp:read` token is refused). An `atb_live_` API key cannot call it — a key is minted for exactly one profile and belongs to no workspace. A member who is not an owner gets `403 forbidden`; a non-member gets `404`, the same answer an unknown id gets, so the status code never confirms that a workspace exists.

**After archiving, every workspace-scoped route answers 404 for it**, and it is absent from `GET /api/v1/workspaces` and from MCP `whoami`.

post.summary: Erase a customer's personal data
post.description:
Erases one person's personal data from this workspace, for **any** provider — GoHighLevel, Stripe, MercadoPago, Shopify, WhatsApp or the browser tracker. **OWNER OR ADMIN ONLY**, and **terminal — there is no un-erase.**

**What it does.** It NULLs the identifying columns and deletes the identifier rows across every store that holds this person's data — the customer profile, the identity graph, conversation message bodies and their media, CRM payloads, order and browser signals — and stamps `redacted_at`. It does NOT delete the customer row: its id is what keeps `outcome_events`, `conversions` and `attribution_touchpoints` referentially whole, so your attribution totals and revenue history are unchanged. Because the columns are emptied rather than flagged, a reader that forgets to check `redacted_at` still cannot surface the person.

**What it deliberately keeps.** `conversion_exports` rows survive: they are the record of what Atribu transmitted to an ad platform on your behalf, and a database trigger refuses to let any path delete them. The personal fields inside their payloads (`client_ip_address`, `client_user_agent`, `fbp`, `fbc`) are stripped; the SHA-256 hashes that were actually sent remain as evidence. Any not-yet-sent export for this person is marked `skipped` so it can never ship.

**Scope is this workspace.** Each workspace is a separate data controller with its own relationship to the person, so this call never reaches another workspace's records. Erasing someone from several workspaces is several calls, each authorised by that workspace's own owner or admin.

**Matching is exact.** Email and phone match exactly (email case-insensitively); there is no suffix or fuzzy matching, because an over-match here erases somebody who did not ask. Supply whichever selector you hold — at least one is required.

**Idempotent.** A repeat answers `200` with `erased: false` and `already_redacted` showing how many were already done, keeping the ORIGINAL `redacted_at`.

**Credentials.** A session bearer, or an MCP `atb_user_…` token whose grant covers `workspaces:write` (a default `mcp:read` token is refused). An `atb_live_` API key cannot call it: a key is minted for exactly one profile, belongs to no workspace, and names no person for the audit row. A member who is not an owner or admin gets `403 forbidden`; a non-member gets `404`, the same answer an unknown workspace gets, so the status code never confirms that a workspace or an e-mail exists.

The DIMENSION-grain companion to `/creative-patterns`. That route mines (hook × format × cta) COMBINATIONS and tells you who is not running them; this one takes one dimension at a time — hook type, narrative arc, CTA and so on — and answers how often an ad carrying a given value ends up a winner.

**The lift is an ASSOCIATION.** `lift_vs_workspace` is the row's win rate over the workspace's own baseline, and `confidence_interval_low`/`_high` is the interval that estimate sits in. get.summary: The signed-in user's own account
get.description:
Who the caller is, how they can sign in, where they are signed in, and what would block them from deleting the account — in one round trip, because a settings surface wants all four at once.

`user` is the editable identity (`PATCH /api/v1/me` changes `full_name` and `locale`). `identities` is the auth-provider list — provider keys and the address each provider knows, never a token. `sessions` is one row per signed-in device, freshest first, with `is_current` resolved from the bearer token this request carried. `sole_owner_workspaces` names the workspaces whose ownership would be orphaned by a deletion.

**App credentials get a different, smaller answer (#1048).** An OAuth app's own HTTP Basic `client_id:client_secret` — the credential `POST /api/v1/profiles` and `POST /api/v1/workspaces` accept — receives `{ data: { app, return_url_supported } }` with no `meta`, since the caller is a credential, not a person. `return_url_supported` is the one fact a consumer needs before passing a `return_url` to any connect start.

Everything here is the CALLER'S OWN data, resolved from the verified token and from nothing the request asserted. There is no parameter naming a user, so reading someone else's account is not expressible — which is also why no PII scope gates it.

**Session bearers only.** An API key is minted for exactly one profile — it is not a person, has no sessions and no linked identities — so this route answers `403 insufficient_scope` for one. Present a Supabase session bearer (the credential Atribu's own console uses).

Each is a real GoTrue flow (a breach check and a rate-limited re-authentication for the password; a dual-confirmation mail for the email) with its own request shape, so neither fits a partial PATCH of two plain columns.

post.description:
Re-points up to 20 ad sets' `promoted_object` at the event this rule sends, one at a time so a single failure cannot cancel the rest. Every write goes through the Meta action layer, so each one has an audit row, an idempotent replay key and a rollback.

post.summary: Apply the Platform-Safe go-live change
post.description: Moves the named ad sets onto the Clean Dataset's neutral Custom Conversion. Each ad set's target is recomputed SERVER-SIDE and never trusted from the body, so a stale tab cannot send an ad set somewhere unexpected. The in-place re-point is always attempted first, even when a preview said it would fail — the attempt is the authoritative test and a preview is a snapshot; only Meta's frozen-ad-set refusal escalates to a rebuild, and only with `confirm_recreate`. Rides the action layer, so every write has pre-state, an audit row and a rollback. Workspace owners and admins only when the caller is a person: this switches which event campaigns optimize on and resets Meta's learning.

post.summary: Re-queue failed, dead-lettered or skipped conversion exports

Resets matching `conversion_exports` rows to `pending` and hands the worker a job.

The profile's legal gate is checked FIRST and refuses with 409 when it blocks — the worker re-checks per candidate, but resetting rows that will only be re-skipped burns their retry budget and reports a replay that will never send. Only enabled destinations are targeted, for the same reason. If the enqueue then fails, the rows are put back to `failed`: a `pending` row with no job is one nothing will ever pick up.

post.summary: Build a campaign blueprint tree
post.description:
Creates a Testing campaign of 1-4 cells plus a CBO Winners campaign, optionally with a retargeting branch, and copies the chosen ads into each cell.

**The refusals are the product.** Seven preflights run BEFORE the first of ~30 Meta writes: an interest-only tree has no control; a budget that cannot feed the chosen event will spend money and learn nothing; more cells than the budget supports starve each below Meta's ~50-event learning threshold; an event that has not fired in 7 days is not wired; an archived ad cannot be copied; a pixel different from the account's live ad sets needs an explicit acknowledgement. Each answers **200** with `outcome: "refused"` and a message — a refusal guarantees nothing was created.

`idempotency_key` is required and replay-safe: a retry whose response was lost reports the tree that exists (`outcome: "replayed"`) rather than re-running the refusals against an account that already has it.

Copies the cell's winning ADS into the CBO Winners ad set (never the ad set itself — Meta freezes `promoted_object` at publish), pauses the source cell, and raises the Winners budget by at most +25%.

**The +25% cap is learning-phase arithmetic, not caution:** a bigger jump re-enters the learning phase and discards exactly the delivery history the graduation was earned with.

**Refuses an API key (403).** This is the one operation on the surface at tier `money` — activating Winners is the moment real spend starts, and Atribu's action executor requires a human on the record before it will move money. Use a signed-in session or an MCP user token.

A key would arm the switch with no one on record, the blueprint would read as auto-graduating, and every promotion would then be silently refused. Disarming needs no human.

get.summary: Budget-scaling guidance for every active ad set
get.description:
A per-ad-set directional call from the traceable-ROAS trend, an early-stage Cox fatigue signal and an instrumentation-health gate. No new attribution math — the guidance is the shared `deriveScaleGuidance`.

**The fatigue leg is directional, not validated.** The deployed Cox models carry no held-out cross-validation, so a `fatiguing` direction is a hint to look, not a proven verdict. Weight it accordingly, and do not present it to an end user as validated.

**Budgets are MINOR units.** Read them with `minor_per_major`; a hardcoded `/100` is wrong by two orders of magnitude for every whole-unit currency. When `currency_unavailable` is true the unit is unknown and no symbol should be printed.

post.summary: Upload a proposed audience to Meta
post.description: THE CONSENT MOMENT. Rebuilds the seed FRESH — the customer base may have moved since the proposal, and what gets uploaded must be what is true now — then creates the value-based Custom Audience and its lookalike stack through the Meta action layer, which brings the audit row, the idempotent replay and the rollback with it. The idempotency key is the proposal's own id, so a retry after a lost response adopts the audience that already exists instead of building a second stack. Identifiers are SHA-256 hashed before they leave.

Creates (or replaces) the pending invitation for this email on this profile and, when the mailer is configured and the 60-second per-email cooldown has elapsed, sends the invitation email. `email_sent` says whether it actually went — the row and its accept link exist either way. `403 app_provisioned_workspace` when the workspace was provisioned by a consumer app: Atribu sends its people no email, so no row is created.

`permissions` is optional: omitted, the role's default bundle is granted. `manage:members` can only be granted by a workspace owner or admin.

**Session bearers only.** Membership administration has no API-key scope: `manage:members` is not in any key's vocabulary, and this route is workspace-scoped, so a key answers `403 insufficient_scope`. Present a Supabase session bearer (the credential Atribu's own console uses).

**Requires `manage:members` on THIS profile.** A workspace owner/admin/analyst holds it by inheritance; anyone else needs it in their `profile_memberships.permissions`. Granting `manage:members` to someone else is narrower still — only a workspace owner or admin may.

get.summary: Get the profile's setup checklist and the one next thing to do
get.description:
An ordered checklist of what this profile still needs before ads, outcomes and attribution work end to end — and, for each unfinished step, the one next action.

**Derived, never stored.** Every step is computed at read time from the state the rest of the product keeps: connections, tracker events, conversion definitions, attribution windows, export destinations and rules, the DPA, the plan, and whether Atribu's attribution pipeline is enabled for this profile at all. There is no checklist table and nothing here is a cached snapshot, so a connection that broke an hour ago shows as `degraded` on the next call.

**`wizard_finished` is not the answer to this question.** It is the legacy `onboarding_completed` boolean — a person pressed Finish — and every wizard step is skippable, so it is reported alongside the steps rather than folded into them.

**A partner-provisioned profile answers `attribution_enabled: blocked`, not an empty checklist.** Profiles created through a partner application deliberately do not hold the `atribu_attribution` entitlement, and Atribu's pipeline is a no-op for them — so every other step can be completed and still produce no attributed conversions. That is reported as the first step, with its reason.

Read `summary.next_step` for the single thing to do now; read `steps` to render the whole flow. This response carries no account ids, no pixel ids, no amounts and no PII.

get.summary: Get the profile's attribution windows
get.description:
The four window settings that decide how far back a touch still gets credit for a conversion: `click_window_days`, `view_window_hours`, `first_touch_window_days` and `cash_window_days`. Returns the table's own defaults (30 / 24 / 90 / null) when the profile has no `profile_attribution_settings` row yet — the same behavior the console's settings page has always had.

This is a NARROW slice of that table: session timeout/mode, geo/user-agent/channel enrichment toggles and the Meta/Google export switches live on the same row but have no v1 surface yet and are not returned here.

patch.description:
A PARTIAL update over the four window columns — an omitted key is left untouched, matching `PATCH /api/v1/profile`'s convention. `cash_window_days: null` clears the override (cash conversions fall back to the normal windows); omitting it leaves the current value alone.

A window change redefines which touches attach to which conversion RETROACTIVELY, so every successful save enqueues ONE full-profile attribution replay — reported as `replay_queued` (+ `replay_error` when it could not be queued), the same non-fatal, REPORTED tail `POST /api/v1/channel-rules` uses for the identical reason. An empty body (no recognized field) is a no-op: it returns the current settings unchanged with `replay_queued: false`.

Out-of-range values answer `400 invalid_parameter` naming the field: `click_window_days` 1–365, `view_window_hours` 1–168, `first_touch_window_days` 1–365, `cash_window_days` null or 1–730.

200.description: The updated (or unchanged) settings, plus the replay outcome

400.description: A window field is out of range, or the body is malformed

post.summary: Create and seed this workspace's demo profile
post.description:
One call gives a workspace something to read before any live account is connected: a profile flagged `is_demo`, sixty days of a fictional clinic's Meta traffic, and a Meta CAPI destination that RECORDS what it would have sent.

**The engine runs for real.** The seed writes INPUTS — ad structure, daily spend, identities, marketing touches, and `outcome_events` through the same CRM-ingest primitive every real provider uses — then enqueues an ordinary recompute. `conversions` and `attribution_touchpoints` across all five attribution models come out of the pipeline, not out of the seed. That is why the counts below report what the recompute WILL produce: it runs asynchronously, so poll `GET /api/v1/overview`.

**What the demo is excluded from.** Its own reads show its own money — that is the point. Every read that spans the profiles of a workspace leaves it out: the pacing aggregate, Top Performers cohorts and the `creative_feature_store` rebuild, the agency Reports hub, alert digest emails, the ML ad-fact and creative-lifecycle passes, and the `active_profiles` plan limit (a demo consumes no seat, and creating one is not gated by the limit).

**Exports never leave.** See `destination.mode`.

**Idempotent.** A workspace holds at most one demo profile. Calling this again re-seeds the existing one and answers 200; only the first call answers 201.

Session bearers and user tokens only — an API key is minted for exactly one profile and belongs to no workspace, so it answers `403 insufficient_scope`.

delete.description:
Removes the demo profile and everything under it — touches, outcome events, conversions, attribution, spend, the seeded ad structure, the recording destination and its ledger — in one call.

**Delete means archive + purge, and audit rows are retained (#1170).** `conversion_exports` records what Atribu transmitted (or, for a demo, would have transmitted) on your behalf, and a database trigger refuses to let any user-facing path erase it. Those rows — and the handful their foreign keys pin in place (the exported outcome event, its customer, the destination and the rule) — stay attached to the archived profile; `retained_audit_rows` counts them. Everything else is gone.

The archived profile disappears from every read (`archived_at IS NULL` is the filter the whole product already applies) and **releases the workspace's demo slot** (`idx_profiles_one_demo_per_workspace` is partial on `archived_at IS NULL`), so `POST /api/v1/profiles/demo` succeeds immediately afterwards.

The `is_demo` predicate is inside the statement, so this can never touch a real profile.

Deleting nothing answers 200 with `deleted: false`, not 404 — a workspace with no demo profile is the state you asked for, and a retry must not look like a failure.

post.summary: Start a sync
post.description:
Queue a manual sync for this profile — one provider, or every connected provider when `provider` is omitted.

**Asynchronous.** `202` means the jobs are queued, not that data has landed; poll `GET /api/v1/connections/sync/status?provider=…` for progress, or read `GET /api/v1/connections` for `sync.last_synced_at`.

**Not keyed by connection id, on purpose.** A profile can hold several connections for one provider (several Meta ad accounts, several GoHighLevel locations), and a sync covers all of them. A route that named one id would enqueue for its siblings anyway; this one says so.

**A sync already in flight is a `409`,** not a second run: the queue holds one job per connection and a duplicate would be dropped silently.

Scope: `attribution:write` — a sync changes what the warehouse will say.

Where one provider's sync has got to on this profile. Safe to poll — the response is `Cache-Control: no-store`, and a progress bar that caches is a progress bar that stops.

**No connection is a 200,** describing a `disconnected` provider with an empty `resources` list. A 404 would make "not connected" indistinguishable from "wrong profile".

Scope: `analytics:read`.

post.summary: Disconnect an integration
post.description:
Delete the connection: stop the provider's push channel, trigger the GoHighLevel Marketplace uninstall where one applies, remove the row, emit `connection.revoked` and write an audit event.

**This is not `DELETE /api/v1/connections/{id}`.** That one is a consumer app's OAuth grant SELF-revoke: it needs an API key, it cuts the keys that grant minted, and it leaves the tenant's connection in place. This one is the tenant giving up their own integration, and it removes it.

**Requires a person, or a delegated key on a profile its own app provisioned.** A signed-in session, an MCP user token, or an `attribution:write` key whose app provisioned this profile (`profiles.provisioned_by` matches the key's app) may call this. Every other API key is a 403 — including that same delegated key on a human-owned profile, or on a profile another app provisioned: deleting a customer's Meta connection is not something a delegated read should be able to do, and an app-provisioned profile is the one case with no person on Atribu's side to do it instead.

**A sync in flight is a 409.** Wait for it: the connector's rows are mid-write.

Scope: `attribution:write`.

post.summary: Recompute attribution
post.description:
Re-run sessions → paths → attribution for this profile. Queue this after anything that changes who gets credit: a customer merge, a channel rule, an attribution-window change.

**Asynchronous.** `202` means queued; poll `GET /api/v1/profile/recompute-status`.

**It skips the freshness cadence.** Background recomputes are throttled to roughly one per profile per window; a request made here is someone waiting on an answer, so it runs at the front. It still coalesces onto a queued job, so a loop cannot outrun the cap.

Scope: `attribution:write`.

get.summary: Is a recompute still running?
get.description:
One boolean, cheap enough to poll. Pair it with `POST /api/v1/profile/recompute` and with any write that queues a recompute of its own — a merge, a channel rule — to know when the numbers you read are the new ones.

Scope: `analytics:read`.

get.summary: Read the profile's tracker and enrichment settings
get.description:
How the tracker sessionises visits and what the enrichment pipeline resolves. The four attribution WINDOW columns live on the same database row but are a different resource — `GET /api/v1/profile/attribution-settings` — because they decide who gets CREDIT, not how an event is captured.

A profile with no settings row yet gets the defaults rather than a 404.

patch.summary: Update the profile's tracker and enrichment settings
patch.description:
A PARTIAL update — an omitted key is left untouched. `export_meta_enabled` / `export_google_enabled` are not accepted: they are owned by Conversion Sync.

Every successful save enqueues ONE full-profile replay, because these settings change how past events would have been sessionised and enriched. The outcome is REPORTED (`replay_queued`, `replay_error`) rather than thrown: the settings were saved either way, and a 500 would tell you the opposite of what happened. An empty body is a no-op — current settings, `replay_queued: false`.

get.description: The profile's verified first-party tracking domain if it has one, else Atribu's own origin. This is the host a marketer pastes into an ad platform's allow-list, and the host the snippet from `GET /api/v1/tracking/snippet` points at for the same profile.

get.description:
Individual tracker events, newest first, for debugging an installation: what arrived, with which UTMs and click ids, and whether it carried an identity.

REQUIRES `visitors:read`, not `analytics:read`. `payload` is the event's own body verbatim, and a `lead_submitted` payload carries the email/phone the tracker captured — so this is the PII tier, the same one `GET /api/v1/visitors` sits on.

Reads the Ephemeral Buffer, whose retention is 30 days. A longer `days` is CLAMPED, and the applied window comes back in `window.days` so a caller never attributes 30 days of numbers to the 90 it asked for. Page with `before` = the previous response's `pagination.next_cursor`.

get.description: Poll this after `POST /api/v1/tracking/verification` to see whether the tracker on the customer's site has echoed the nonce back. `data` is `null` when no attempt was ever started.

post.description: Mints a nonce valid for 15 minutes. Load any tracked page with `?atb_verify=<nonce>` appended; the installed tracker posts it back and the attempt flips to `verified`, recording the URL and User-Agent it was seen on. This is the only proof that the snippet is actually live on the page the marketer thinks it is.

Marks the key revoked. Events sent with it after this stop being accepted, so a site still carrying it goes dark.

REFUSES (400) on the profile's LAST active key: the tracker authenticates with it, so revoking the only one would silently stop every event the site sends. Issue a replacement first with `POST /api/v1/tracking/keys` and `force_new: true`, deploy it, then revoke the old one. A key belonging to another profile answers 404, never 403 — a caller must not be able to probe which key ids exist. Revoking an already-revoked key is idempotent.

get.description: What the ingestion and enrichment pipeline REJECTED or repaired over the window: malformed events, enrichment-stage failures, identity reassignments, and the analytics runs (plus their steps) that processed them. This is the read that answers 'my numbers look wrong — did something fail?'.

get.summary: Is this profile's tracking healthy?
get.description:
Rates and counts describing the SETUP, not the people: how many events arrived, how many carried a click id, how often `identify()` fired, and whether the Meta bridge and the CAPI export are actually working.

TWO NUMBERS THAT LOOK LIKE ONE, deliberately kept apart. `summary.conversion_events` counts the TRACKER's conversion events; `business_conversions` counts the profile's conversions over the same window. A profile whose sales close in a CRM will show a large gap, and that gap is the honest answer rather than a fault.

`diagnostics.meta_exports.sent` is a count over a bounded SAMPLE — read it with `sampled_conversions` and `complete`. Reads the Ephemeral Buffer, so `days` is clamped to its 30-day retention and the applied window is echoed in `window.days`.

get.summary: List the profile's first-party tracking domains

A custom domain makes tracking FIRST-PARTY. Collection through `atribu.app` is a third-party request, which ad blockers and browser privacy lists drop outright — those visitors are not degraded, they are absent. `trk.yourstore.com` gets through.

`cname_target` is what every domain here must point at.
